policy_name: Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF)
incentive_name: Bank Term Loan Financing & Margin Money Support

policy_goals: To help increasing of milk and meat processing capacity and product diversification thereby providing greater access for unorganized rural milk and meat producers to organized milk and meat market
To make available increased price realization for the producer
To make available quality milk and meat products for the domestic consumer

To fulfill the objective of protein enriched quality food requirement of the growing population of the country and prevent malnutrition in one of the highest malnourished children population in the world
Develop entrepreneurship and generate employment
To promote exports and increase the export contribution in the milk and meat sector
To make available quality concentrated animals feed to the cattle, buffalo, sheep, goat, pig and poultry to provide balanced ration at affordable prices
Incentivize investments to establish dairy processing, meat processing, value addition infrastructure, and animal feed plants
policy_details.policy_summary: Announced under the Prime Minister's AtmaNirbhar Bharat Abhiyan stimulus package with an outlay of Rs. 15,000 crore, the Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF) provides bank loans up to 90% of the project cost, an interest subvention of 3% per annum for up to 8 years (including a 2-year principal moratorium), and a credit guarantee coverage of up to 25% under a dedicated Rs. 750 crore Credit Guarantee Fund managed by NABARD for MSMEs. The fund covers infrastructure projects in dairy processing and value addition, meat processing and value addition, and animal feed manufacturing plants.
policy_details.benefit_headline: 3% interest subvention and up to 90% bank loan financing with credit guarantee coverage up to 25% for dairy, meat, and animal feed infrastructure projects.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: 4. ELIGIBLE ENTITIES (EEs) FOR SUPPORT UNDER AHIDF: a) Farmer Producer Organization(FPO), b) Private companies, c) Individual entrepreneurs, d) Section 8 companies, e) Micro Small and Medium Enterprises. Activities eligible for availing benefits: Dairy Processing (Establishment of new units and Strengthening of existing dairy Processing Units with quality and hygienic milk processing facilities, packaging facilities or any other activities related to dairy processing); Value added dairy product manufacturing (Ice Cream unit, Cheese manufacturing unit, UHT Milk processing unit with tetra packaging facilities, Flavoured Milk manufacturing unit, Milk Powder manufacturing unit, Whey powder manufacturing unit, Any other milk products and value addition manufacturing unit); Meat processing and Value addition of facilities (sheep/goat/poultry/pig/buffalo units, Large scale integrated meat processing facilities/plant/unit, Value Added Products like Sausage, nuggets, ham, salami, bacon, etc. compulsory inclusion of ETP, Meat Microbiological Testing Laboratory, Residue Testing laboratory, Cold storage, skin/hide processing and preservation/refrigeration for minimum 24 hours); Animal Feed manufacturing (Mini, Medium and Large Animal Feed Plant, Total Mixed Ration Block Making Unit, By pass protein unit, Mineral Mixture Plant, Enrich Silage making unit, Animal Feed Testing Laboratory).
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Interest subvention will not be allowed for the loan sanctioned for procurement of land, working capital, old machineries and vehicle for personal use. A project will be non-starter if no drawls are made within six months from sanction date; sanction lapses if EE fails to ground project within 12 months. Defaulters of loan repayment in any given year cannot receive interest subvention. Beneficiaries not covered under MSME norms are not eligible for credit guarantee.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Land required for the project must be acquired at own cost (or held on long-term lease of minimum 30 years with NOC for mortgage). Meat processing plants must compulsorily include Effluent Treatment Plant (ETP), Meat Microbiological Testing Laboratory, Residue Testing laboratory, and cold storage/refrigeration facilities for minimum 24 hours. Applications must be submitted via the SIDBI Udyami Mitra Portal with a Detailed Project Report (DPR).
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: All States and Union Territories across India. Projects can be in rural, semi-urban, or urban areas.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Udyami Mitra registration, MSME registration (for MSMEs), Company registration under Companies Act (for companies), applicable State and central statutory clearances including FSSAI, Pollution Control Board (COE/CO), and local trade licenses.

incentive_details.description: Scheduled banks disburse loans up to 90% of the project cost with differentiated promoter/beneficiary contribution based on enterprise category.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: Bank loan financing up to 90% of estimated or actual project cost with minimum promoter margin of 10% to 25%.
incentive_details.application_process: Submission of viable project report along with required statutory clearances and land documentation via SIDBI Udyami Mitra Portal.

quantified_benefits.description: Loan percentage eligible from Scheduled Banks.
quantified_benefits.source_text: The project under the AHIDF shall be eligible for loan up to 90% of the estimated/ actual project cost from the Scheduled Bank based on submission of viable projects by eligible beneficiaries.

quantified_benefits.description: Beneficiary margin money contribution required for Micro and Small units.
quantified_benefits.source_text: The beneficiary contribution in case of Micro and Small units as per MSME defined ceiling could be 10%

quantified_benefits.description: Beneficiary margin money contribution required for Medium enterprises.
quantified_benefits.source_text: while in case of Medium Enterprises as per defined MSME ceiling, beneficiary contribution could go up to 15%.

quantified_benefits.description: Beneficiary contribution required for other enterprise categories.
quantified_benefits.source_text: The beneficiary contribution in other categories of enterprises could go up to 25%.

Eligible for establishment of new units and strengthening/expansion of existing processing/manufacturing facilities.

Scheduled Lender picks up LAF, conducts due diligence, approves loan, and uploads sanction letter. Ministry approves interest subvention on the portal, following which lender disburses funds.

parent_policy_name: Assistance to Medical Device Clusters for Common Facilities (AMD-CF)
policy_name: Assistance for Common Facilities (CF)
incentive_name: Administrative and Management Support Assistance

policy_goals: Strengthen existing and new Medical Device clusters by providing financial assistance for creation of Common Infrastructure Facilities to boost domestic manufacturing capacity, improve cluster quality, and drive sustainable growth.

Support Central or State Governments, institutions, and private organizations to establish or strengthen Testing Laboratories for Medical Devices to meet regulatory testing needs under the Medical Devices Rules (MDR), 2017.
Reduce manufacturing costs and enhance global competitiveness of domestic medical device manufacturers.
policy_details.policy_summary: The Assistance for Common Facilities (CF) sub-scheme under AMD-CF provides financial assistance to Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs) formed by medical device manufacturing clusters (or State Government promoted clusters) for creating Common Infrastructure Facilities (CIF). Eligible facilities include R&D labs, testing and calibration centres, rapid prototyping, clean rooms, sterilization facilities, component testing, and common effluent/waste management plants. The scheme covers up to 70% of approved project costs (or 90% in Himalayan and North Eastern States), capped at ₹20 crore per cluster.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to 70% grant-in-aid (90% for Himalayan and NE States) capped at ₹20 crore for establishing Common Infrastructure Facilities in medical device clusters.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Ministry of Chemicals & Fertilizers, Department of Pharmaceuticals

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: 10.2. Intended Beneficiaries: i. Medical Devices manufacturing units in a cluster who have come together to form a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) to execute the project of developing common facility. There shall be a minimum of 5 Medical Device manufacturing units as members of SPV. ii. Medical Devices clusters promoted by the State Governments: Such a Project Implementing Agency shall be legal entity under the Indian law with foresight of the State Governments. Such a cluster may be exempted from the requirement of formation of SPV & will be deemed to be an SPV for the purpose of this Scheme, provided separate accounts are maintained for the funds to be used for the projects assisted under AMD-CF and an Executive Committee (EC) is set up for implementation of the project. 10.3. Eligibility Criterion for SPV: i. The SPV or the Executive Committee, as the case may be, will have representatives from cluster members, financial institutions, State and Central Government and R&D organization. ii. Individual manufacturing unit cannot hold more than 40% in the SPV. iii. Medical Devices enterprises shall hold at least 51% equity of the SPV. iv. The combined net worth of members of SPV shall be equivalent to total grant amount applied for and each SPV member must have a net worth of at least 1.5 times of their proposed equity contribution. v. The SPV members shall be legally independent entities without any related-party relationship with each other as described under Accounting Standard (AS) 18 of the Companies (Accounting Standard) Rules, 2006.

policy_name: Horticulture Cluster Development Programme (CDP)
incentive_name: Financial Assistance for Horticulture Cluster Development (Mega, Midi, Mini Clusters)

policy_goals: Address the concerns of horticulture and MSME value chains from pre-production, production, post-harvest, infrastructure creation, common facilities, to logistics, marketing and branding in an integrated manner
Reduce harvest and post-harvest losses and build competitiveness of focus clusters for domestic and global markets
Promote green and sustainable manufacturing technology and create Common Facility Centres (CFCs) and upgraded Infrastructure Development (ID) projects for micro and small enterprises
Leverage cluster-based geographical specialisations and provide financial grant assistance to enhance farmers' and entrepreneurs' income
policy_details.policy_summary: The Horticulture Cluster Development Programme (CDP) is a Central Sector programme announced by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare (MoA&FW) and implemented by the National Horticulture Board (NHB). It aims to achieve holistic growth and global competitiveness for 53 identified horticulture clusters (12 in the pilot phase). Interventions are divided into three verticals: (1) Pre-production and Production, (2) Post-Harvest Management and Value Addition, and (3) Logistics, Marketing and Branding. Financial grant assistance is admissible up to ₹100 crore for Mega clusters (>15,000 Ha), ₹50 crore for Midi clusters (5,000 to 15,000 Ha), and ₹25 crore for Mini clusters (up to 5,000 Ha), released in four instalments (30:30:30:10) over a 48-month implementation timeline.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Financial assistance of up to ₹100 crore per Mega cluster, ₹50 crore per Midi cluster, and ₹25 crore per Mini cluster for integrated horticulture interventions.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare and Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises, Government of India

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: Entities eligible for becoming Implementing Agencies (IAs) include Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs/FPCs) and their federations, Cooperatives/Societies, Partnership Firms, Proprietorship Firms, Companies, State Agriculture and Marketing Boards and Federations and other Public Sector entities of Central/State Governments. The applicant entity should have a net-worth of minimum two times of the proposed equity contribution as per the latest audited balance sheet. IA should contribute at least 20% of the eligible project cost as promoters' contribution. IA must bring at least 20% of eligible project cost as term loan from scheduled commercial banks/RBI approved Financial Institutions (FIs). In-principle or final term loan sanction by bank along with the bank appraisal note is required. IA must have relevant experience as an agri/horti input supplier/producer/aggregator/trader/food processor/exporter/retailer/logistics provider, etc., depending on the vertical applied for. The applicant entity and/or its shareholders/partners/directors/key management persons must not have defaulted on debt obligations in the last three years and should not appear on RBI list of wilful defaulters.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Second-hand/old machines; Reconditioned and refurbished plant & machinery; Cost of land; Site development; Approach/internal roads; Administrative office building/guest house; Compound wall; Canteen/restaurants; Preliminary/pre-operative expenses including IDC; Working capital/margin money; All applicable taxes, insurance, freight, stationery, operational costs (salaries, rentals, maintenance).
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Identified horticulture clusters across India as designated by MoA&FW (covering Mega, Midi, and Mini clusters).
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Registration/incorporation certificate, PAN, TAN, GST, PFMS (CGA) registration, Trust and Retention Account (TRA) agreement with a Scheduled Bank.
special_category_benefits: FPOs/FPCs receive 50% relaxation with respect to turnover criteria and years of experience

incentive_details.description: Grant-in-aid assistance provided by NHB through Cluster Development Agencies (CDAs) to Implementing Agencies (IAs) across three verticals: Pre-production and Production; Post-harvest Management and Value Addition; and Logistics, Marketing and Branding. Maximum 40% of cluster assistance can be utilized within a single vertical (relaxed for an integrated project by a single IA). Assistance is disbursed in 4 instalments: 30% (first instalment within 12 months), 30% (second instalment within 24 months), 30% (third instalment within 36 months), and 10% (fourth instalment within 48 months on project completion).
incentive_details.benefit_headline: Up to ₹100 crore financial assistance for Mega clusters, ₹50 crore for Midi clusters, and ₹25 crore for Mini clusters disbursed in four milestone-based instalments.
incentive_details.application_process: CDA invites composite Call for Proposals based on Cluster Gap Assessment Report. Applicants submit proposals and DPR in prescribed format. Technical evaluation is conducted by Evaluation Committee (EC) on 100 marks and Approval Committee (AC) on 50 marks. Final selection is based on combined merit.

quantified_benefits.source_text: Mega: More than 15,000 Ha - Amount of financial assistance admissible per cluster: Up to 100 (INR in crore)

quantified_benefits.description: Financial assistance for Midi cluster (area under focus crop between 5,000 Ha to 15,000 Ha)

quantified_benefits.description: Financial assistance for Mini cluster (area under focus crop up to 5,000 Ha)
quantified_benefits.source_text: Mini: Up to 5,000 Ha - Amount of financial assistance admissible per cluster: Up to 25 (INR in crore)

policy_name: Micro & Small Enterprises Cluster Development Programme (MSE-CDP)
incentive_name: Common Facility Centres (CFC) Grant Assistance

policy_goals: Address the concerns of horticulture and MSME value chains from pre-production, production, post-harvest, infrastructure creation, common facilities, to logistics, marketing and branding in an integrated manner
Reduce harvest and post-harvest losses and build competitiveness of focus clusters for domestic and global markets
Promote green and sustainable manufacturing technology and create Common Facility Centres (CFCs) and upgraded Infrastructure Development (ID) projects for micro and small enterprises
Leverage cluster-based geographical specialisations and provide financial grant assistance to enhance farmers' and entrepreneurs' income
policy_details.policy_summary: The Micro & Small Enterprises Cluster Development Programme (MSE-CDP) is a flagship scheme of the Ministry of MSME, revised in May 2022 (and amended July 2022), providing grant-in-aid to enhance competitiveness, sustainability, and infrastructure for MSEs. The scheme has two components: (1) Common Facility Centers (CFCs) for creating tangible shared assets (processing, testing, R&D, training, effluent treatment, bio-waste, raw material bank, etc.) with project costs between ₹5 crore and ₹30 crore; and (2) Infrastructure Development (ID) Projects for setting up new industrial estates/flatted factory complexes (₹5 crore to ₹15 crore) or upgrading existing ones (₹5 crore to ₹10 crore). Grants range from 50% to 80% depending on component, project cost, and cluster location/ownership.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to 80% GoI grant (max project cost ₹30 crore) for Common Facility Centres and up to 70% GoI grant (max project cost ₹15 crore) for Infrastructure Development.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare and Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises, Government of India
special_focus_areas: Aspirational Districts and LWE affected districts
North Eastern Region (NER), Hill States and Island territories

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: For Common Facility Centers (CFC), projects must be implemented through a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) registered as a Section 8 Company under the Companies Act 2013 (or Registered Society/Cooperative for Sikkim). SPV must consist of a minimum of 20 MSEs/Startups/Greenfield MSEs/FPOs for projects above ₹10 crore, and minimum 10 MSEs for projects below ₹10 crore. No single unit will hold more than 10% of equity capital. Minimum member contribution is 10% (5% for NER) for projects < ₹10 crore, and 20% (15% for NER) for projects > ₹10 crore. SPV members must evidence ability to utilize at least 60% of installed capacity. Land/building must be owned by SPV or leased for not less than 15 years (25 years if on leased land). For Infrastructure Development, projects are implemented by State/UT Government agencies on land owned by the State Government/IA with clear title.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Projects costing less than ₹5 crore (except designated rural/livelihood projects under SFURTI or FPO agro-processing). Recurring expenses, replacement, renovation, or expansion of capital assets. Operational expenses. Cost escalation above sanctioned amount.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Notified industrial estates, industrial areas, or contiguous MSE clusters pan-India. Priority given to Gram Panchayats, municipal areas, Aspirational Districts, North Eastern Region (NER), Hill States, Island territories, and LWE affected districts.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Udyam registration for member MSEs; Section 8 Company registration for SPV; Geo-tagging of project site.
special_category_benefits: Clusters located in Aspirational Districts, NER, Hill States, Island territories, LWE affected districts, and clusters with more than 50% (a) micro/village, (b) women-owned, or (c) SC/ST owned units receive enhanced GoI grant of 70% to 80% for CFCs and 60% to 70% for ID projects with reduced SPV/State share.

incentive_details.description: Grant-in-aid from Government of India for setting up tangible common facility assets including testing, design, R&D, training, common production/processing, effluent treatment plants, raw material bank, packaging, bio-waste/biogas, plug-and-play facilities, and service sector common facilities. Eligible project cost is between ₹5 crore and ₹30 crore (projects above ₹30 crore are capped at ₹30 crore for calculating GoI grant). Disbursed in 3 instalments in the ratio of 50:40:10.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: 60% to 80% GoI grant for Common Facility Centres with project costs between ₹5 crore and ₹30 crore.
incentive_details.application_process: Online submission of DPR and appraisal report via scheme portal (www.cluster.dcmsme.gov.in). Examination by MSME-DI, approval/recommendation by State Level Steering Committee (SLSC), and final approval by National Project Approval Committee (NPAC).

quantified_benefits.source_text: Common Facility Centre: Rs 5 crore to Rs 10 crore - Funding Pattern: Govt of India 70%, State Govt 20%, SPV 10%

policy_name: Micro & Small Enterprises Cluster Development Programme (MSE-CDP)
incentive_name: Infrastructure Development (ID) Projects Grant Assistance

policy_goals: Address the concerns of horticulture and MSME value chains from pre-production, production, post-harvest, infrastructure creation, common facilities, to logistics, marketing and branding in an integrated manner
Reduce harvest and post-harvest losses and build competitiveness of focus clusters for domestic and global markets
Promote green and sustainable manufacturing technology and create Common Facility Centres (CFCs) and upgraded Infrastructure Development (ID) projects for micro and small enterprises
Leverage cluster-based geographical specialisations and provide financial grant assistance to enhance farmers' and entrepreneurs' income
policy_details.policy_summary: The Micro & Small Enterprises Cluster Development Programme (MSE-CDP) is a flagship scheme of the Ministry of MSME, revised in May 2022 (and amended July 2022), providing grant-in-aid to enhance competitiveness, sustainability, and infrastructure for MSEs. The scheme has two components: (1) Common Facility Centers (CFCs) for creating tangible shared assets (processing, testing, R&D, training, effluent treatment, bio-waste, raw material bank, etc.) with project costs between ₹5 crore and ₹30 crore; and (2) Infrastructure Development (ID) Projects for setting up new industrial estates/flatted factory complexes (₹5 crore to ₹15 crore) or upgrading existing ones (₹5 crore to ₹10 crore). Grants range from 50% to 80% depending on component, project cost, and cluster location/ownership.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to 80% GoI grant (max project cost ₹30 crore) for Common Facility Centres and up to 70% GoI grant (max project cost ₹15 crore) for Infrastructure Development.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare and Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises, Government of India
special_focus_areas: Aspirational Districts and LWE affected districts
North Eastern Region (NER), Hill States and Island territories

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: For Common Facility Centers (CFC), projects must be implemented through a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) registered as a Section 8 Company under the Companies Act 2013 (or Registered Society/Cooperative for Sikkim). SPV must consist of a minimum of 20 MSEs/Startups/Greenfield MSEs/FPOs for projects above ₹10 crore, and minimum 10 MSEs for projects below ₹10 crore. No single unit will hold more than 10% of equity capital. Minimum member contribution is 10% (5% for NER) for projects < ₹10 crore, and 20% (15% for NER) for projects > ₹10 crore. SPV members must evidence ability to utilize at least 60% of installed capacity. Land/building must be owned by SPV or leased for not less than 15 years (25 years if on leased land). For Infrastructure Development, projects are implemented by State/UT Government agencies on land owned by the State Government/IA with clear title.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Projects costing less than ₹5 crore (except designated rural/livelihood projects under SFURTI or FPO agro-processing). Recurring expenses, replacement, renovation, or expansion of capital assets. Operational expenses. Cost escalation above sanctioned amount.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Notified industrial estates, industrial areas, or contiguous MSE clusters pan-India. Priority given to Gram Panchayats, municipal areas, Aspirational Districts, North Eastern Region (NER), Hill States, Island territories, and LWE affected districts.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Udyam registration for member MSEs; Section 8 Company registration for SPV; Geo-tagging of project site.
special_category_benefits: Clusters located in Aspirational Districts, NER, Hill States, Island territories, LWE affected districts, and clusters with more than 50% (a) micro/village, (b) women-owned, or (c) SC/ST owned units receive enhanced GoI grant of 70% to 80% for CFCs and 60% to 70% for ID projects with reduced SPV/State share.

incentive_details.benefit_headline: 50% to 70% GoI grant for setting up new Industrial Estates (up to ₹15 crore) or upgrading existing ones (up to ₹10 crore).
incentive_details.application_process: DPR along with land details submitted by State Government/Industrial Park Development Agency to MSME-DI. Evaluated and recommended by SLSC and submitted to NPAC for final approval.

policy_name: Development of Production Infrastructure (DPI) Scheme
incentive_name: Capital Subsidy for New Coir Processing Units

policy_goals: Facilitate development of domestic and export markets for coir and coir products
Provide skill development, training, and entrepreneurship creation for sustainable growth of the coir sector
Empower rural women artisans through self-employment opportunities and modern machinery
Promote modernization, technology upgradation, and quality improvement across production units
Enhance raw material utilization and promote coir industry in non-traditional coconut producing regions
Provide social security and personal accident welfare insurance coverage for coir workers
policy_details.policy_summary: The Development of Production Infrastructure (DPI) scheme provides capital financial assistance at the rate of 25% of the cost of equipment and infrastructural facilities (excluding land) for establishing new coir processing units with project cost above ₹10 lakhs (or above the Coir Udyami Yojana ceiling), and up to ₹2.00 lakhs for modernizing existing units that have completed at least 3 years of successful operation.
policy_details.benefit_headline: 25% capital subsidy up to ₹6 lakhs for de-fibering units, ₹4 lakhs for automatic spinning, ₹5 lakhs for other coir units, and ₹9 lakhs for multiple units.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Coir Board, Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Government of India

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: All new coir processing units registered with Coir Board under Coir Industry (Registration) Rules, 2008 and registered with the DIC of the respective region of the entire coir sector of the country with project cost exceeding Rs.10/- lakh each or more than the ceiling fixed in Coir Udyami Yojana Scheme are eligible for assistance under the scheme. Power connection or generator should be available at the location of the coir unit. A unit which has availed financial assistance would be eligible for financial assistance under modernization only after successful running of the unit for a minimum period of 3 years.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Land cost is excluded from project cost calculation. Entrepreneurs who have availed any other Central / State government subsidy (like PMEGP, CUY, TUF, MSE-CDP) for the same purpose are disqualified.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Must submit application within 12 months from the date of commencement of commercial production. Must execute an agreement on ₹100 non-judicial stamp paper and maintain fire/general insurance for not less than the subsidy amount for at least 5 years. Grant recoverable if unit goes out of production within 3 years.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Entire coir sector of India, across traditional and non-traditional coconut producing states.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Registration with Coir Board under Coir Industry (Registration) Rules 2008, MSMED acknowledgement / DIC registration.

incentive_details.description: Financial assistance provided @ 25% of the total project cost (excluding land cost, but including machinery, building, generator, and dedicated rural power lines) subject to item-wise and overall monetary ceilings.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: 25% capital subsidy up to ₹6 lakhs for Defibering, ₹4 lakhs for Automatic Spinning, ₹5 lakhs for others, and ₹9 lakhs for composite units.
incentive_details.application_process: Apply in Form No. 1 online/offline to RO/SRO. RO/SRO conducts inspection, verifies valuation from Chartered Engineer, and submits recommendation to Head Office Screening Committee. Subsidy remitted directly to bank account within 21 days of sanction.

quantified_benefits.conditions: Must produce multiple coir items

quantified_benefits.source_text: For a Composite or a Multiple Unit, the maximum monetary ceiling of assistance would be Rs. 9 lakh.

policy_details.policy_summary: The Domestic Market Promotion Scheme provides Market Development Assistance (MDA) linked to sales performance of coir cooperatives and public sector enterprises, promotes participation in domestic exhibitions, and supports aggressive nationwide publicity and showroom renovation.
policy_details.benefit_headline: 10% annual Market Development Assistance on average coir sales turnover, funded 1:1 by Central and State Governments.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Coir Board, Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Government of India

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: Apex Co-operative Societies, Central Co-op. Societies, Primary Co-operative Societies, Public Sector Enterprises in the coir industry and the Showroom and Sales Depots / Hindustan Coir of the Coir Board. Must be committed to payment of minimum wages and other obligatory benefits to coir workers.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Apex/Central Societies are not eligible for MDA on sales of coir fibre/yarn purchased from Primary Societies that have already claimed MDA.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: State/UT government must communicate willingness in advance and provide 50% matching share. Assistance must be utilized exclusively for publicity, opening/renovating showrooms, market studies, CAD/design upgradation, godowns, and discounts.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Participating States and Union Territories with matching budgetary allocations.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Registered coir cooperative societies, federations, or state PSUs.

incentive_details.description: Financial assistance granted at 10% of average annual sales turnover of coir products over preceding 3 financial years, shared 1:1 between Central and State/UT Governments.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: 10% financial assistance based on average 3-year sales turnover of coir products.
incentive_details.application_process: Beneficiaries submit claims through State/UT Government in Annexure A or B with audited certificates and utilization certificates.

quantified_benefits.value_raw: 10% of their average annual sales turnover
quantified_benefits.conditions: Shared on 1:1 basis between Central and State/UT Government; backed by audited accounts of preceding 3 years
quantified_benefits.description: MDA grant based on average annual sales turnover
quantified_benefits.source_text: The MDA is granted at the rate of 10% of their average annual sales turnover of coir products including coir fibre, coir pith... during the preceding three financial years. This Assistance will be shared on 1:1 basis between the Central Government and the concerned State/Union Territory Government.
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: Apex, Central, and Primary Coir Cooperative Societies, and State PSUs

policy_details.policy_summary: The Export Market Promotion (EMP) scheme supports coir exporters and MSMEs to access international markets, participate in overseas fairs, delegations, buyer-seller meets, catalogue shows, and international conferences, with assistance provided under the External Market Development Assistance (EMDA) component, alongside international publicity and annual Coir Industry Awards.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to ₹2.50 lakhs financial assistance for participating in overseas trade fairs, including 100% economy airfare and stall rental.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Coir Board, Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Government of India

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: All exporters with FOB turnover of less than Rs.2 crore worth coir and coir products in the previous year and micro, small & medium entrepreneurs of coir and coir products, registered with the Coir Board, would be eligible for assistance under the scheme, provided they have not availed the facility from any other source for the same purpose or participated three times in the same exhibition or undertaken sales promotion tour to the same destination thrice with government assistance.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Exporters with previous year FOB turnover of ₹2 crore or more; entities that have participated 3 times in the same event/destination with government assistance; entities charged, debarred, prosecuted, or blacklisted under Foreign Trade Policy or by Coir Board.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Assistance permissible for one senior level employee/Director/Partner/Proprietor for air travel in Economy Class via shortest route. Maximum three assisted events per financial year. Application must be submitted at least 14 days before departure.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Registered with Coir Board as an exporter or MSME of coir products.

incentive_details.description: Financial assistance covering 100% economy class airfare and registration/participation charges for one representative attending BSMs, trade delegations, and seminars abroad.

incentive_details.application_process: Apply to Coir Board 14 days in advance and file post-event claims with proof of travel and payment.

Sponsoring agencies and trainees for skill upgradation programmes must provide valid ID proof (Election ID Card/Aadhar Card).

policy_details.policy_summary: The Group Personal Accident Insurance Scheme covers all bonafide coir workers aged 18 years and above across India against accidental death, permanent total disability, and permanent partial disability. 100% of the insurance premium is paid directly by the Coir Board, ensuring free social security coverage.

policy_details.issuing_authority: Coir Board, Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Government of India

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: Coir Workers working anywhere in India are covered under the scheme. Coir worker means any person who is employed for wages to do any work in connection with the various processes in coir industry and who gets his wages directly or indirectly from the employer, dealer or producers of coir products and includes any person employed by or through a contractor or through an agent and depends mainly on coir industry for his livelihood. Coir worker aged 18 years and above engaged in the industry (no upper age limit) are covered under the Insurance Scheme.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Non-coir workers or non-accidental events not covered under the policy terms.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Worker must be identifiable by Coir Board as a bonafide coir worker. Includes specialized women's accident coverage (sterilization complications, childbirth, etc.).
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: All coir producing states and territories in India.

incentive_details.application_process: Claim intimation routed through Coir Board with FIR, death/disability certificate, and ID proof; insurance company settles claim within 15 days.

policy_goals: Train personnel in the cadres of Supervisors, Instructors, and Artisans to meet the skilled manpower requirements of the coir industry
Facilitate transfer of technology to non-traditional coconut growing areas through skill development of coir workers
Provide self-employment opportunities to rural women artisans in coir fibre producing and processing regions
Improve productivity, product quality, working conditions, and income while eliminating drudgery involved in traditional spinning and manufacturing
Inculcate quality consciousness at the grassroots level and educate workers on producing standard quality fibre, yarn, and products
Encourage new entrepreneurs through Entrepreneurship Development Programmes (EDPs) to establish coir industrial units
Create awareness among coconut growers and entrepreneurs to modernize existing units and utilize coconut husk for wealth creation
Generate gainful rural employment across coconut producing States
policy_details.policy_summary: Mahila Coir Yojana (MCY) is a women-oriented self-employment scheme implemented by the Coir Board since 1994. The scheme empowers rural women artisans in coconut husk processing areas by providing specialized training in spinning coir yarn and producing value-added coir goods. Under earlier XII Plan provisions, it offered a 75% capital subsidy (up to ₹7,500) for procuring motorized ratts, electronic ratts, and specified processing machinery/equipment. Under updated Coir Vikas Yojana guidelines, trained women artisans receive sophisticated machinery training, integration with Livelihood Business Incubators (LBI), and handholding support to access credit and capital subsidy under the Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) for project costs up to ₹25 lakhs.
policy_details.benefit_headline: 75% capital subsidy up to ₹7,500 on motorized ratts/machinery, and handholding for coir project loans up to ₹25 lakhs under PMEGP.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Coir Board, Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Government of India

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: Rural women artisans in regions processing coconut husk who have successfully completed the training programme in spinning of coir yarn or value-added product manufacturing through any of the training centres of the Coir Board. Not more than one artisan per household is eligible to receive assistance under the scheme. The beneficiary must deposit 25% beneficiary contribution in a separate account opened in a scheduled/nationalized bank or post office. Beneficiary shall not mortgage the equipment except to financing agencies from whom loan/grant is availed. The unit must not go out of production within 3 years from the date of commencement.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Not more than one artisan per household is eligible. Units that go out of production within 3 years, or where assistance was obtained through misrepresentation or used for other purposes, are subject to subsidy recovery.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Rural households in regions processing coconut husk / producing coir fibre across India.

policy_details.policy_summary: Mahila Coir Yojana (MCY) is a women-oriented self-employment scheme implemented by the Coir Board since 1994. The scheme empowers rural women artisans in coconut husk processing areas by providing specialized training in spinning coir yarn and producing value-added coir goods. Under earlier XII Plan provisions, it offered a 75% capital subsidy (up to ₹7,500) for procuring motorized ratts, electronic ratts, and specified processing machinery/equipment. Under updated Coir Vikas Yojana guidelines, trained women artisans receive sophisticated machinery training, integration with Livelihood Business Incubators (LBI), and handholding support to access credit and capital subsidy under the Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) for project costs up to ₹25 lakhs.

The beneficiary must deposit 25% beneficiary contribution in a separate account opened in a scheduled/nationalized bank or post office. eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Not more than one artisan per household is eligible. Units that go out of production within 3 years, or where assistance was obtained through misrepresentation or used for other purposes, are subject to subsidy recovery.

policy_name: Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups (CGSS)
incentive_name: Transaction-based Guarantee Cover

policy_goals: Provide guarantee upto a specified limit against credit instruments extended by Member Institutions (MI) to finance eligible Startups
Provide the much needed collateral free debt funding to Startups
policy_details.policy_summary: The Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups (CGSS), notified by DPIIT under S.O. 2046(E) on May 8, 2025 (superseding the earlier notification dated October 6, 2022), provides credit guarantees to Member Institutions (Scheduled Commercial Banks, Financial Institutions, eligible NBFCs, and SEBI-registered Alternative Investment Funds/Venture Debt Funds) for loans and venture debt facilities extended to DPIIT-recognized startups. The scheme operates under two structures: (1) Transaction-based guarantee cover for individual loans/credit facilities, offering up to 85% cover for loans up to ₹10 crore and 75% cover for loans exceeding ₹10 crore, capped at ₹20 crore per borrower, with an Annual Guarantee Fee of 2% (reduced to 1.5% for North East and women entrepreneurs, and 1% for 27 Champion Sectors); and (2) Umbrella-based guarantee cover for Venture Debt Funds (VDFs) covering pooled investments up to 5% or actual losses, subject to a ₹20 crore cap per borrower, with an Annual Commitment Charge of 0.15% p.a. The scheme is administered through the Credit Guarantee Fund for Startups (CGFS) managed by National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company Limited (NCGTC).
policy_details.benefit_headline: Collateral-free credit guarantee cover up to ₹20 crore per borrower, covering up to 85% of default amount for DPIIT-recognized startups.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
special_focus_areas: 27 Champion Sectors under Make in India

eligibility_criteria.raw_text:
4. Eligible borrower
The eligibility criteria for an entity to borrow under the Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups shall be as follows, wherein an entity should be:
i. Startup as recognized by DPIIT as per Gazette Notifications issued from time to time, and
ii. Startup not in default to any lending/investing institution and not classified as Non-Performing Asset as per RBI guidelines, and
iii. Startup whose eligibility is certified by the Member Institution for the purpose of guarantee cover.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Startup in default to any lending/investing institution or classified as Non-Performing Asset as per RBI guidelines. Credit facilities already covered under any other guarantee scheme. Non-startup investments in VDF portfolios.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Loan/Debt facilities sanctioned to an eligible borrower on or after the date of notification of the scheme (May 8, 2025). The startup eligibility must be certified by the Member Institution for the purpose of guarantee cover.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Startup as recognized by DPIIT as per Gazette Notifications issued from time to time
special_category_benefits: Enterprises in the North East region (concessional AGF of 1.5% p.a.)
Enterprises in 27 Champion Sectors under Make in India (concessional AGF of 1.0% p.a.)

incentive_details.description: Provides guarantee cover on a single eligible borrower basis against credit instruments including venture debt, working capital, subordinated debt/mezzanine debt, debentures, optionally convertible debt, and other fund-based and non-fund-based facilities. Coverage is capped at ₹20 crore per borrower. Annual Guarantee Fee (AGF) is 2.0% p.a. standard, 1.5% p.a. for North East region and women entrepreneurs, and 1.0% p.a. for 27 Champion Sectors. Claims can be invoked after a 12-month lock-in period upon loan recall and initiation of legal recovery proceedings (IBC, SARFAESI, DRT, etc.), with 75% paid within 60 days and 25% paid upon conclusion of recovery or write-off.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: Up to 85% guarantee cover on default amounts for loans up to ₹10 crore, and 75% for loans above ₹10 crore, capped at ₹20 crore.
incentive_details.application_process: Eligible Member Institution evaluates proposal with banking prudence, certifies startup eligibility, enters into agreement with Trustee/NCGTC, pays Annual Guarantee Fee within 30 days of Demand Advice Note (CGDAN), and lodges claim following recovery initiation via IBC, SARFAESI, DRT, etc.

quantified_benefits.cap_raw: loan amount up to Rs. 10 crore
quantified_benefits.conditions: Maximum guarantee cover per borrower shall not exceed Rs. 20 crore; minimum 12 months lock-in period.
quantified_benefits.description: Guarantee cover percentage on amount in default for loan amount up to ₹10 crore
quantified_benefits.source_text: 85% of the amount in default for loan amount up to Rs. 10 crore

quantified_benefits.cap_raw: subject to a maximum of Rs. 20 crore per borrower
quantified_benefits.conditions: Subject to maximum guarantee cover of Rs. 20 crore per borrower.
quantified_benefits.description: Guarantee cover percentage on amount in default for loan amount exceeding ₹10 crore
quantified_benefits.source_text: 75% of the amount in default for loan amount exceeding Rs. 10 crore.

quantified_benefits.conditions: Paid upfront to the Trust within 30 days from the date of CGDAN.
quantified_benefits.description: Concessional Annual Guarantee Fee (AGF) for startups from North East region and women entrepreneurs
quantified_benefits.source_text: For units from the North East region as well as those of women entrepreneurs, the Member Institution shall pay a standard rate of 1.5% p.a. of the disbursement/outstanding amount (on sanction amount, in case of working capital facility and non-fund based facility) as on the date of application of guarantee cover

policy_name: Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme (CLCSS) / CLCS Component of CLCS-TUS
incentive_name: Upfront Capital Subsidy for Technology Upgradation

policy_goals: Facilitate technology upgradation of Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs) by providing upfront capital subsidy on institutional finance.
Promote induction of well-established, proven, clean, green, and energy-efficient technologies across manufacturing and service sectors.
Enhance capacity, competitiveness, and marketability of SC/ST owned enterprises to fulfill the mandated 4% public procurement target by Central/State Governments and CPSEs.
Support small scale industries graduating from small to medium scale and encourage price competitiveness in global and domestic markets.
policy_details.policy_summary: The Credit Linked Capital Subsidy (CLCS) component facilitates technology upgradation of Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs) by providing an upfront capital subsidy of 15% on institutional credit availed from eligible primary lending institutions for induction of approved and benchmarked technologies. The ceiling limit of term loan eligible for subsidy calculation is Rs. 1.00 crore, resulting in a maximum capital subsidy of Rs. 15 lakhs based on the purchase cost of eligible plant and machinery.
policy_details.benefit_headline: 15% upfront capital subsidy up to a maximum cap of Rs. 15 lakhs on institutional term loans up to Rs. 1 crore for technology upgradation.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Office of the Development Commissioner (MSME), Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Government of India

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: The subsidy will be given to existing and new enterprise having MSE status. Their Constitution may be sole proprietorships, partnerships, Co-operative and societies, private limited / LLP companies in the sector. The MSEs shall have valid UAN at the time application implying registration under MSMED Act, 2006. Industry graduating from small scale to medium scale on account of sanction of additional loan under CLCS shall be eligible. Priority given to SC/ST category, women entrepreneurs and entrepreneurs from NER, Hill states (J&K, HP, Uttarakhand), island territories (A&N, Lakshadweep) and Aspirational / LWE Districts. Units in RED category as per MoEFCC are excluded. Fabricated and second-hand plant and machinery shall not be eligible.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Second-hand or fabricated plant and machinery; replacement of existing equipment with the same technology/equipment; industries categorized under RED category per MoEFCC; investments made through buyers credit, usance credit, leasing / hire purchase, and sellers credit.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Valid Udyog Aadhaar Number (UAN) / Udyam Registration and entry into the MSME Data Bank are mandatory. The term loan sanctioned must not be for less than 3 years including moratorium. Units must remain in commercial production for at least 3 years after installation and commissioning.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Valid Udyam Registration / Udyog Aadhaar Memorandum (UAM) and MSME Data Bank registration.
special_category_benefits: Enterprises owned by SC/ST categories (51% and above)
Units located in NER, Hilly States, Island territories, and Aspirational / LWE districts

incentive_details.description: 15% capital subsidy calculated on the eligible investment/purchase price of approved plant and machinery (or loan amount, whichever is lower) availed through term loans up to Rs. 100 lakh from notified primary lending institutions. The subsidy is kept in the form of a non-interest-earning Term Deposit Receipt (TDR) for three years and liquidated into the loan account upon successful completion of the retention period.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: 15% capital subsidy up to Rs. 15 lakhs on eligible investment in plant and machinery.
incentive_details.application_process: Borrowing unit applies to PLI for term loan. After sanction, disbursement, and installation of machinery, PLI submits online claim via Nodal Agency through the dedicated tracking software on FIFO basis.

quantified_benefits.conditions: Term loan must be sanctioned by eligible PLIs with a minimum repayment period of 3 years.
quantified_benefits.description: Upfront capital subsidy on cost of eligible plant and machinery funded by term loan.
quantified_benefits.source_text: The subsidy would be 15% of the loan / credit amount or cost of P/M whichever is lower, maximum up to Rs.15 lakh.
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: All eligible Micro and Small Enterprises

incentive_details.application_deadline: Before the end of the quarter immediately following the quarter in which the final instalment of term loan is disbursed.
incentive_details.application_authority: Designated Nodal Banks/Agencies (e.g. SIDBI, NABARD, SBI, PNB, Canara Bank, BOB, BOI, Indian Bank, etc.) via Ministry of MSME portal
incentive_details.incentive_specific_eligibility: Machinery must belong to the approved lists of technologies across eligible sub-sectors/products.

policy_name: Special Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme (SCLCSS) for SC/ST MSEs
incentive_name: Special Capital Subsidy for SC/ST MSEs

policy_goals: Facilitate technology upgradation of Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs) by providing upfront capital subsidy on institutional finance.
Promote induction of well-established, proven, clean, green, and energy-efficient technologies across manufacturing and service sectors.
Enhance capacity, competitiveness, and marketability of SC/ST owned enterprises to fulfill the mandated 4% public procurement target by Central/State Governments and CPSEs.
Support small scale industries graduating from small to medium scale and encourage price competitiveness in global and domestic markets.
policy_details.policy_summary: Under the National SC/ST Hub (NSSH), a special provision of 25% upfront capital subsidy is extended to SC/ST-owned MSEs on institutional finance up to Rs. 1 crore for procurement of plant and machinery or service equipment, capped at Rs. 25 lakhs. It applies without any sector-specific technology restrictions for both manufacturing and service sectors.
policy_details.benefit_headline: 25% capital subsidy up to Rs. 25 lakhs on institutional term loans up to Rs. 1 crore for SC/ST-owned MSEs.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Office of the Development Commissioner (MSME), Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Government of India

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: Sole Proprietorships, Partnerships, Co-operative societies, Private and Public limited companies owned by SC/ST Entrepreneurs of MSE sector engaged in manufacturing and service activities. Clear ownership of 51% & above must be held by SC/ST entrepreneurs. Units graduated from small to medium scale are eligible for 3 years from graduation. Valid Udyam Registration is mandatory. Excludes RED category industries under MoEFCC rules.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Second-hand or fabricated plant and machinery/equipment; RED category industries per MoEFCC; PBGs submitted as EMD; multiple claims against single loans.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Valid Udyam Registration mandatory. Unit must maintain commercial production or service for at least 3 years following installation and commissioning.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Udyam Registration.
special_category_benefits: SC/ST entrepreneurs holding 51% or more shareholding

incentive_details.description: 25% capital subsidy on institutional term loans up to Rs. 100 lakhs availed from PLIs for purchasing new plant, machinery, and equipment in manufacturing and service sectors without sector-specific technological restrictions.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: 25% capital subsidy up to a maximum of Rs. 25 lakhs for SC/ST MSEs.
incentive_details.application_process: Eligible claims submitted through dedicated online portal via PLIs / Nodal agencies to NSSH Cell / Ministry on FIFO basis.

quantified_benefits.conditions: Term loan sanctioned by PLIs; machines purchased on or after term loan sanction date.
quantified_benefits.description: Capital subsidy on eligible investment in plant and machinery or equipment.
quantified_benefits.source_text: A special provision of 25% subsidy to SC/ST MSEs under National SC/ST Hub (NSSH) on institutional finance up to Rs.1 Cr. for procurement of Plant & Machinery (i.e. a subsidy cap of Rs.25 Lakhs) without any sector specific restrictions.

incentive_details.application_deadline: Claim with reference date of each quarter should reach up to the end of next quarter.
incentive_details.application_authority: NSSH Cell / NSIC / Office of DC (MSME)
incentive_details.incentive_specific_eligibility: Entities must be SC/ST owned (at least 51% equity holding).

incentive_name: Participation in Domestic Exhibitions / Trade Fairs

policy_goals: Facilitate technology upgradation of Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs) by providing upfront capital subsidy on institutional finance.
Promote induction of well-established, proven, clean, green, and energy-efficient technologies across manufacturing and service sectors.
Enhance capacity, competitiveness, and marketability of SC/ST owned enterprises to fulfill the mandated 4% public procurement target by Central/State Governments and CPSEs.
Support small scale industries graduating from small to medium scale and encourage price competitiveness in global and domestic markets.
policy_details.policy_summary: Provides comprehensive marketing and market access support to SC/ST MSMEs for participating in domestic and international exhibitions, trade fairs, buyer-seller meets, and vendor development programmes. Subsidies cover 100% stall charges on minimum stall size, 100% economy airfare or 3-tier AC train/bus fare, enhanced daily allowance, and freight charges.
policy_details.benefit_headline: 100% airfare/travel, 100% stall subsidy, and allowances up to Rs. 3 lakhs per event for trade fairs and exhibitions.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Office of the Development Commissioner (MSME), Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Government of India

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: SC/ST entrepreneurs allowed reimbursement for maximum of 2 international events and 4 domestic events in a financial year, irrespective of units owned. A person cannot represent more than one MSE in a financial year. Minimum participation of 5 SC/ST enterprises required for international exhibitions/trade fairs abroad. Application must be submitted at least 1 month in advance for domestic events and 2 months for international events.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Representation of multiple MSEs by one person in the same financial year is prohibited; exceeding the event cap (2 international, 4 domestic per year).
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Advance application (1 month for domestic, 2 months for international) submitted to implementing agency.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Valid Udyam Registration showing SC/ST ownership.

incentive_details.description: 100% subsidy on minimum stall size, 100% actual travel fare (bus/train AC-III/air limited to Rs. 10,000), and actual freight charges up to Rs. 15,000 per exhibition, subject to maximum ceiling of Rs. 1.50 lakhs per participating enterprise per event.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: 100% stall and travel support up to Rs. 1.50 lakhs per event for domestic exhibitions.
incentive_details.application_process: Application submitted to NSIC/NSSH; post-event submission of bills and boarding passes.

quantified_benefits.conditions: Application at least 1 month in advance; maximum 4 domestic events per financial year.
quantified_benefits.description: Maximum budgetary support per SC/ST enterprise per domestic event.
quantified_benefits.source_text: Maximum Budgetary support: Rs. 1.50 Lacs for a participating SC/ST enterprise per event

incentive_details.application_deadline: At least 1 month in advance of domestic event.

policy_goals: Facilitate technology upgradation of Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs) by providing upfront capital subsidy on institutional finance.

Enhance capacity, competitiveness, and marketability of SC/ST owned enterprises to fulfill the mandated 4% public procurement target by Central/State Governments and CPSEs.

eligibility_criteria.exclusions: PBGs submitted as EMD; non-accredited laboratories; clubbing with any other government or private subsidy schemes.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Valid Udyam Registration and proof of payment/debit required.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Udyam Registration.

incentive_details.description: Reimbursement of bank charges paid for issuance of PBG in favor of buyer departments where work has been awarded.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: 80% reimbursement up to Rs. 1,00,000 on Performance Bank Guarantee charges.
incentive_details.application_process: Online claim submission on NSSH portal with supply/work order and bank debit statement.

quantified_benefits.conditions: PBG issued in favor of Central/State government departments or CPSEs/SPSEs. EMD guarantees excluded.
quantified_benefits.description: Reimbursement of PBG bank charges.
quantified_benefits.source_text: The assistance under this scheme will be limited to 80% or Rs. 1,00,000/- (excluding GST and all other applicable taxes), whichever is less, on PBG charges paid in a financial year.

incentive_details.application_deadline: End of next quarter from reference date.

policy_goals: Facilitate technology upgradation of Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs) by providing upfront capital subsidy on institutional finance.
Promote induction of well-established, proven, clean, green, and energy-efficient technologies across manufacturing and service sectors.
Enhance capacity, competitiveness, and marketability of SC/ST owned enterprises to fulfill the mandated 4% public procurement target by Central/State Governments and CPSEs.
Support small scale industries graduating from small to medium scale and encourage price competitiveness in global and domestic markets.
policy_details.policy_summary: Provides reimbursements to SC/ST-owned MSEs on multiple operational and compliance costs including bank loan processing fees (80% up to Rs. 1 lakh), performance bank guarantee charges (80% up to Rs. 1 lakh), testing fees from NABL/BIS accredited labs (80% up to Rs. 1 lakh), export promotion council membership (80% up to Rs. 20,000), top 50 NIRF management institute course fees (90% up to Rs. 1 lakh), e-commerce portal membership (80% up to Rs. 25,000), and 100% subsidy for NSIC Single Point Registration Scheme (SPRS).
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to 80-100% reimbursement on loan processing fees, PBG charges, testing fees, NIRF training, and registrations for SC/ST MSEs.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Office of the Development Commissioner (MSME), Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Government of India

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: MSEs owned by SC/ST entrepreneurs (minimum 51% shareholding) having valid Udyam Registration. Claims must be submitted within the quarter immediately following the transaction/debit date.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: PBGs submitted as EMD; non-accredited laboratories; clubbing with any other government or private subsidy schemes.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Valid Udyam Registration and proof of payment/debit required.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Udyam Registration.

incentive_details.description: 100% subsidy for obtaining NSIC registration under the Single Point Registration Scheme for government purchases, subject to a nominal fee of Rs. 100/-.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: 100% subsidy on NSIC Single Point Registration Scheme (SPRS) with only Rs. 100 nominal fee.
incentive_details.application_process: Apply online at www.nsicspronline.com or duplicate physical form at nearest NSIC branch.

quantified_benefits.conditions: Applicant pays a nominal fee of Rs. 100/-.
quantified_benefits.description: Full subsidy on NSIC SPRS registration charges.
quantified_benefits.source_text: The component has provision for reimbursement of 100% subsidy to obtain NSIC's Registration under the Single Point Registration Scheme (SPRS) for government purchases with a nominal fee of Rs. 100/-.

parent_policy_name: Credit Linked Capital Subsidy and Technology Up-gradation Scheme (CLCS-TUS) / National Manufacturing Competitiveness Programme (NMCP)
policy_name: Lean Manufacturing Competitiveness Scheme (LMCS)
incentive_name: Financial Assistance for Lean Manufacturing Consultancy Fees

policy_goals: Enhance the manufacturing competitiveness of the MSME sector through the adoption of Lean Manufacturing (LM) techniques
Reduce waste and manufacturing costs through scientific inventory management, better space utilization, and improved process flows
Increase labour and resource productivity in MSMEs
Introduce innovative management practices and promote Zero Defect Zero Effect manufacturing
Inculcate good management systems and imbibe a culture of continuous improvement in MSME clusters
policy_details.policy_summary: The Lean Manufacturing Competitiveness Scheme (LMCS) assists Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in reducing manufacturing costs and improving product quality by adopting Lean Manufacturing (LM) techniques such as 5S, Visual Control, Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), Just in Time (JIT), KANBAN, Cellular Layout, Value Stream Mapping, Poka Yoke, SMED, Total Productive Maintenance (TPM), and Kaizen Blitz. Under the scheme, MSMEs form Mini Clusters (ideally 10 units, minimum 4 units) organized as a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) or Distinct Product Group (DPG). Government of India provides financial assistance covering up to 80% of the Lean Manufacturing Consultant (LMC) fees, while the remaining 20% is contributed by the beneficiary units. Implementation is structured in 5 milestone stages over a period of 18 months, monitored by the National Monitoring and Implementing Unit (NMIU) and the Project Monitoring and Advisory Committee (PMAC) / Screening and Steering Committee (SSC).
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to 80% financial support by Government of India towards consultant fees for implementing Lean Manufacturing techniques in MSME Mini Clusters.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Office of the Development Commissioner (Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises), Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Government of India

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: The Scheme is open to all Micro, Small and Medium Manufacturing Enterprises throughout the country which qualify as per the definition of the MSME Act, 2006. The units should be registered with Ministry of MSME U.A.M. (Udyog Aadhaar Memorandum). The units are required to form a MC ideally of 10 units (minimum 4) in the form of a SPV (Trust, Private Limited Company, Society, or Distinct Product Group/Sub Group under an Association). Units that have availed benefits in the pilot phase as well as up-scaled (2013) will not be allowed to take benefit in the up-scaled, Phase-II (2019) scheme.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Units that have already availed benefits in the pilot phase (2009) or up-scaled phase (2013) are not eligible to take benefit in the up-scaled Phase-II (2019) scheme.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Registration with Ministry of MSME under Udyog Aadhaar Memorandum (UAM) / Entrepreneurs Memorandum (EM); formalization of Mini Cluster via an SPV (Trust under Indian Trust Act 1882, Private Limited Company under Companies Act, Society under Societies Registration Act 1860, or Distinct Product Group/Sub Group under an Association).
special_category_benefits: Heterogeneous clusters permitted for ST/SC/Women entrepreneurs with dissimilar products

incentive_details.description: Financial assistance by the Government of India covering up to a maximum of 80% of the Lean Manufacturing Consultant (LMC) fees for each Mini Cluster to implement LM techniques. The remaining 20% of the consultancy cost is contributed by the beneficiary MSME units forming the cluster. Payments are released on a milestone basis across 5 stages.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: 80% government subsidy on Lean Manufacturing Consultant fees for MSME Mini Clusters.
incentive_details.application_process: Eligible MSME units form a Mini Cluster of ideally 10 (minimum 4) units, execute a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) and Power of Attorney appointing a Nodal Officer, incorporate an SPV (or form a Distinct Product Group under an Association), and submit the prescribed application format (Annexure 1) along with copies of UAM/EM to the NMIU/Implementing Agency for appraisal and approval by PMAC/SSC.

quantified_benefits.description: Government of India financial support for Lean Manufacturing Consultant fees per Mini Cluster
quantified_benefits.source_text: A financial support by the Government of India upto a maximum of 80% of the Consultant fees for each Mini Cluster will be provided. Remaining 20% is to be brone by the beneficiaries MSME units.

incentive_details.application_authority: National Monitoring and Implementing Unit (NMIU) / National Productivity Council (NPC) / Quality Council of India (QCI) / Office of DC (MSME)

policy_name: Cyber Security Policy 2024 - Operational and Procedural Guidelines (Public Domain)
incentive_name: Cyber Security R&D Project Funding Matching Grant

policy_goals: Make Karnataka the leading cyber security hub in the country by instilling a culture of cyber security and data privacy amongst citizens and businesses
Promote a thriving cyber security industry and start-up ecosystem in Karnataka
Build awareness across government departments, citizens, vulnerable groups, MSMEs, and colleges
Foster skill building and develop next-generation cyber security professionals through specialized curriculum and internships
Promote cutting-edge research, innovation, and R&D matching grants in collaboration with academic institutes
Support industry and start-ups through mentorship, pilot implementations, preferential procurement, and audit reimbursements
Establish institutions including K-CERT and Regional Centres of Excellence for capacity building and incident response
policy_details.policy_summary: The Cyber Security Policy 2024 was announced vide Government Order no. ITBT 48 ADM 2021 dated 16-03-2024 by the Department of Electronics, IT, BT & ST, Government of Karnataka. The public-facing guidelines are structured around five key pillars: Building Awareness, Skill Building, Promoting Research and Innovation, Promotion of Industry and Start-ups, and Partnerships and Collaborations for Capacity Building. The operational framework provides structured fiscal support administered via KITS (Karnataka Innovation and Technology Society), including: (1) internship stipend reimbursement of up to ₹10,000/month for undergraduate and ₹15,000/month for postgraduate interns for up to 3 months; (2) R&D matching grants of up to 50% of project costs capped at ₹50 lakhs for joint startup-academia research projects; and (3) audit reimbursement up to ₹1 lakh for CERT-In empaneled cyber security audits for registered start-ups. Non-fiscal interventions include setting up K-CERT, Regional Centres of Excellence, a Use Case Clearing House, specialized college curricula, preferential government procurement, and awareness sessions across districts and panchayats.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to ₹50 lakhs R&D matching grant, ₹15,000/month intern stipend reimbursement, and ₹1 lakh audit cost reimbursement for cyber security companies and start-ups in Karnataka.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Department of Electronics, IT, BT & ST, Government of Karnataka
special_focus_areas: Vulnerable groups (women, children, youth, first-time users, elderly)
Karnataka-based MSMEs and Start-ups working in cyberspace
Higher education cyber security curriculum and student skill building
State digital infrastructure resilience and K-CERT incident response

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: Clause 2.2 & 2.9 (Internship): Karnataka-based companies (MNCs, MSMEs, working in cyberspace, Start-ups) providing cyber security solutions and hiring students for cyber security roles. All applicants should be registered with KITS or in Karnataka under Shops and Establishment Act. Companies can hire students from only Karnataka based academic institutes, universities, colleges, polytechnics, etc. Clause 3.1 (R&D Funding): R&D projects driven by Karnataka-based start-ups in collaboration with Karnataka-based academic institutes. The start-up has to be registered with KITS, based in Karnataka & should provide cyber security services, while preference will be given to all academic institutions in Karnataka. The project shall be executed within Karnataka. Clause 4.4 (Audit Reimbursement): The applicant should be a Startup registered with KITS. The start-up can use the services of only CERT-In empaneled service providers for cyber security audit, incident management and incidence response activities. Certificate issued by the service provider of availment of cyber security audit to be submitted.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Projects that have received support from another domestic or international Government research grant source will not be eligible to receive further assistance through the R&D Fund. R&D costs borne before approval of the application shall not be eligible for reimbursement.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Internship scheme applications are processed on a rolling basis up to annual quota caps. For R&D grants, the applicant must have required expertise and team capacity; projects at Beta Site stage are also eligible.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Must be based in Karnataka; academic partners and student interns must also be from Karnataka-based institutions.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Registered with KITS (Karnataka Innovation and Technology Society) or registered in Karnataka under the Shops and Establishment Act; Start-ups must be registered with Karnataka Start-up Cell / KITS.

incentive_details.description: A conditional matching grant provided to Karnataka-based start-ups undertaking approved cutting-edge R&D projects in cyber security in joint collaboration with academic institutions. The scheme covers up to 50% of the approved project R&D expenditures up to ₹50 lakhs. The remaining 50% is borne by the startup and/or academic institution/industry partner. Up to 5 projects are funded each year, with each entity eligible once over the policy period. Grants are disbursed in milestone-based tranches following execution of a Project Funding Agreement.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: Matching grant of up to 50% of project R&D cost, capped at ₹50 lakhs for startup-academia collaborative cyber security research.
incentive_details.application_process: Submit application online on www.itbtst.karnataka.gov.in. An R&D Sub-Committee conducts techno-financial and onsite evaluation (50% innovation, 30% business impact, 20% implementation capabilities). Recommendations are sent to the Approval Committee. Approved applicants sign a Project Funding Agreement (PFA); funds are released in tranches based on predefined milestones.

quantified_benefits.conditions: Project must be executed within Karnataka; entity can avail grant once over policy period; project must focus on innovative products leveraging cutting-edge cyber security technologies.
quantified_benefits.description: Matching grant for approved cyber security R&D project expenditure
quantified_benefits.source_text: For R&D projects driven by Karnataka based start-ups in collaboration with Karnataka-based academic institutes, a matching grant of up to a maximum of 50% of the total project R&D cost, or up to Rs. 50 lakhs, whichever is lower will be provided.
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: Karnataka-based start-ups collaborating with academic institutions on cyber security R&D

incentive_details.application_deadline: Rolling basis (limited to 5 approved projects per year)
incentive_details.application_authority: KITS / Approval Committee headed by Managing Director, KITS
incentive_details.incentive_specific_eligibility: Must be a Karnataka-based start-up registered with KITS providing cyber security services, partnering with an academic institution. Projects must not have received funding from another government research source.

incentive_details.description: Government of Karnataka provides monthly stipend reimbursement to Karnataka-based companies (MNCs, MSMEs, and Start-ups) offering cyber security solutions and hiring Karnataka-based students for cyber security roles for a maximum period of 3 months. In Year 1 and Year 2, support is provided to 200 undergraduate and 40 postgraduate interns per year; from Year 3 onwards, support expands to 400 undergraduate and 80 postgraduate interns per year. Per company annual limits are up to 10 interns for Start-ups, up to 15 interns for MSMEs, and up to 20 interns for MNCs (with single cycle caps of up to 30 UG & 10 PG students in Years 1-2, and 60 UG & 10 PG students in Year 3 onwards).
incentive_details.benefit_headline: Stipend reimbursement of ₹10,000/month for UG interns and ₹15,000/month for PG interns for up to 3 months.
incentive_details.application_process: Apply online to KITS detailing intern headcount, proposed stipend, and activities. The company pays monthly stipend to interns and issues completion certificates. Post-internship, the company submits claim to KITS along with CA-certified stipend payment proofs for Approval Committee sanction and fund release.

quantified_benefits.cap_raw: INR 10,000 per month for a maximum period of three months (₹30,000 total per intern)
quantified_benefits.conditions: Maximum period of 3 months; students must be from Karnataka-based academic institutes, universities, colleges, or polytechnics.
quantified_benefits.description: Monthly stipend reimbursement for Karnataka-based undergraduate interns in cyber security roles
quantified_benefits.source_text: GoK will reimburse INR 10,000 per month for a maximum period of three months, to companies hiring Karnataka based undergraduate cyber security interns.
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: Undergraduate interns hired by eligible Karnataka cyber security companies

quantified_benefits.cap_raw: INR 15,000 per month for a maximum period of three months (₹45,000 total per intern)
quantified_benefits.conditions: Maximum period of 3 months; students must be from Karnataka-based academic institutes, universities, colleges, or polytechnics.
quantified_benefits.description: Monthly stipend reimbursement for Karnataka-based postgraduate interns in cyber security roles
quantified_benefits.source_text: GoK will reimburse INR 15,000 per month for a maximum period of three months, to companies hiring Karnataka based postgraduate cyber security interns.
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: Postgraduate interns hired by eligible Karnataka cyber security companies

incentive_details.application_deadline: Rolling basis until the annual quota cap is reached
incentive_details.application_authority: Karnataka Innovation and Technology Society (KITS) / Department of Electronics, IT, BT & ST
incentive_details.incentive_specific_eligibility: Company must be registered with KITS or under Karnataka Shops and Establishment Act. Interns must be recruited strictly from Karnataka-based academic institutions and assigned exclusively to cyber security roles.
