Available to 100 start-ups per year, once per start-up over the 5-year policy period.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: Reimbursement of up to ₹1 lakh for cyber security audit and incident management services by CERT-In empaneled providers.
incentive_details.application_process: Eligible start-up engages and pays a CERT-In empaneled provider, completes the audit, and submits Form 3 to KITS with audit certificate, invoice, and payment receipt. Approval Committee reviews and recommends to the Governing Council for final sanction and disbursal.

quantified_benefits.value_raw: up to a maximum of INR 1 lakh
quantified_benefits.conditions: Services must be availed from Karnataka-based, CERT-In empaneled service providers between 16th March 2024 and 15th March 2029; maximum once over policy period excluding GST.
quantified_benefits.description: Cost reimbursement for cybersecurity audit, incident management, and incident response activities
quantified_benefits.source_text: The Government of Karnataka will reimburse the cost up to a maximum of INR 1 lakh towards engagement of Karnataka-based, CERT-In empaneled service providers by start-ups registered with Karnataka Start-up Cell for cyber security audit, incident management and incident response activities. This may be availed by a start-up once over the policy period. This benefit will be provided to 100 start-ups each year.
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: Start-ups registered with Karnataka Start-up Cell / KITS

incentive_details.application_deadline: Applicable for services undertaken from 16th March 2024 to 15th March 2029
incentive_details.incentive_specific_eligibility: Start-up must be registered with KITS / Karnataka Start-up Cell. Service provider must be Karnataka-based and CERT-In empaneled.

policy_name: Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS)
incentive_name: Additional Turnover Linked Incentive for Domestic Localization

policy_goals: Develop a robust component manufacturing ecosystem by attracting global and domestic investments across the value chain
Increase Domestic Value Addition (DVA) in electronics manufacturing
Increase the share of Bharat's exports in global electronic trade by integrating the domestic electronic industry with Global Value Chains (GVCs)

policy_name: Karnataka Engineering Research & Development (Engineering R&D) Policy 2021
incentive_name: Applied Research in Academia Program

policy_goals: Enable Karnataka to contribute ~45% to India's Engineering R&D during the policy period
Create an additional ~50,000 new jobs (direct & indirect) for skilled manpower in the Engineering R&D sector during the policy period
Grow regional economies by promoting innovation and Engineering R&D across Karnataka beyond Bengaluru Urban District
Develop a research-oriented skilled talent pool and foster a knowledge economy
Attract Engineering R&D intensive investment into Karnataka
Augment capacity by bridging the gap between Engineering/Research talent and industry technology needs
policy_details.policy_summary: The Karnataka Engineering Research & Development (Engineering R&D) Policy 2021 aims to establish Karnataka as the premier destination for Engineering R&D by attracting Multinational Companies (MNCs), Global Capability Centers (GCCs), and Engineering Service Providers (ESPs). Built on three strategic pillars—attracting entities to set up or expand operations, marketing Karnataka's ER&D advantages globally, and bridging the talent-opportunity gap—the policy focuses on 5 priority sectors: Aerospace & Defence; Auto, Auto Components & EV; Biotechnology, Pharma & Medical Devices; Semiconductors, Telecom & ESDM; and Software Products. It provides comprehensive fiscal incentives including rental reimbursements, recruitment assistance, investment subsidies on fixed infrastructure, technological innovation grants, common testing/prototyping infrastructure support, corporate innovation labs funding, digital public challenge grants, event and academic research sponsorships, student skill courses, internship stipends, and Ph.D. fellowships.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to ₹8 Cr R&D innovation grants, ₹50 Cr testing infrastructure assistance, 20% capex subsidy, and ₹2 Cr rental reimbursement for ER&D enterprises in Karnataka.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Department of Electronics, Information Technology, Biotechnology and Science & Technology, Government of Karnataka
special_focus_areas: Women in Tech and Engineering (25% to 33% mandatory quotas)
Deep-tech and Emerging Technologies (AI/ML, IoT, 5G, Robotics, Blockchain, Quantum Computing)
Intellectual Property (IP) Registration and Retention in India

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: To avail the policy incentives and concessions, an entity must belong to one of the following categories: a.i. MNC Indian entities setting up or expanding GCCs with global revenue of USD 2 billion (~ INR 15,477 Cr) (highest revenue of the last 3 financial years) and above and with commitment of minimum employment of 200 for Offering 3.5.A.1; and a.ii. MNC Indian entities with revenue of INR 200 crores (highest revenue of the last 3 financial years) and above for Offerings 3.5.A.2 to 3.5.A.5 and Offerings 3.5.C.1 & 3.5.C.3. c. ESP with revenue of INR 200 crores and above (highest revenue of the last 3 financial years) applicable for Offerings 3.5.C.1, 3.5.C.3, and 3.5.C.4. d. State Government Universities / State Government Universities' Affiliated Colleges based in Karnataka and students enrolled in these academic institutions for Offerings 3.5.C.1, 3.5.C.2 and 3.5.C.4. Additionally, entities should fulfill: Nature of Business: All legal entities operating in the Engineering R&D industry. Location: Registered office in Karnataka as per Companies Act 1956/2013 or registered as per Karnataka Shops & Commercial Establishment Act 1961, setting up new or expanding existing operations in Karnataka. Employment: At least 50% of the entity's total qualified technical workforce must be based out of Karnataka (excluding contract employees). Minimum 25% employment to women personnel.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Contract employees are excluded from the 50% technical workforce calculation; temporary R&D personnel employed and paid by a related company are not supported as direct labor; third parties engaged for mass production, general legal/business consultation, or general administration are excluded from R&D grant expenditures; projects that have received support from another Government source are ineligible for the Engineering R&D Fund.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Entities must register with Karnataka Innovation and Technology Society (KITS). Projects must fall within 5 priority sectors. Full-scale R&D projects must range from TRL4 to TRL9 and commercialize within 3 years (5 years for Aerospace & Defence). New IP registration in India is a mandatory prerequisite for R&D funding.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Operations must be located in Karnataka; incentives under Pillar A (Establishment of R&D Centers, R&D Infrastructure, Innovation Labs) specifically require units to be established beyond Bengaluru Urban District (Bengaluru North, Bengaluru North Addl., Bengaluru South, Bengaluru East, and Anekal).
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Registration under KITS / Department of Electronics, IT, Bt and S&T, Government of Karnataka; registration under Companies Act 1956/2013 or Karnataka Shops & Commercial Establishment Act 1961.
special_category_benefits: Women (minimum 25% employment commitment across projects; 33% female representation required in Future Skills training and internships; 25% female fellowship quota in CM Research Fellowship)

incentive_details.description: Grants to academic research institutions (State Govt Universities and Affiliated Colleges offering B.Tech/M.Tech/PhD) partnering with an ER&D GCC or ESP for cutting-edge applied research.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: 75% funding up to ₹75 Lakhs for single-institution projects and up to ₹1 Crore for collaborative projects across two institutions.
incentive_details.application_process: Call for proposal, industry partner selection and research area matchmaking, evaluation of university infrastructure, signing of tri-partite agreement, and milestone-based disbursement.

quantified_benefits.description: 75% funding of approved budget for 12 months for single academic institution projects (industry partner funds remaining 25%)
quantified_benefits.source_text: GoK will provide funding equivalent to 75% of the approved budget, up to INR 75 lakhs for 12 months (while the participating entity funds the remaining 25% of the approved project cost).
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: State Government Universities/Affiliated Colleges in Karnataka with Industry Partner

quantified_benefits.description: Enhanced grant funding for applied research projects conducted in collaboration between two different institutions
quantified_benefits.source_text: If the project is conducted in collaboration with two different institutions, the project will be eligible to receive a funding of up to INR 1 crore for 12 months.
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: Joint academic projects across two institutions with ER&D industry partner

incentive_details.application_deadline: As notified under Call for Proposals

Reduce demand for physical gold and outflow of foreign exchange through the Sovereign Gold Bond Scheme

policy_details.policy_summary: Under Section 80EE of the Income-tax Act, first-time home buyers availing home loans from financial institutions are provided an additional deduction of up to ₹50,000 per financial year in respect of interest paid on loan taken for acquisition of residential house property. The incentive applies to properties valued under ₹50 lakhs with an approved loan amount not exceeding ₹35 lakhs sanctioned between 1st April 2016 and 31st March 2017, and continues till the repayment of the loan.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Additional income tax deduction of up to ₹50,000 per year for interest on home loans for first-time home buyers, over and above Section 24.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Ministry of Finance, Government of India

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: In furtherance of the goal of the Government of providing 'Housing For All', section 80EE of the Income-tax Act has been substituted to incentivise first-home buyers availing home loans, by providing additional deduction of Rs 50,000 in respect of interest on loan taken for acquisition of a residential house property from any financial institution. This incentive has been extended to a house property of a value less than fifty lakhs rupees in respect of which a loan of an amount not exceeding thirty five lakh rupees has been sanctioned during the period from the 1st day of April, 2016 to the 31st day of March, 2017. Further, this benefit of deduction is extended till the repayment of loan continues. This deduction under section 80EE shall be over and above the deduction of two lakh rupees available under section 24 of the Income tax Act for interest payable on loan taken for self-occupied property.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: The assessee must be an individual first-time home buyer who does not own any residential house property on the date of sanction of loan. Loan must be sanctioned by a financial institution or housing finance company between 1st April 2016 and 31st March 2017.

incentive_details.description: An additional deduction of up to ₹50,000 per assessment year in respect of interest payable on loan taken for acquisition of a residential house property, available until the repayment of the loan continues, over and above the limit of ₹2,00,000 under section 24.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: Up to ₹50,000 annual deduction on home loan interest till full loan repayment.
incentive_details.application_process: Claimed by individual taxpayers in their annual income tax return.

quantified_benefits.description: Additional annual income tax deduction on interest paid on residential housing loan
quantified_benefits.source_text: providing additional deduction of Rs 50,000 in respect of interest on loan taken for acquisition of a residential house property from any financial institution.

policy_goals: Promote employment generation across all sectors by incentivizing recruitment of new employees

policy_details.policy_summary: To facilitate Indian corporates in raising overseas capital via Rupee Denominated Bonds (Masala Bonds) and provide relief against currency fluctuation risk, Section 48 of the Income-tax Act was amended to exempt capital gains resulting from rupee appreciation between the date of issue and the date of redemption from capital gains tax for non-resident investors.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Full capital gains tax exemption for non-resident investors on currency appreciation gains from Rupee Denominated Bonds.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Ministry of Finance, Government of India

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: The Reserve Bank of India permitted Indian corporates to issue rupee denominated bonds outside India as a measure to enable the Indian corporates to raise funds from outside India. Accordingly, with a view to provide relief to non-resident investor who bears the risk of currency fluctuation, section 48 of the Income-tax Act has been amended to provide that the capital gains, arising in case of appreciation of rupee between the date of issue and the date of redemption against the foreign currency in which the investment is made shall be exempt from tax on capital gains.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Applicable to non-resident investors investing in rupee denominated bonds issued outside India by Indian corporate entities.

incentive_details.description: Capital gains arising on account of foreign exchange fluctuations/appreciation of the rupee between issue and redemption dates against the invested foreign currency are completely exempt from tax on capital gains.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: Exemption from capital gains tax on currency appreciation gains for non-resident investors.

quantified_benefits.value_raw: Exempt from tax on capital gains
quantified_benefits.description: Exemption from capital gains tax on gains arising from rupee appreciation between issue and redemption dates
quantified_benefits.source_text: capital gains, arising in case of appreciation of rupee between the date of issue and the date of redemption against the foreign currency in which the investment is made shall be exempt from tax on capital gains.

policy_details.policy_summary: To provide tax parity between physical gold and Sovereign Gold Bonds (SGB) and reduce foreign exchange outflow from physical gold imports, the Income-tax Act was amended to exempt capital gains on redemption of SGBs by individuals from tax. Furthermore, indexation benefits are provided on long-term capital gains arising from the transfer of SGBs to all assessees.
policy_details.benefit_headline: 100% capital gains tax exemption on redemption of Sovereign Gold Bonds for individuals, plus indexation benefits on transfer.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Ministry of Finance, Government of India

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: Section 47 of the Income-tax Act has been amended so as to provide that any redemption of Sovereign Gold Bond under the Scheme, by an individual shall not be treated as transfer and therefore shall be exempt from tax on capital gains. Further, Section 48 of the Income-tax Act has also been amended so as to provide indexation benefits to long term capital gains arising on transfer of Sovereign Gold Bond to all assessees.

incentive_details.description: Redemption of Sovereign Gold Bonds by an individual investor is not treated as a transfer under section 47 of the Income-tax Act, making gains arising on redemption fully exempt from capital gains tax.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: Complete exemption from capital gains tax on redemption of Sovereign Gold Bonds by individuals.

quantified_benefits.value_raw: Exempt from tax on capital gains

quantified_benefits.source_text: any redemption of Sovereign Gold Bond under the Scheme, by an individual shall not be treated as transfer and therefore shall be exempt from tax on capital gains.

Further the goal of 'Housing For All' by incentivizing first-home buyers availing home loans
Reduce demand for physical gold and outflow of foreign exchange through the Sovereign Gold Bond Scheme

policy_details.policy_summary: Section 80JJAA of the Income-tax Act provides a tax deduction of thirty percent of additional employee cost (emoluments paid to new regular employees) for three assessment years to businesses subject to tax audit. The incentive is available across all sectors for employees earning emoluments up to ₹25,000 per month who are employed for at least 240 days in the financial year (relaxed to 150 days for apparel, footwear, and leather manufacturing). In the first year of a new business, 30% of all emoluments paid or payable are eligible for deduction.
policy_details.benefit_headline: 30% additional tax deduction for 3 years on salaries paid to newly hired employees earning up to ₹25,000 per month.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Ministry of Finance, Government of India

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: Deduction under section 80JJAA is available to an assessee deriving business income and liable for tax audit under the Income Tax Act, 1961. Deduction is available in respect of cost incurred on any new employee whose total emoluments are less than or equal to twenty five thousand rupees per month. Employees must have worked for at least 240 days in the financial year (or at least 150 days for an assessee engaged in the business of manufacturing of apparel, footwear, or leather products). Salary must be paid via banking channels (not cash), and employees should be registered under Provident Fund (PF) laws with PF deductible. In the first year of a new business, 30% of all emoluments paid or payable to employees employed during the previous year shall be allowed as deduction. No deduction is allowed in respect of cost incurred on those employees for whom the entire contribution under Employees' Pension Scheme notified in accordance with Employees' Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952, is paid by the Government.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Employees for whom the entire contribution under the Employees' Pension Scheme (EPS) is paid by the Government; employees whose monthly emoluments exceed ₹25,000; employees employed for less than 240 days (or 150 days for apparel/footwear/leather); salary payments made in cash.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Taxpayer must have business income and be liable to tax audit under Income Tax Act, 1961. Deduction must be claimed in the return of income accompanied by a report in the prescribed form from a chartered accountant.

incentive_details.description: A deduction equal to thirty per cent of additional employee cost incurred in the course of business in the previous year is allowed for three assessment years including the assessment year relevant to the previous year in which such employment is provided. In the first year of a new business, thirty per cent of all emoluments paid or payable to employees employed during the previous year is allowed as a deduction.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: 30% deduction on emoluments of new employees for 3 consecutive assessment years (total 90% additional deduction over and above normal 100% business expense).
incentive_details.application_process: Detailed calculation based on employment and payroll data, filing of the relevant income tax audit report form certifying the deduction, and claiming the deduction in the Return of Income.

quantified_benefits.description: Tax deduction of 30% of additional employee cost paid or payable to eligible new employees for three assessment years
quantified_benefits.source_text: section 80JJAA has been substituted to provide that the deduction under the said provisions shall be available in respect of cost incurred on any employee whose total emoluments are less than or equal to twenty five thousand rupees per month... thirty per cent of additional wages paid to new regular workmen in a factory for three years.

quantified_benefits.description: In the first year of a new business, 30% deduction of all emoluments paid or payable to employees employed during the previous year
quantified_benefits.source_text: It is also provided that in the first year of a new business, thirty per cent of all emoluments paid or payable to the employees employed during the previous year shall be allowed as deduction.

policy_goals: Envisage Goa as an aspirational geographical and human resource base for IT Units
Establish Goa as a preferred destination for IT investment and expansion
policy_details.policy_summary: Framed in pursuance of clause 6.2.1 of the Goa IT Policy 2018, this scheme provides a one-time rebate on the purchase of land or built-up office space for creating IT office space and operations in Goa. Units must maintain direct employment proportional to built-up space up to 80 sq. ft. per employee for at least 12 months. Rebate is disbursed in three tranches post-COD and prorated based on the share of Goan employees.
policy_details.benefit_headline: One-time rebate up to 60% of land cost (up to ₹1.5 crore) or up to 20% of built-up office space cost (up to ₹1 crore) for IT units in Goa.

eligibility_criteria.raw_text:
4.1. All the New and Existing Units must have their operations in Goa.
4.2. The applicant must be one of the below: Proprietorship Firm, Private Limited Company, Public Limited Company, Registered Partnership Firm, Limited Liability Partnership.
4.3. The bank accounts of unit and/or its partner(s)/director(s) should be linked to Aadhaar.
4.4. The applicant unit shall be eligible for the benefits under this scheme only up on production of Udyog Aadhaar.
4.5. The unit can avail land/ built up area rebate only if the unit has operated from the said office space for a period of more than one year.
4.6. For claiming the incentive, the unit should achieve the targets (both investments and employment) mentioned in the business plan.
4.7. This rebate will be reimbursed to the companies in three tranches post Commercial Operation Date or from the date of notification of the policy, whichever is later.
4.8. The Units availing similar financial incentives under any other policy of the Government of Goa are not eligible.

policy_details.policy_summary: The Karnataka Aerospace & Defence Policy 2022-2027 provides incentives across Karnataka's zonal framework (Zone 1, 2, and 3) for MSMEs and Large/Mega/Super Mega enterprises in aerospace, civil & defence aviation assemblies, MRO, satellite space applications, composite manufacturing, and electronics. Benefits include investment promotion subsidies up to 35% of VFA for MSMEs, 20% subsidy on plant & machinery, 20-25% subsidy on land up to 50 acres, 1% production-linked incentive (PLI) for 5 years, anchor subsidies up to ₹10 Crores, and complete stamp duty exemptions.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to 35% MSME capital subsidy, 20% Plant & Machinery subsidy, 25% Land subsidy, and 1% PLI on annual turnover for 5 years.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Karnataka Digital Economy Mission (KDEM), Department of Electronics, IT, BT and S&T, Government of Karnataka
special_focus_areas: Civil and Defence Aviation End Assemblies

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: Incentives will be provided only to new investments or for capacity expansion. It will not be applicable for existing companies. Total quantum of incentives sanctioned to a unit shall not exceed 40% of Value of Fixed Assets created by the unit in Zone-3 and 50% of the Value of Fixed Assets (VFA) created by the unit in Zone-1 & 2 (or 100% of VFA for manufacturing/assembly units under specific packages). Plant & machinery subsidy for integrated aviation assemblies requires min investment of INR 1,000 Crore, and for MRO requires min investment of INR 500 Crore.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Existing companies without new investments or capacity expansions are not eligible.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Minimum 20 direct employees for first INR 10 Crore and additional 7 employees for every additional INR 10 Crore investment for Medium Enterprises.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Zonal categorization: Zone 1, Zone 2, Zone 3. Land subsidy available outside Bengaluru Urban and Rural districts.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Clearance via Karnataka Udyog Mitra single window mechanism.
special_category_benefits: SC/ST, Women, Minorities, Physically Challenged, and Ex-Servicemen Entrepreneurs receive additional 5% VFA subsidy (up to ₹5 Lakhs extra)

incentive_details.description: 20% subsidy on Plant & Machinery (paid in 5 equal annual installments) and 20% to 25% subsidy on land up to 50 acres outside Bengaluru Urban and Rural districts.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: 20% subsidy on Plant & Machinery and up to 25% land subsidy on up to 50 acres.
incentive_details.application_process: Apply through KUM single window system.

quantified_benefits.conditions: Paid over five equal annual payments; minimum investment of INR 1000 Cr for end assemblies, INR 500 Cr for MRO
quantified_benefits.description: Subsidy on Plant & Machinery for focus sub-sectors
quantified_benefits.source_text: Capital investment Subsidy: 20% on Plant & Machinery. The 20% capital Investment subsidy on Plant & Machinery shall be paid over five equal annual payments.
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: Large, Mega, Ultra Mega, and Super Mega Enterprises in focus sub-sectors

quantified_benefits.conditions: Up to an extent of 50 acres outside Bengaluru Urban and Rural districts

quantified_benefits.source_text: 25% on Land only in areas other than Bengaluru Urban and Bengaluru Rural District up to an extent of 50 acres on actual procurement cost.

policy_details.policy_summary: The Karnataka Biotechnology Policy 2017-2022 aims to simplify clearances, coordinate integrated R&D, leverage Bio-IT tools, and provide funding mechanisms for biotech startups and manufacturers. Key incentives include an Anchor Investment Subsidy of ₹5 Crore per taluk for manufacturing units, DPR preparation reimbursement, industrial power tariff concessions, 6% interest subsidy for MSME technology upgradation, standardization certificate assistance up to ₹5 Lakhs, and patent cost reimbursements.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Anchor investment subsidy of ₹5 Crore per taluk, 6% interest subsidy for MSME tech upgradation, and ₹5 Lakhs standardization support.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Karnataka Digital Economy Mission (KDEM), Department of Electronics, IT, BT and S&T, Government of Karnataka

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: Only registered Biotechnology companies can apply for the subsidies / incentives / grants available under this policy. A first-time applicant needs to apply for registration as a Biotechnology company by completing the Biotech registration form through the online portal https://itbtst.karnataka.gov.in. Most incentives (DPR reimbursement, standardization certificate, patent registration, marketing incentives) apply to enterprises with annual turnover not exceeding INR 50 Crore.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Anchor subsidy is not available in taluks where manufacturing enterprises with investment of INR 50 Crore and above already exist.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Enterprises must have an annual turnover not exceeding INR 50 Crore for most operational incentives.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Karnataka taluks; specific conditions for anchor units.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Registered as a Biotechnology company via https://itbtst.karnataka.gov.in or http://registration.k-tech.org/

incentive_details.benefit_headline: ₹5 Crore Anchor Investment Subsidy for new greenfield manufacturing investments of ₹50+ Crores.
incentive_details.application_process: Apply via Biotech portal at https://itbtst.karnataka.gov.in.

quantified_benefits.description: Anchor Investment Subsidy per unit

This subsidy will be applicable only in taluks where no such manufacturing or industrial enterprises with an investment of INR 50 Crore and above currently exist.

policy_details.policy_summary: The Karnataka Data Centre Policy 2022-2027 provides incentives to attract investments into data centre infrastructure outside Bengaluru Urban District. Benefits include a 7% capital subsidy up to ₹10 Crores on fixed assets (excluding land and building), 10% land subsidy up to ₹3 Crores, 100% stamp duty and land conversion fee exemptions, concessional registration charges, industrial power tariffs for units with at least 30% green power, ₹0.50/unit green tariff surcharge reimbursement up to ₹1.25 Crores, and 5-year electricity duty exemption.
policy_details.benefit_headline: 7% capital subsidy up to ₹10 Crores, 10% land subsidy up to ₹3 Crores, and 100% stamp duty exemption for Data Centres outside Bengaluru Urban District.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Karnataka Digital Economy Mission (KDEM), Department of Electronics, IT, BT and S&T, Government of Karnataka
special_focus_areas: Green and Renewable Energy Powered Data Centres

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: To avail incentives, concessions and subsidies under the Policy, the applicant must be registered with KITS/Department. Applicants are required to submit registration application as per the process. Upon successful verification of the submitted application and the assessment of all the facts and information, Applicants will be required to make a one-time registration processing fees payment of Rs. 10,000/- + (18% GST).
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Minimum 30% green energy component required for industrial power tariff; above 50% renewable energy for green tariff surcharge reimbursement.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Outside Bengaluru Urban District for capital, land, stamp duty, and conversion fee incentives.

policy_details.policy_summary: The Karnataka Electric Vehicles and Energy Storage Policy 2017 aims to make Karnataka a preferred investment hub for EV and component manufacturing, battery assembly, and charging infrastructure. It offers investment promotion subsidies for MSMEs (up to 25% or ₹50 Lakhs), 20% capital subsidy up to ₹20 Crores for EV battery units, 100% stamp duty exemption, 100% land conversion reimbursement, 50% ETP capital subsidy (up to ₹50 Lakhs for MSMEs, ₹200 Lakhs for Large/Mega), and 100% electricity duty exemption for 5 years.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to 25% investment subsidy for MSMEs, 20% subsidy up to ₹20 Crores for EV battery units, and 100% stamp duty exemption.

special_focus_areas: Lithium-ion Battery Pack and Cell Manufacturing

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: All the EV manufacturing Enterprises will be eligible for the incentives and concessions. Manufacturing Enterprises of components required for Electric Vehicles such as Motors, Power Trains, Power Electronics kits, etc. will be eligible for incentives and concessions as per the policy subject to the approval of the Technical Committee which would be substituted & mandated to define/certify EV component manufacturing enterprises. All the EV Battery manufacturing/ Assembly Enterprises will be eligible for the incentives and concessions.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Component manufacturers subject to approval and certification by the designated Technical Committee.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: State of Karnataka.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Certified by Technical Committee mandated to define/certify EV component and battery manufacturing enterprises.

incentive_details.application_process: Apply through KUM.

policy_details.policy_summary: The Karnataka ER&D Policy 2021-2026 seeks to position Karnataka as a global destination for engineering design and R&D. It offers rental reimbursements up to ₹2 Crores, recruitment assistance of ₹20 Lakhs, investment subsidies up to 20% (max ₹2 Crores), innovation grants up to 40% (max ₹8 Crores), open innovation labs funding, and prototyping infrastructure grants up to ₹50 Crores for GCCs and MNCs expanding Beyond Bengaluru Urban District.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to ₹2 Crore rental reimbursement, ₹20 Lakh recruitment assistance, and ₹8 Crore innovation grants for ER&D GCCs Beyond Bengaluru.

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: MNC Indian entities setting up or expanding GCCs with global revenue of USD 2 billion and above and with commitment of minimum employment of 200, and MNC Indian entities setting up or expanding GCCs with revenue of INR 200 crores and above. State Government Universities / Affiliated Colleges based in Karnataka and students enrolled. All legal entities operating in ER&D industry with registered office in Karnataka. At least 50% of entity's total qualified workforce should be based out of Karnataka (excluding contract employees) and provide at least 25% employment to women personnel.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Contract employees are not counted toward the 50% qualified workforce requirement.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: At least 25% of employment must be provided to women personnel.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Registered office in Karnataka; incentives largely applicable beyond Bengaluru Urban District.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Registered under Companies Act 2013 or Shops & Commercial Establishment Act 1961 in Karnataka.

policy_details.policy_summary: The Karnataka ESDM Policy 2017-2022 promotes electronics system design and manufacturing across Karnataka. Registered KESDM companies are eligible for anchor unit capital subsidies of up to 10% (max ₹10 Crore), patent reimbursements, international marketing reimbursements, R&D grants, prototyping subsidies, PF/ESI support, interest subsidies up to 6%, stamp duty exemptions, and ETP subsidies.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to 10% capital subsidy (max ₹10 Crore) for anchor units, 100% stamp duty exemption for MSMEs, and 6% interest subsidy.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Karnataka Digital Economy Mission (KDEM), Department of Electronics, IT, BT and S&T, Government of Karnataka

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: The company or entity should be engaged in manufacturing/design of electronics products, intermediates, EMS, design/IP/software services, or NPE/NPM verticals. The company or entity should be registered in Karnataka under the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishment Act, 1961. The company or entity employs at least 50 percent of its total workforce in Karnataka, which should not include contract employees. The company or entity should do value addition within the state (Year 1: 25%, Year 2: 30%, Year 3: 35%, Year 4: 40%, Year 5: 45%).
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Contract employees are excluded from workforce headcount calculation.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Must achieve progressive BOM value addition from 25% in Year 1 to 45% in Year 5. One-time registration charge of Rs. 10,000 + GST.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Registered in Karnataka under Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishment Act, 1961.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Must be registered with KITS as a KESDM company via http://registration.k-tech.org/

incentive_details.description: Up to 10% capital subsidy capped at INR 10 Crores to registered KESDM companies, applicable to the first two anchor units in each greenfield cluster.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: Up to 10% capital subsidy up to ₹10 Crores for the first two anchor units in greenfield clusters.
incentive_details.application_process: Apply online at www.itbtst.karnataka.gov.in.

quantified_benefits.conditions: Applicable to the first two anchor units in each greenfield cluster
quantified_benefits.description: Capital subsidy for first two anchor units in greenfield cluster
quantified_benefits.source_text: The Govt. of Karnataka will provide up to 10% capital subsidy, up to a maximum of INR 10 Crores to registered KESDM companies, which will be applicable to the first two anchor units in each greenfield cluster.
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: First two anchor units in each greenfield cluster

incentive_details.incentive_specific_eligibility: First two anchor units in greenfield clusters.

policy_details.policy_summary: The Karnataka IT Policy 2020-2025 aims to foster IT and ITeS growth across Karnataka, especially focusing on areas outside Zone 3 and emerging tech clusters Beyond Bengaluru. It provides financial support for IT hubs, co-working spaces, rental reimbursements, stamp duty exemptions, subsidized industrial power tariffs, quality certifications, marketing assistance, PF/ESI reimbursements, patent cost support, and matching grants for emerging technologies such as 5G.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to ₹3 Crore subsidy for IT Hubs, ₹2 Crore for co-working spaces, 100% stamp duty exemption outside Zone 3, and 33% R&D matching grants up to ₹1 Crore.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Karnataka Digital Economy Mission (KDEM), Department of Electronics, IT, BT and S&T, Government of Karnataka

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: The entity must be registered with KITS, Department of Electronics, IT, BT, and S&T, Government of Karnataka as an IT/ITeS entity. The entity shall be engaged in Information Technology (IT) or IT Enabled Services. The entity must have a registered office in Karnataka as per the companies Act, 2013, or the Entity should be registered as per the Karnataka Shops & Commercial Establishment Act, 1961. The entity employs at least 50% of its total qualified workforce in Karnataka, which shall not include contract employees.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Contract employees are not counted toward the minimum 50% qualified workforce requirement. Indian subsidiaries of foreign entities are not eligible for R&D Support.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Entity must pay a one-time registration processing fee of Rs. 10,000 + 18% GST and incentive processing fees of Rs. 10,000 to Rs. 20,000 + 18% GST.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Registered office in Karnataka; incentives such as Lease/Rental reimbursement, PF/ESI reimbursement, and Quality Certification apply to entities set up outside Zone 3.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Registered with KITS, Department of Electronics, IT, BT, and S&T, Government of Karnataka as an IT/ITeS entity.

incentive_details.application_process: Apply online through www.itbtst.karnataka.gov.in.

quantified_benefits.conditions: Minimum built-up area of 15000 sq. ft. and minimum occupancy rate of 60% by IT/ITeS entities or minimum occupancy by 300 professionals in IT/ITeS.

incentive_details.incentive_specific_eligibility: Minimum built-up area of 15,000 sq. ft.

policy_details.policy_summary: The Karnataka Startup Policy 2022-2027 supports startups across Karnataka, prioritizing emerging tech clusters Beyond Bengaluru and socially inclusive entrepreneurship. Key offerings include Idea2PoC grants of up to ₹50 Lakhs, a ₹100 Crore Venture Capital Fund (25% reserved for women entrepreneurs), incubator establishment and augmentation grants up to ₹50 Lakhs, 100% SGST reimbursement, marketing cost reimbursement, patent cost support, internship subsidies, and special initiatives such as Elevate-Unnati and Elevate WomEN.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to ₹50 Lakhs Idea2PoC grant, ₹100 Crore VC fund, 100% SGST reimbursement, and incubator capital grants up to ₹50 Lakhs.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Karnataka Digital Economy Mission (KDEM), Department of Electronics, IT, BT and S&T, Government of Karnataka

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: The entity should meet the definition of Startup as per the Startup Policy and must be registered with Karnataka Startup Cell under KITS, Department of Electronics, IT, BT and S&T, GoK as a Startup. 1. The Startup should be incorporated as a private limited company (as defined in the Companies Act, 2013) or registered as a partnership firm (under section 59 of the Partnership Act, 1932) or a limited liability partnership (under the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008) in Karnataka. 2. Turnover of the entity for any of the financial years since incorporation/registration has not exceeded INR 100 Crores. 3. An entity shall be considered as a Startup up to 10 years from the date of its incorporation. 4. The Startup should be working towards innovation/ improvement of existing products, services and processes and should have the potential to generate employment/ create wealth.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Turnover exceeding INR 100 Crores in any financial year or incorporation beyond 10 years.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Entity must be working towards innovation/improvement of existing products, services, and processes with wealth/job generation potential.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Incorporated/registered in Karnataka; special incentives for Beyond Bengaluru (outside Bengaluru Urban District).
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Registered with Karnataka Startup Cell under KITS via www.missionstartupkarnataka.org

incentive_details.description: One-time grant of up to Rs. 50 lakhs released in tranches based on the lifecycle of the business plan to support early-stage startups.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: One-time Idea2PoC grant of up to ₹50 Lakhs released in milestone-based tranches.
incentive_details.application_process: Apply online at www.missionstartupkarnataka.org.

quantified_benefits.conditions: Released in tranches based on the life cycle of the business plan
quantified_benefits.description: One-time grant up to Rs. 50 lakhs
quantified_benefits.source_text: Funding will be in the form of Idea2PoC Grant-in-aid limited to a one-time grant of up to Rs. 50 lakhs to be released in tranches based on the life cycle of the business plan.

quantified_benefits.value_raw: Covering 220 countries and territories and 5,300 products

incentive_name: Advertisement and Publicity Assistance (Physical Exhibitions)

policy_goals: Capacity build MSMEs for entering the export market by facilitating their participation in international exhibitions, trade fairs, conferences, seminars, and buyer-seller meets abroad
Provide MSMEs with actionable market-intelligence and reimbursement of various costs involved in export of goods and services
Provide opportunities to MSMEs to continuously update themselves to meet the challenges emerging out of changes in technology, changes in demand, and emergence of new markets
Advance the position of MSMEs as emerging export players
policy_details.policy_summary: Sub-Component I of the International Cooperation Scheme provides financial assistance to facilitate the participation of MSME delegations in international exhibitions, trade fairs, and buyer-seller meets abroad (in physical or virtual mode), as well as organizing international conferences, summits, workshops, and seminars in India or virtually. Benefits cover space rent, airfare, freight charges, registration fees, duty allowances for office bearers, and event organizing charges, with enhanced ceilings for ZED certified units.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to 100% reimbursement for stall rent (up to ₹3 Lakh), economy airfare (up to ₹1.5 Lakh), and freight charges (up to ₹75,000), plus enhanced assistance for ZED certified MSMEs.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Government of India

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: Events can be organised by: a) Ministry of MSME and organizations under the Ministry; b) State/Central Government Organisations/Institutions; and c) Registered Industry/Enterprise Associations. Conditions: (i) The applicant organization should be suitably registered under the relevant Act (Companies Act, Societies Act, etc.) with the primary objective of promotion and development of MSMEs. (ii) The applicant organization should have regular audited accounts for the past 3 years. (iii) Events must be from the list of approved exhibitions/events/buyer-seller meets finalized by the Ministry of MSME in each financial year. (iv) Financial assistance to one applicant organisation would normally be restricted to three events in a financial year. (v) The quantum of assistance shall only be supplemental in nature to the contribution of organizer. (vi) Industry Associations/organizations are allowed to participate in a particular event continuously for 3 years; then eligible after a gap of 2 Years. (vii) Selection of participating units based on eligibility score card (Annexure C); in no case an MSME unit scoring less than 60 percent marks will be eligible. (viii) One MSME unit must not participate in more than 2 events in a financial year under the scheme. (ix) Minimum delegation size cannot be less than 10 MSME units. Valid Udyam Registration required.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Valid Udyam Registration Certificate for participating MSME units; Registration under Companies Act/Societies Act for organizing associations; PFMS registration; NGO Darpan portal ID (for NGOs)
special_category_benefits: Adequate representation and priority for SC/ST/Women/NER entrepreneurs
Additional incentives for ZED (Zero Defect Zero Effect) certified MSMEs under Bronze, Silver, and Gold categories
Priority to units that have not participated in such events earlier with Government grant

incentive_details.description: Financial assistance to the applicant organization for publicity and advertising connected to the delegation.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: Publicity assistance of up to ₹2.50 Lakh (delegations up to 14 units) or ₹5.00 Lakh (delegations of 15+ units).

quantified_benefits.description: Advertisement charges for delegation size up to 14 MSMEs
quantified_benefits.source_text: A maximum of Rs. 2.50 lakh or actual, whichever is less, for a delegation size up to 14 MSME units

quantified_benefits.description: Advertisement charges for delegation size of 15 or more MSMEs
quantified_benefits.source_text: Maximum of Rs. 5.00 Lakh or actual, whichever is lower subject to the condition that the minimum MSME Units must be 15 or more subject to production of all bills.

policy_name: Market Development Assistance of MSMEs (MDA)
incentive_name: Physical Mode Airfare Reimbursement

policy_goals: Capacity build MSMEs for entering the export market by facilitating their participation in international exhibitions, trade fairs, conferences, seminars, and buyer-seller meets abroad
Provide MSMEs with actionable market-intelligence and reimbursement of various costs involved in export of goods and services
Provide opportunities to MSMEs to continuously update themselves to meet the challenges emerging out of changes in technology, changes in demand, and emergence of new markets
Advance the position of MSMEs as emerging export players
policy_details.policy_summary: Sub-Component I of the International Cooperation Scheme provides financial assistance to facilitate the participation of MSME delegations in international exhibitions, trade fairs, and buyer-seller meets abroad (in physical or virtual mode), as well as organizing international conferences, summits, workshops, and seminars in India or virtually. Benefits cover space rent, airfare, freight charges, registration fees, duty allowances for office bearers, and event organizing charges, with enhanced ceilings for ZED certified units.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to 100% reimbursement for stall rent (up to ₹3 Lakh), economy airfare (up to ₹1.5 Lakh), and freight charges (up to ₹75,000), plus enhanced assistance for ZED certified MSMEs.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Government of India

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: Events can be organised by: a) Ministry of MSME and organizations under the Ministry; b) State/Central Government Organisations/Institutions; and c) Registered Industry/Enterprise Associations. Conditions: (i) The applicant organization should be suitably registered under the relevant Act (Companies Act, Societies Act, etc.) with the primary objective of promotion and development of MSMEs. (ii) The applicant organization should have regular audited accounts for the past 3 years. (iii) Events must be from the list of approved exhibitions/events/buyer-seller meets finalized by the Ministry of MSME in each financial year. (iv) Financial assistance to one applicant organisation would normally be restricted to three events in a financial year. (v) The quantum of assistance shall only be supplemental in nature to the contribution of organizer. (vi) Industry Associations/organizations are allowed to participate in a particular event continuously for 3 years; then eligible after a gap of 2 Years. (vii) Selection of participating units based on eligibility score card (Annexure C); in no case an MSME unit scoring less than 60 percent marks will be eligible. (viii) One MSME unit must not participate in more than 2 events in a financial year under the scheme. (ix) Minimum delegation size cannot be less than 10 MSME units. Valid Udyam Registration required.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Valid Udyam Registration Certificate for participating MSME units; Registration under Companies Act/Societies Act for organizing associations; PFMS registration; NGO Darpan portal ID (for NGOs)
special_category_benefits: Adequate representation and priority for SC/ST/Women/NER entrepreneurs
Additional incentives for ZED (Zero Defect Zero Effect) certified MSMEs under Bronze, Silver, and Gold categories
Priority to units that have not participated in such events earlier with Government grant

policy_name: Karnataka Aerospace and Defence Policy 2022-27
incentive_name: Exemption from Tax on Electricity Tariff for MSMEs

policy_goals: Attract investments to the tune of INR 45,000 crore (USD 6 Bn) in the Aerospace & Defence sector during the policy period of 5 years.
Create additional employment opportunities (direct and indirect) of 60,000 persons during the policy period of 5 years.
To develop Karnataka as the Aerospace & Defence manufacturing hub including MRO and space applications for both Indian market and exports.
To strengthen R&D infrastructure for achieving innovative and cutting-edge technologies.
To create enhanced facilitation mechanism for ease of doing business through industry friendly policy framework.
policy_details.policy_summary: The Karnataka Aerospace and Defence Policy 2022-27 aims to establish Karnataka as a globally competitive manufacturing, MRO, R&D, and space applications hub. It provides extensive fiscal incentives, including investment promotion subsidies, capital subsidies on land and plant/machinery, stamp duty exemptions, electricity duty waivers, power tariff subsidies, technology upgradation assistance, and testing infrastructure support for MSMEs as well as Large, Mega, Ultra Mega, and Super Mega enterprises in designated focus and general aerospace/defence sub-sectors across Zones 1, 2, and 3.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to 35% investment promotion subsidy for MSMEs, 20% capital subsidy on plant, machinery, and land for large focus sub-sectors, and 100% stamp duty exemption.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Commerce & Industries Department, Government of Karnataka

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: For the purpose of availing benefits under this policy, the eligible Aerospace & Defence units are defined as those which are designing, engineering, manufacturing, servicing, supplying such material / components / sub-assemblies, etc. fully or partially to the OEMs / Tier 1 / Tier 2/ Tier 3 companies of Aerospace / Defence majors including HAL, ISRO, all defence PSUs of Gol, all defence & security forces viz. Army, Navy, Air Force, Coast Guard, CRPF, etc. Construction of MRO Aircraft hangars will also be considered as Aerospace / Defence Industry. All the Industrial units which have got the AS9100 certification are considered as Aerospace / Defence related industrial / service units. The incentives and concessions as per this Policy shall be applicable only to all new and additional investments made on or after the launch of this policy vide a Government Order. The incentives and concessions under this policy will be available to all new investments both for establishment of new enterprises or for expansion, diversification, and modernization of existing industries. To be eligible for considering as expansion / diversification/ modernization, enterprises shall make an additional investment of at least 25% of the original investment of the existing unit and there shall be 25% increase in the production capacity. All new Enterprises shall create maximum possible additional employment opportunities and provide a minimum 75% of employment to the local people on an overall basis and 100% in case of Group D employees.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Incentives will be provided only to new investments or for capacity expansion. It will not be applicable for existing companies without expansion.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Minimum 75% of overall employment and 100% of Group D employment must be provided to local people, monitored by DIC for 5 years. For expansion/modernization, minimum 25% of original investment and 25% increase in production capacity is mandatory.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Categorized across Zone 1, Zone 2, and Zone 3 as per Karnataka Industrial Policy 2020-25 taluk classification.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: AS9100 certification or registered supplier/contractor to defence/aerospace OEMs/PSUs/forces, or approved under DPP with valid orders.

incentive_details.description: 100% exemption from tax on electricity tariff consumed by MSME units for a period ranging from 4 to 8 years.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: 100% electricity duty exemption for 4 to 8 years for MSME units.

quantified_benefits.source_text: Zone 1: 100% for 7 years; Zone 2: 100% for 6 years; Zone 3: 100% for 4 years

quantified_benefits.description: Electricity tariff tax exemption for Special Category
quantified_benefits.source_text: Zone 1: 100% for 8 years; Zone 2: 100% for 7 years; Zone 3: 100% for 5 years

policy_name: Karnataka Agribusiness and Food Processing Policy 2015
incentive_name: Concessional Registration Charges

policy_goals: Achieve the target of 10% of agro processing by 2020 and 25% by 2025 in Karnataka
Increase value addition to farm produce and reduce post-harvest wastage, thereby increasing the income of farmers
Maximize direct and indirect employment generation opportunities in rural and semi-urban areas
Create necessary supply chain infrastructure including transportation, warehouses, and cold storages across the agro processing sector
Increase the flow of investments across the supply chain from farm to market
Extend the supply chain and infrastructure opportunities into rural areas
policy_details.policy_summary: The Karnataka Agribusiness & Food Processing Policy 2015 was formulated to accelerate the growth of agribusiness and agro-processing, integrate supply chains, reduce post-harvest losses, and ensure remunerative prices for farmers. Classifying the entire State of Karnataka as a single unified zone for incentives, the policy covers activities spanning agricultural, horticultural, floricultural, spices, medicinal/aromatic plants, fisheries, meat, poultry, dairy, and biotechnology-based agro projects. Major benefits include investment promotion subsidies of up to 35% (max Rs. 65 Lakhs for MSMEs), 100% stamp duty exemption, concessional registration charges, 100% land conversion fee reimbursement, multi-year entry tax exemptions, effluent treatment plant capital subsidies up to Rs. 200 Lakhs, 6% interest subsidy for micro enterprises, 100% electricity tax exemption for 8 years, VAT reimbursement up to 80% (MSME: 75%), technology adoption subsidies, and a 10-year market fee exemption for new processing industries.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to 35% investment subsidy (capped at ₹65 Lakhs for MSMEs), 100% stamp duty exemption, 100% electricity tax exemption for 8 years, and 10-year market fee exemption across Karnataka.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Agriculture Department, Government of Karnataka
special_focus_areas: Group Crop Insurance for Contract Farming

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: Agro processing units, agribusiness, and food processing enterprises covering warehousing, silos, cold storage logistics related to agribusiness, export, processing, handling, storage of agricultural, horticultural, floriculture, spices, medicinal & aromatic plants, fish, meat, poultry, dairy, organic produce, research for varietal development, bio-technology, bio-informatics, food testing laboratories, quality certifications in entire value chain, tissue culture laboratories, seed processing units, irradiation units, food-grade packaging material units and preservatives, horticulture hub, food parks, sea food parks and spice park. Classified as MSMEs (Micro: up to Rs.25 Lakhs investment in plant & machinery or up to Rs.10 Lakhs in equipment; Small: Rs.25 Lakhs to Rs.500 Lakhs in plant & machinery or Rs.10 Lakhs to Rs.200 Lakhs in equipment; Medium: Rs.500 Lakhs to Rs.1000 Lakhs in plant & machinery or Rs.200 Lakhs to Rs.500 Lakhs in equipment), Category 'A' Enterprises (Rs.10 Crores to Rs.75 Crores in fixed assets), Category 'B' Enterprises (Rs.75 Crores to Rs.150 Crores in fixed assets), Category 'C' Enterprises (above Rs.150 Crores in fixed assets), and Category 'D' Enterprises (first two agro food processing enterprises in a taluka providing minimum direct employment of 100 persons with minimum investment of Rs.150 Crores). The list of ineligible activities is specified under Annexure-IV.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Breweries and Distilleries of all types excluding Winery; Masala making without Cold Process Grinding, powder of Chilly, Turmeric, Masala, Spices, Curry, Sambar, Papad etc., except those having FSSAI certification; Preparation of Sweetmeat and Salted Snacks, Mixture, Bhujia; Khandasari making enterprises; Jaggery making enterprises except those having FSSAI Certification; Mineral Water and aerated Soft Drinks, Alcoholic Beverages; Tea Blending / Mixing Units, Coffee Roasting & Grinding units having installed capacity of less than 2 TPD; Production of Popcorn, Ice Block, Production of Ice Candy and Ice Fruits etc. Ice-cream manufacturing without FSSAI certification; Units connected with Raw-Tobacco and Tobacco Based Products; Fertilizer Mixing Units; Poultry excluding Hatcheries.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Applicable across the entire state of Karnataka, declared as a single unified zone.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: FSSAI certification required for certain processed foods (spices/masalas, jaggery, ice-cream) to qualify for exemptions/incentives. Units intended to avail Electricity Tax Exemption require necessary certificate from Department of Commerce and Industries.

incentive_details.description: Registration charges capped at a concessional rate of Rs. 0.50 per Rs. 1000 for loan documents, lease deeds, lease-cum-sale deeds, and sale deeds executed by MSME, Category A, B, and C enterprises.

quantified_benefits.source_text: For all loan documents, lease deeds and sale deeds, the registration charges shall be at a concessional rate @ Rs.0.50 per Rs.1000 irrespective of promoter classification for MSME, Category ‘A’, ‘B’ & ‘C’ enterprises.
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: MSME, Category A, B and C enterprises

policy_name: Karnataka Agribusiness and Food Processing Policy 2015
incentive_name: Subsidy for Setting Up Effluent Treatment Plant (ETP)

policy_goals: Achieve the target of 10% of agro processing by 2020 and 25% by 2025 in Karnataka
Increase value addition to farm produce and reduce post-harvest wastage, thereby increasing the income of farmers
Maximize direct and indirect employment generation opportunities in rural and semi-urban areas
Create necessary supply chain infrastructure including transportation, warehouses, and cold storages across the agro processing sector
Increase the flow of investments across the supply chain from farm to market
Extend the supply chain and infrastructure opportunities into rural areas
policy_details.policy_summary: The Karnataka Agribusiness & Food Processing Policy 2015 was formulated to accelerate the growth of agribusiness and agro-processing, integrate supply chains, reduce post-harvest losses, and ensure remunerative prices for farmers. Classifying the entire State of Karnataka as a single unified zone for incentives, the policy covers activities spanning agricultural, horticultural, floricultural, spices, medicinal/aromatic plants, fisheries, meat, poultry, dairy, and biotechnology-based agro projects. Major benefits include investment promotion subsidies of up to 35% (max Rs. 65 Lakhs for MSMEs), 100% stamp duty exemption, concessional registration charges, 100% land conversion fee reimbursement, multi-year entry tax exemptions, effluent treatment plant capital subsidies up to Rs. 200 Lakhs, 6% interest subsidy for micro enterprises, 100% electricity tax exemption for 8 years, VAT reimbursement up to 80% (MSME: 75%), technology adoption subsidies, and a 10-year market fee exemption for new processing industries.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to 35% investment subsidy (capped at ₹65 Lakhs for MSMEs), 100% stamp duty exemption, 100% electricity tax exemption for 8 years, and 10-year market fee exemption across Karnataka.

policy_name: Krishi Navodyama Scheme (ಕೃಷಿ ನವೋದ್ಯಮ ಯೋಜನೆ)
incentive_name: Financial Assistance for New Agri-Startups at Incubation Stage

policy_goals: Promote innovation, value addition, and modern marketing in the agriculture sector
Encourage rural youth, agricultural graduates, and progressive farmers to establish agri-startups and generate employment
Commercialize novel technologies and innovations developed in agricultural universities and research institutes
Facilitate agricultural produce processing, export infrastructure usage, international certifications, quality testing, and market linkages for Karnataka agri-exporters
policy_details.policy_summary: Krishi Navodyama is a flagship scheme formulated under paragraph 40 of the Karnataka State Budget 2023-24 with an outlay of ₹10.00 crore under the Watershed Development Department / Agriculture Department. It supports innovative agricultural enterprises, value addition, and agri-marketing technologies. The scheme provides a 50% back-ended capital subsidy through bank loans for new agri-startups at the incubation stage (₹5.00 to ₹20.00 lakhs) and for the scaling up or expansion of established startups (₹20.00 to ₹50.00 lakhs). It also establishes a dedicated Mentoring and Acceleration Programme (MAP) with specialized training via premier scientific institutions like UAS, ICAR, CFTRI, CSIR, and C-CAMP.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to 50% back-ended capital subsidy ranging from ₹5 lakhs to ₹50 lakhs for new and scaling agri-startups in Karnataka.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Department of Agriculture, Government of Karnataka & Karnataka State Agricultural Produce Processing and Export Corporation Limited (KAPPEC)

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: Agri-Startup Registration: The applicant Agri-Startup must be compulsorily registered in Karnataka as a Private Limited Company (under Companies Act, 2013), Partnership Firm (under section 59 of the Partnership Act, 1932), or Limited Liability Partnership (under the LLP Act, 2008). Turnover: Annual turnover should not exceed ₹5.00 crore in any financial year since incorporation. Age of Startup: Must not have completed more than 3 years from the date of registration. Scope of Work: The Agri-Startup must belong to the agriculture sector, focusing on novel innovations, useful products, and services with employment generation potential. Priority will be given to farmer-led startups that encourage farmers to transition into entrepreneurs via allied occupations. Minimum qualifying score: Startups must secure at least 60 marks out of 100 in the technical evaluation matrix (covering market potential, feasibility, impact, innovation/USP, team competence, fund utilization plan, and presentation).
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Agri-startups with turnover exceeding ₹5.00 crore in any year, enterprises older than 3 years from registration, entities not registered in Karnataka under the specified Acts, or projects seeking duplicate subsidies already availed from other government schemes/departments.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Must achieve at least 60 out of 100 marks in Form-1 evaluation by District Technical Committee and undergo physical site verification. Must obtain bank loan sanction as subsidy is back-ended.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Must be compulsorily registered and operating within the state of Karnataka.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Private Limited Company (Companies Act, 2013), Partnership Firm (Section 59, Partnership Act 1932), or LLP (LLP Act 2008) registered in Karnataka.
special_category_benefits: Priority to progressive farmers and farmer-led startups transitioning to entrepreneurship

incentive_details.benefit_headline: 50% subsidy from ₹5.00 lakhs to ₹20.00 lakhs for incubation stage agri-startups via bank loan.
incentive_details.application_process: Applications invited online at district level through the K-kisan webpage developed by the Department of Agriculture. Scrutinized by District Technical Committee (Form-1 evaluation, min 60 marks required), recommended by District Implementation Committee, and approved by State Level Approval Committee.

quantified_benefits.conditions: Subject to minimum ₹5.00 lakh and maximum ₹20.00 lakh, routed through bank loan against predefined milestone achievements.
quantified_benefits.description: Back-ended capital subsidy on approved project report cost for new agri-startups at incubation stage
quantified_benefits.source_text: ಕೃಷಿ ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರದಲ್ಲಿ ನೂತನ ಪರಿಕಲ್ಪನೆಯೊಂದಿಗೆ ಆರಂಭಿಸುವ ಹೊಸ ಕೃಷಿ ನವೋದ್ಯಮಗಳಿಗೆ ಅನುಮೋದಿತ ಯೋಜನಾ ವರದಿಯ ಶೇಕಡ 50 ರಷ್ಟು ಸಹಾಯಧನವನ್ನು (ಕನಿಷ್ಠ-ರೂ. 5.00 ಲಕ್ಷದಿಂದ ಗರಿಷ್ಠರೂ. 20 ಲಕ್ಷಗಳವರೆಗೆ) ಬ್ಯಾಂಕ್ ಸಾಲದ ಮುಖಾಂತರ (Backended subsidy) ನೀಡಲಾಗುವುದು.

incentive_details.incentive_specific_eligibility: Agri-startups at incubation stage working on POC, prototype, or product trials with less than 3 years from registration.

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: Only registered KAVGC companies can apply for the subsidies/incentives/grants available under this policy. Location: The company or entity should be registered in Karnataka under the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishment Act, 1961. Employment: Company employs at least 50% of its total workforce in Karnataka, which will not include contract employees. If the startup/company is already availing benefits for a particular type of incentive from other policies of the Government of Karnataka, the startup/company cannot apply for a similar benefit under the AVGC Policy. A first-time applicant needs to apply for registration as a KAVGC company by completing the KAVGC registration form with a one-time charge of INR 10,000.

policy_goals: Foster sustained growth, innovation, and leadership in Karnataka's Animation, Visual Effects, Gaming, Comics, and Extended Reality (AVGC-XR) sector
Support early-stage startups and established AVGC-XR entities through comprehensive financial incentives, infrastructure, and production grants
Build a future-ready talent ecosystem through accredited skill development, holistic curriculum updates, vocational training, and finishing schools

Establish world-class infrastructure including Centres of Excellence (CoE 2.0), AVGC-XR Park (SEZ cum tourism center), Digital Art Centers (DACs 2.0), and dedicated Technology Business Incubators (TBIs)
Propel Karnataka companies into global markets via international production support, trade expo access, Global Innovation Alliance (GIA) partnerships, and an AVGC-XR IP Marketplace
Provide venture capital assistance via KITVEN Fund-4 (AVGC) with an allocated corpus of ₹20 crore
policy_details.policy_summary: The Operational Guidelines for the Karnataka AVGC-XR Policy 3.0 (2024-29) provide implementation rules, eligibility criteria, and sanctioning procedures for registered KAVGC companies operating in Animation, Visual Effects, Gaming, Comics, and Extended Reality within Karnataka. Administered by the Karnataka Innovation and Technology Society (KITS), the policy offers financial support spanning skill development course fee reimbursement (up to 50%, cap ₹7.5 lakhs), EPF/ESI reimbursement for new jobs (₹3,000/employee/month, cap ₹12 lakhs), early-stage startup assistance (marketing, office leasing, server rental, and compliance setup costs), infrastructure subsidies (20% on IT hardware up to ₹20 lakhs and rentals up to ₹5 lakhs), IP filing assistance (50% up to ₹20 lakhs international / ₹5 lakhs domestic), production grants across animation films, series, VR/AR/VFX, mobile and non-mobile games, and international co-productions (reimbursements up to ₹1 crore), quality assurance certification reimbursement (30% up to ₹5 lakhs), and international market access/trade expo participation (40% up to ₹5 lakhs per year, total ₹15 lakhs). It also covers institutional setups like KITVEN Fund-4 (₹20 crore corpus), Technology Business Incubators (up to ₹10 crore per TBI), and specialized testing facilities.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Comprehensive financial support including production grants up to ₹1 crore, 50% IP filing aid up to ₹20 lakhs, 20% IT infrastructure capital subsidy up to ₹20 lakhs, and early-stage startup expense reimbursements.

special_focus_areas: Emerging Tech in Fine Arts & Digital Art Centers (DACs 2.0)
Technology Business Incubators in Tier-2/3 Clusters (Mangalore, Mysore, Hubli-Dharwad)

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: Only registered KAVGC companies can apply for the subsidies/incentives/grants available under this policy. A first-time applicant needs to apply for registration as a KAVGC company by completing the KAVGC registration form. There is a one-time charge of INR 10,000 for KAVGC registration that should be paid as a demand draft in favor of 'Managing Director, KITS'. If the company has previously registered as a Karnataka company, there is no charge. Location: The company or entity should be registered in Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishment Act, 1961. Employment: Company employs at least 50% of its total workforce in Karnataka, which will not include contract employees. If the startup/company is already availing benefits for a particular type of incentive from other policies of the Government of Karnataka, the startup/company cannot apply for a similar benefit under the AVGC Policy.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Gambling software applications are strictly excluded. Companies that have already availed similar incentives from other policies of the Government of Karnataka, or specific skills council incentives for the same training, are not eligible for duplicate benefits.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Must hold valid KAVGC Registration issued by KITS. Physical verification may be conducted by authorized officials on-site before sanction.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Entity must be registered under the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishment Act, 1961 and employ at least 50% of its total permanent workforce within Karnataka.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Registration under Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishment Act, 1961; KAVGC Registration Certificate from KITS (or Karnataka IT-BT registration certificate).

incentive_details.description: Reimbursement of legal and compliance expenses incurred during setup including incorporation fees, audit fees, AVGC-XR industry specific regulations, contract drafting, and GDPR compliance costs.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: 50% reimbursement of legal and compliance setup costs up to ₹2,00,000.
incentive_details.application_process: Submit Application Form 22.1.3 with legal bills, incorporation receipts, and auditor verification.

quantified_benefits.conditions: Costs incurred during setup period; company <= 2 years old; must have MVP; < 15 full-time staff.
quantified_benefits.description: Reimbursement of legal and regulatory compliance costs during company setup
quantified_benefits.source_text: Up to 50% reimbursement on legal and compliance costs incurred during company setup, capped at INR 2,00,000, per company during the policy period.
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: Startups not older than 2 years with MVP and fewer than 15 full-time employees

incentive_details.incentive_specific_eligibility: Startups <= 2 years old, working prototype or MVP, < 15 full-time employees.

incentive_name: Infrastructure Support - IT Hardware Infrastructure

policy_goals: Foster sustained growth, innovation, and leadership in Karnataka's Animation, Visual Effects, Gaming, Comics, and Extended Reality (AVGC-XR) sector
Support early-stage startups and established AVGC-XR entities through comprehensive financial incentives, infrastructure, and production grants
Build a future-ready talent ecosystem through accredited skill development, holistic curriculum updates, vocational training, and finishing schools

Establish world-class infrastructure including Centres of Excellence (CoE 2.0), AVGC-XR Park (SEZ cum tourism center), Digital Art Centers (DACs 2.0), and dedicated Technology Business Incubators (TBIs)
Propel Karnataka companies into global markets via international production support, trade expo access, Global Innovation Alliance (GIA) partnerships, and an AVGC-XR IP Marketplace
Provide venture capital assistance via KITVEN Fund-4 (AVGC) with an allocated corpus of ₹20 crore
policy_details.policy_summary: The Operational Guidelines for the Karnataka AVGC-XR Policy 3.0 (2024-29) provide implementation rules, eligibility criteria, and sanctioning procedures for registered KAVGC companies operating in Animation, Visual Effects, Gaming, Comics, and Extended Reality within Karnataka. Administered by the Karnataka Innovation and Technology Society (KITS), the policy offers financial support spanning skill development course fee reimbursement (up to 50%, cap ₹7.5 lakhs), EPF/ESI reimbursement for new jobs (₹3,000/employee/month, cap ₹12 lakhs), early-stage startup assistance (marketing, office leasing, server rental, and compliance setup costs), infrastructure subsidies (20% on IT hardware up to ₹20 lakhs and rentals up to ₹5 lakhs), IP filing assistance (50% up to ₹20 lakhs international / ₹5 lakhs domestic), production grants across animation films, series, VR/AR/VFX, mobile and non-mobile games, and international co-productions (reimbursements up to ₹1 crore), quality assurance certification reimbursement (30% up to ₹5 lakhs), and international market access/trade expo participation (40% up to ₹5 lakhs per year, total ₹15 lakhs). It also covers institutional setups like KITVEN Fund-4 (₹20 crore corpus), Technology Business Incubators (up to ₹10 crore per TBI), and specialized testing facilities.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Comprehensive financial support including production grants up to ₹1 crore, 50% IP filing aid up to ₹20 lakhs, 20% IT infrastructure capital subsidy up to ₹20 lakhs, and early-stage startup expense reimbursements.

special_focus_areas: Emerging Tech in Fine Arts & Digital Art Centers (DACs 2.0)
Technology Business Incubators in Tier-2/3 Clusters (Mangalore, Mysore, Hubli-Dharwad)

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: Only registered KAVGC companies can apply for the subsidies/incentives/grants available under this policy. A first-time applicant needs to apply for registration as a KAVGC company by completing the KAVGC registration form. There is a one-time charge of INR 10,000 for KAVGC registration that should be paid as a demand draft in favor of 'Managing Director, KITS'. If the company has previously registered as a Karnataka company, there is no charge. Location: The company or entity should be registered in Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishment Act, 1961. Employment: Company employs at least 50% of its total workforce in Karnataka, which will not include contract employees. If the startup/company is already availing benefits for a particular type of incentive from other policies of the Government of Karnataka, the startup/company cannot apply for a similar benefit under the AVGC Policy.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Gambling software applications are strictly excluded. Companies that have already availed similar incentives from other policies of the Government of Karnataka, or specific skills council incentives for the same training, are not eligible for duplicate benefits.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Must hold valid KAVGC Registration issued by KITS. Physical verification may be conducted by authorized officials on-site before sanction.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Entity must be registered under the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishment Act, 1961 and employ at least 50% of its total permanent workforce within Karnataka.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Registration under Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishment Act, 1961; KAVGC Registration Certificate from KITS (or Karnataka IT-BT registration certificate).

incentive_details.description: Subsidy on purchases of IT hardware equipment applicable for an AVGC-XR company from OEMs or authorized suppliers. Software and licenses, refurbished, and certified pre-owned equipment are excluded.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: Up to 20% subsidy on IT hardware purchases capped at ₹20 lakhs, allowed up to 5 sanctions per company.
incentive_details.application_process: Submit Application Form for Infrastructure (Annexure 22.1.4) with valid GST invoices, OEM authorization proofs, declaration of equipment status, and statutory declaration.

quantified_benefits.conditions: Must purchase from OEMs and authorized suppliers/resellers/distributors; equipment must not be refurbished or pre-owned; valid GST invoice required; leasing and subscriptions not eligible; maximum 5 sanctions per company.
quantified_benefits.description: Reimbursement on one-time purchase of new IT hardware equipment
quantified_benefits.source_text: Up to 20% of the cost incurred, capped at INR 20 Lakhs limited to up to 5 sanction per company during the policy period. Purchases of IT Hardware equipment applicable for an AVGC-XR company. Software and licenses are not eligible.
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: Existing or newly established registered KAVGC companies

incentive_details.incentive_specific_eligibility: KAVGC companies operating in Animation, Visual Effects, Gaming, and Comics sectors.

quantified_benefits.applicable_to: KAVGC companies with at least one year of operation

incentive_details.incentive_specific_eligibility: Minimum 1 year of operational track record; must hold a portfolio of work to showcase and an official invitation.
