incentive_details.description: Reimbursement of costs incurred for IP filing (patent, trademark, copyright) and legal consultation for domestic and international intellectual property.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: Up to 50% reimbursement of IP filing and legal consultation costs capped at ₹20 lakhs for international IP and ₹5 lakhs for domestic IP.
incentive_details.application_process: Submit Application Form for IP Creation and Protection (Annexure 22.1.5) with patent filing receipt, grant certificate (if granted), expense invoices, and bank statements.

quantified_benefits.conditions: 50% released after filing; remaining 50% released after grant of patent. Must provide proof of original work and legal consultation.
quantified_benefits.description: Reimbursement of IP filing and legal consultation for International IP
quantified_benefits.source_text: Up to 50% of the costs for IP filing and legal consultation, capped at INR 20 Lakhs for International Intellectual Property and INR 5 Lakhs for Domestic Intellectual Property, during the policy period. The remaining 50% would be released after the patent is granted.

quantified_benefits.conditions: 50% released upon filing; 50% upon grant.
quantified_benefits.description: Reimbursement of IP filing and legal consultation for Domestic IP
quantified_benefits.source_text: Up to 50% of the costs for IP filing and legal consultation, capped at INR 20 Lakhs for International Intellectual Property and INR 5 Lakhs for Domestic Intellectual Property, during the policy period. Intellectual Property Rights filed in India will qualify for Domestic IP incentive claim.
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: Domestic Intellectual Property filings in India

incentive_details.incentive_specific_eligibility: KAVGC companies owning original creations and actively engaging or planning to file for copyright, trademark, or patent.

It also covers institutional setups like KITVEN Fund-4 (₹20 crore corpus), Technology Business Incubators (up to ₹10 crore per TBI), and specialized testing facilities.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Comprehensive financial support including production grants up to ₹1 crore, 50% IP filing aid up to ₹20 lakhs, 20% IT infrastructure capital subsidy up to ₹20 lakhs, and early-stage startup expense reimbursements.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Department of Electronics, Information Technology, Biotechnology and Science & Technology, Government of Karnataka / Karnataka Innovation and Technology Society (KITS)
special_focus_areas: Emerging Tech in Fine Arts & Digital Art Centers (DACs 2.0)
Technology Business Incubators in Tier-2/3 Clusters (Mangalore, Mysore, Hubli-Dharwad)

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: Only registered KAVGC companies can apply for the subsidies/incentives/grants available under this policy. A first-time applicant needs to apply for registration as a KAVGC company by completing the KAVGC registration form. There is a one-time charge of INR 10,000 for KAVGC registration that should be paid as a demand draft in favor of 'Managing Director, KITS'. If the company has previously registered as a Karnataka company, there is no charge. Location: The company or entity should be registered in Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishment Act, 1961. Employment: Company employs at least 50% of its total workforce in Karnataka, which will not include contract employees. If the startup/company is already availing benefits for a particular type of incentive from other policies of the Government of Karnataka, the startup/company cannot apply for a similar benefit under the AVGC Policy.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Gambling software applications are strictly excluded. Companies that have already availed similar incentives from other policies of the Government of Karnataka, or specific skills council incentives for the same training, are not eligible for duplicate benefits.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Must hold valid KAVGC Registration issued by KITS. Physical verification may be conducted by authorized officials on-site before sanction.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Entity must be registered under the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishment Act, 1961 and employ at least 50% of its total permanent workforce within Karnataka.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Registration under Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishment Act, 1961; KAVGC Registration Certificate from KITS (or Karnataka IT-BT registration certificate).

incentive_details.description: Reimbursement of up to 30% of costs incurred for obtaining national or international quality certifications (e.g., ISO 9001:2015, ISO/IEC 27001:2013, CMMI, SEI-CMMI, NASSCOM, Six Sigma, PEGI, WCAG, ESRB, Unreal/Unity Engine).

quantified_benefits.conditions: Company must undergo an audit; detailed quality measures report and staff training evidence required; up to 3 sanctions per company.
quantified_benefits.description: Reimbursement of audit, application, and licensing fees for quality certifications
quantified_benefits.source_text: Reimbursement of up to 30% of the costs incurred for obtaining certifications, capped at INR 5 lakhs per company; limited to 3 sanction per company during the policy period.
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: KAVGC companies obtaining recognized national/international certifications

incentive_details.incentive_specific_eligibility: KAVGC companies adhering to recognized international or national quality standards.

policy_name: Karnataka Biotechnology Policy 2024-2029 - Fiscal Incentives and Concessions
incentive_name: Capital Cost Reimbursement for Biotechnology Incubation/Acceleration Centre

policy_goals: Strengthen educational institutions for skilling in biotechnology from employability and entrepreneurship perspectives
Streamline biotech and related regulations to ease business establishment, operational clarity, and promote investments
Support biomanufacturing for products aligning with health, climate, and energy goals, enhancing food security and bioeconomy
Support the biotech startup and MSME ecosystem with incubation, seed funding, acceleration, grow-out facilities, and preferential procurement
Enable preferential government procurement norms for Made-in-Karnataka Biotech Products & Services and facilitate sandbox mechanisms for rare diseases and health-tech

Support R&D and commercialization efforts in emerging biotechnology areas (Bio-Agri, Bio-Industrial, Marine Biotech, Synthetic Biology, MedTech, AI/ML, AMR, Multi-omics, Cell & Gene Therapy, Space Biotech)
Facilitate the establishment and growth of at least 300 Biotechnology companies, including 50 particularly innovative or high-profile entities
Create 30,000 new, high-quality jobs in the biotech sector by 2029 and partner with 200+ institutions to train at least 20,000 individuals
policy_details.policy_summary: The Karnataka Biotechnology Policy 2024-2029 aims to elevate Karnataka's bioeconomy to $100 billion by 2030 by driving 'Focused Transformation through Impactful Implementation'. The policy focuses on six key pillars: Skill Development for a future-ready workforce, Streamlining Regulatory Frameworks, Specific Support to Bio-Manufacturing, Scaling up Biotech Startup & MSME Ecosystem, Preferential Procurement & Regulatory Sandbox, and Fiscal Incentives & Concessions. The fiscal framework provides targeted support across Startups, MSMEs, and Large Scale Industries, covering SGST reimbursement, patent filing costs, international marketing, quality certification, prototyping expenses, interest subsidies, land conversion reimbursements, stamp duty exemptions, STP setup, rainwater harvesting, land cost subsidies, and production-linked incentives (PLI).
policy_details.benefit_headline: Comprehensive fiscal package offering up to 100% SGST reimbursement, 100% stamp duty exemption, 6% interest subsidy, up to ₹1 crore capital grants, and 2.25% turnover-based PLI for biotechnology entities in Karnataka.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Department of Electronics, Information Technology, Biotechnology and Science & Technology, Government of Karnataka
special_focus_areas: Cell and Gene Therapies for Rare Diseases

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: Applicant should be registered as a Karnataka based biotech company under the Karnataka Biotechnology policy 2024-2029. Applicant should produce KYC (PAN, AADHAAR, UDYOG AADHAAR, GST certificate, Bank letter with RTGS details, Cancelled Cheque). For a Startup: Incorporated as Pvt Ltd, registered Partnership, or LLP in Karnataka; working towards innovation/improvement of existing products, services and processes with potential to generate employment or wealth; turnover for any FY since incorporation should not have exceeded ₹100 crores; tenure up to 10 years from incorporation; not formed by demerger, splitting, or reconstitution; not a Section 8 company/trust/society, PPP firm, franchisee, or subsidiary of a non-startup firm. For an MSME: Founded and based in Karnataka, registered on Udyam portal / RoC / Shops & Commercial Establishment Act, employing at least 50% of its total workforce in Karnataka (excluding contract staff), meeting MSMED Act 2006 investment/turnover criteria. For Large Industry: Founded and based in Karnataka, registered under RoC / Factories Act / Shops & Commercial Establishment Act, employing at least 50% of workforce in Karnataka, with investment in fixed assets up to ₹250 crore (investments above ₹250 crore assessed case-to-case). Mandatory to have obtained SLSWCC/SHLCC approval for New and Diversification/Expansion units.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: A company should not have been formed by demerger or reconstitution of a business already in existence; not a Section 8 company or Trust/Association/Society; not a Public-private partnership company/firm; not a franchisee of an existing business or promoted/sponsored/related to an industrial group in the state; not a subsidiary of a firm in the state other than the startup itself.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Must employ at least 50% of total workforce in Karnataka (excluding contract labor) for MSMEs and Large Enterprises. Large enterprises availing incentives must adhere to minimum local employment norms (Kannadigas) as per the Dr. Sarojini Mahishi Report (not less than 70% overall and 100% in Group D).
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Certain incentives require registration outside Bengaluru Urban district or outside Bengaluru Urban and Bengaluru Rural districts; Land Cost and PLI incentives are classified based on Zones 1, 2, and 3 under the Karnataka Industrial Policy 2020-25.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Registration with KITS under Karnataka Biotechnology Policy 2024-2029; Udyam Registration for MSMEs; RoC/Partnership/LLP registration; SLSWCC/SHLCC approval for new or expansion projects.
special_category_benefits: Special category entrepreneurs (SC/ST/Minority/Women) receive 75% land conversion reimbursement in Zone 3 compared to Nil for General

incentive_details.description: One-time capital grant of 50% or up to ₹1 Crore on Fixed Cost Investment (FCI / VFA, excluding land & building) for establishing new incubation/acceleration centres outside Bengaluru Urban and Rural districts. For upgradation/expansion, 50% grant up to ₹50 Lakhs.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: Up to 50% capital grant (capped at ₹1 Crore for new, ₹50 Lakhs for expansion) for biotech incubators outside Bengaluru Urban/Rural.
incentive_details.application_process: Submit prescribed application form along with DPR, plant and machinery invoices, and turnover certificate.

quantified_benefits.conditions: Excludes land and building; paid only once.
quantified_benefits.description: One-time capital grant for setting up new Biotechnology Incubation/Acceleration centre
quantified_benefits.source_text: For outside Bengaluru urban and Bengaluru rural district Biotechnology Incubation /Acceleration centre - A one-time capital grant of maximum 50% or ₹ 1 Crore (whichever is less) for Fixed Cost Investment (FCI) excluding land & building.
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: New incubation/acceleration centres outside Bengaluru Urban and Rural

quantified_benefits.conditions: Excludes land and building; paid only once.
quantified_benefits.description: One-time capital grant for Upgradation/Expansion of existing Incubation/Acceleration centre
quantified_benefits.source_text: Support for Upgradation/Expansion a one-time capital grant of 50% FCI (excluding land and building) with ceiling of ₹ 50 Lakhs
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: Expansion/upgradation of incubation/acceleration centres outside Bengaluru Urban and Rural

incentive_details.incentive_specific_eligibility: Incubators with minimum 2,500 sq. ft. area and at least 20 seats located outside Bengaluru Urban and Rural districts.

incentive_details.benefit_headline: 6% interest subsidy on term loans up to ₹1 Crore for up to 8 years for new large biotech investments.
incentive_details.application_process: Submit Annexure 14 with bank term loan sanction letter, bank release certificate (Annexure 15), and first sale invoice.

quantified_benefits.conditions: Applicable only to new investments; loans up to ₹1 Crore (or ₹5 Crore under section 5.3.3.4) with tenure <= 8 years; enterprise must not have defaulted.
quantified_benefits.description: 6% interest subsidy on term loan for new large biotech investments

incentive_details.incentive_specific_eligibility: New large-scale biotechnology enterprises.

The fiscal framework provides targeted support across Startups, MSMEs, and Large Scale Industries, covering SGST reimbursement, patent filing costs, international marketing, quality certification, prototyping expenses, interest subsidies, land conversion reimbursements, stamp duty exemptions, STP setup, rainwater harvesting, land cost subsidies, and production-linked incentives (PLI).
policy_details.benefit_headline: Comprehensive fiscal package offering up to 100% SGST reimbursement, 100% stamp duty exemption, 6% interest subsidy, up to ₹1 crore capital grants, and 2.25% turnover-based PLI for biotechnology entities in Karnataka.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Department of Electronics, Information Technology, Biotechnology and Science & Technology, Government of Karnataka
special_focus_areas: Cell and Gene Therapies for Rare Diseases

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: Applicant should be registered as a Karnataka based biotech company under the Karnataka Biotechnology policy 2024-2029. Applicant should produce KYC (PAN, AADHAAR, UDYOG AADHAAR, GST certificate, Bank letter with RTGS details, Cancelled Cheque). For a Startup: Incorporated as Pvt Ltd, registered Partnership, or LLP in Karnataka; working towards innovation/improvement of existing products, services and processes with potential to generate employment or wealth; turnover for any FY since incorporation should not have exceeded ₹100 crores; tenure up to 10 years from incorporation; not formed by demerger, splitting, or reconstitution; not a Section 8 company/trust/society, PPP firm, franchisee, or subsidiary of a non-startup firm. For an MSME: Founded and based in Karnataka, registered on Udyam portal / RoC / Shops & Commercial Establishment Act, employing at least 50% of its total workforce in Karnataka (excluding contract staff), meeting MSMED Act 2006 investment/turnover criteria. For Large Industry: Founded and based in Karnataka, registered under RoC / Factories Act / Shops & Commercial Establishment Act, employing at least 50% of workforce in Karnataka, with investment in fixed assets up to ₹250 crore (investments above ₹250 crore assessed case-to-case). Mandatory to have obtained SLSWCC/SHLCC approval for New and Diversification/Expansion units.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: A company should not have been formed by demerger or reconstitution of a business already in existence; not a Section 8 company or Trust/Association/Society; not a Public-private partnership company/firm; not a franchisee of an existing business or promoted/sponsored/related to an industrial group in the state; not a subsidiary of a firm in the state other than the startup itself.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Must employ at least 50% of total workforce in Karnataka (excluding contract labor) for MSMEs and Large Enterprises. Large enterprises availing incentives must adhere to minimum local employment norms (Kannadigas) as per the Dr. Sarojini Mahishi Report (not less than 70% overall and 100% in Group D).
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Certain incentives require registration outside Bengaluru Urban district or outside Bengaluru Urban and Bengaluru Rural districts; Land Cost and PLI incentives are classified based on Zones 1, 2, and 3 under the Karnataka Industrial Policy 2020-25.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Registration with KITS under Karnataka Biotechnology Policy 2024-2029; Udyam Registration for MSMEs; RoC/Partnership/LLP registration; SLSWCC/SHLCC approval for new or expansion projects.
special_category_benefits: Special category entrepreneurs (SC/ST/Minority/Women) receive 75% land conversion reimbursement in Zone 3 compared to Nil for General

incentive_details.description: Interest subsidy of up to 6% per annum on term loans taken from scheduled banks or state financial institutions (e.g. KSFC) during the policy period for loans up to ₹50 Lakhs (or up to ₹5 Crore per OPG section 5.2.5.4) for up to 5-8 years, applicable strictly to new investments.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: 6% interest subsidy on term loans up to ₹50 Lakhs / ₹5 Crore for up to 8 years for new biotech investments.
incentive_details.application_process: Submit Annexure 14, bank sanction letter, loan disbursement certificate (Annexure 15), and first sale invoice.

quantified_benefits.cap_raw: loan upto ₹ 50 Lakhs (or up to ₹ 5 Crore as per OPG 5.2.5.4)
quantified_benefits.conditions: Strictly for new investments (not expansion); tenure up to 8 years; enterprise must not have defaulted on loan repayments; claimed only after commercial production.
quantified_benefits.description: Interest subsidy on term loans for new biotech investment
quantified_benefits.source_text: Interest subsidy of 6% for loan upto ₹ 50 Lakhs not exceeding 8 years, only in case of new investment and not expansion.

incentive_details.incentive_specific_eligibility: Term loans sanctioned by scheduled commercial banks or KSFC for new biotech units.

policy_name: Karnataka Clean Mobility Policy 2025-2030
incentive_name: Capital Investment Subsidy for Large, Mega, and Ultra Mega Enterprises

policy_goals: Attracting investments of Rs 50,000 Cr across the entire clean mobility vehicle value chain during the Policy Period
Generating approximately 100,000 new jobs during the Policy Period
Making Karnataka #1 in Asia in Future Clean Mobility, fueled by Equitable and Sustainable Development
Accelerating Clean Mobility Vehicle Adoption in Karnataka through a Robust Charging Infrastructure Network or hydrogen stations
Create a Clean Mobility Vehicle ecosystem that fosters innovation in the State of Karnataka
policy_details.policy_summary: The Karnataka Clean Mobility Policy 2025-2030 positions Karnataka as the premier destination for clean mobility vehicle manufacturing across the entire value chain, covering EVs (battery and fuel cell), hydrogen-based vehicles, cells and battery packs, vehicle components, charging and swapping equipment, hydrogen stations, battery recycling, testing facilities, and R&D. The policy outlines demand-side concessions (road tax and registration exemptions) and supply-side fiscal incentives including Capital Investment Subsidies for Micro, Small, Medium, Large, Mega, and Ultra Mega enterprises scaled by zonal classification (Zone 1, Zone 2, Zone 3), 100% stamp duty exemption/reimbursement, concessional registration charges of INR 1 per INR 1,000, 100% reimbursement of land conversion fee, electricity duty exemptions, ETP subsidies, capital subsidies for fast charging/battery swapping/hydrogen stations, and R&D cost reimbursements.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to 35% capital subsidy, 100% stamp duty exemption, and road tax waivers for clean mobility manufacturing, charging stations, and R&D in Karnataka.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Commerce and Industries Department, Government of Karnataka

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: Following activities/products for which investments are made during the policy period as per Section 7 would be eligible for availing incentives under this policy: 1. Clean mobility vehicle and Clean Mobility components: Manufacturing/Assembly of Electric Vehicles (fixed battery/swappable battery), hydrogen based vehicles, fuel cell based electric vehicles; Manufacturing of clean mobility cells, clean mobility battery pack/module manufacturing and assembly (Li Ion cells, fuel cells, hydrogen cells or any advanced chemistry battery cells); Manufacturing of clean mobility vehicle components (Electric motor & drive, Motor Controllers/Power Control Units, Inverters/converters, AC/DC charging inlet, Battery system/BMS/Thermal management system, Auxiliary Battery System, EV specific electrical infrastructure, Electric compressor). 2. Li-ion & fuel cell components: Cathode Active Materials, Anode Materials, Separator, Carbonate Solvents, Processing of minerals used for Li-ion processing only (e.g. Li, Ni, Co, Mn), Consumables. 3. Manufacturing of Electric Vehicle Charging/Swapping Infrastructure Equipment and Hydrogen stations. 4. Re-use and Recycling of batteries through recycling centers. 5. Clean Mobility vehicle testing facility. Note: Components manufacturers shall supply minimum 50% of their products to EV and clean mobility OEM. All new EV Enterprises shall create maximum possible employment opportunities and provide a minimum 70% of employment to the local people on overall basis [100% employment to local people in case of Group D category]. For Expansion/Diversification/Modernization, the Enterprise has to increase installed capacity by at least 25% or average production during immediate 3 years prior to commercial production, and make an additional investment of at least 25% of original fixed investment.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Slow charging stations receive no incentives. Motor cars, jeeps, omni buses, and private service vehicles run on electricity having vehicle cost exceeding Rs. 25 lakhs are not exempt from tax under Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1957. For Large/Mega/Ultra Mega enterprises, land capital subsidy includes only districts other than Bengaluru Urban and Bengaluru Rural up to an extent of 50 acres.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Incentives are differentiated by taluk-based zonal classification across Karnataka into Zone 1, Zone 2, and Zone 3 (Zone 3 comprising Bengaluru Urban taluks and Bengaluru Rural taluks).
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: As certified by Technical Committee or automatically covered under Section 4.1.1; clearance via Karnataka Udyoga Mitra.

policy_name: Incentives and Offerings under Karnataka Data Centre Policy 2022
incentive_name: Capital Subsidy

policy_goals: Support the Data Centre ecosystem and industry located within Karnataka through targeted incentives, concessions, and subsidies
Encourage investment in Data Centres outside Bengaluru Urban district
Promote green energy and sustainable power consumption in Data Centre operations
Streamline single-window approval and institutional clearances for Data Centre parks and units
policy_details.policy_summary: The Operational Guidelines detail the execution, registration, and sanction mechanisms for incentives offered under the Karnataka Data Centre Policy 2022, notified vide GO No. ITBT/79/ADM/2021 dated 7th May 2022. Administered by the Karnataka Innovation and Technology Society (KITS), the policy offers capital subsidy outside Bengaluru Urban district, land subsidy, 100% stamp duty exemption with concessional registration charges, full exemption of land conversion fee, power tariff concessions (industrial power tariff), green power tariff reimbursement of ₹0.50 per unit, 100% electricity duty exemption for 5 years, and extensive building norms relaxations (including up to 60% ground coverage, 3.0 + 1.0 FAR, and multi-level DG stacking).
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to ₹10 Crore capital subsidy, ₹3 Crore land subsidy, 100% stamp duty and conversion fee exemptions, and 5-year power tariff concessions for Data Centres in Karnataka.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Department of Electronics, IT, Bt and S&T, Government of Karnataka
special_focus_areas: Data Centres outside Bengaluru Urban district
Green energy adoption (minimum 30% to 50% renewable energy component)
Data Centre Parks and specialized IT infrastructure

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: An Applicant should meet the following general eligibility criteria: 1. Registration with KITS/Department as a Data Centre Entity. 2. Nature of Business: Entity must be engaged as Data Centre, Data Centre Developer, Data Centre Park Developer, Data Centre Operator, or Cloud Service Provider hosting IT infrastructure in DC/DC Parks. 3. Location: The entity must have registered office in Karnataka as per Companies Act 2013 or registered as per Karnataka Shops & Commercial Establishment Act 1961. Both New and Existing units are eligible according to specific incentive matrices.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Proportionate land utilised for solar power plants or other non-DC projects established along with data centre units is excluded from land subsidy. Entities cannot avail dual benefits across multiple State policies.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Most financial incentives (Capital Subsidy, Land Subsidy, Stamp Duty Exemption, Land Conversion Exemption) are applicable specifically outside Bengaluru Urban district. Electricity duty exemption, building norms, and power tariff concessions apply across all districts of Karnataka.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Mandatory Registration Certificate or Provisional Registration Certificate with KITS/Department; Registered under Companies Act, 2013 or Karnataka Shops & Commercial Establishment Act, 1961.

incentive_details.description: One-time 7% Capital subsidy on Value of Fixed Assets (VFA) excluding land and building, provided to eligible New Data Centre entities established outside Bengaluru Urban district. Disbursed within 5 years with an annual ceiling of INR 2 Crore, up to an overall cap of INR 10 Crore or 7% of VFA, whichever is less.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: 7% capital subsidy up to ₹10 Crore (capped at ₹2 Crore annually over 5 years) for new units outside Bengaluru Urban.
incentive_details.application_process: Apply online through www.itbtst.karnataka.gov.in using Form 4.3 along with required invoices, GSTR-2A, CA certificate, and power service letter.

quantified_benefits.cap_raw: INR 10 Crore (with annual ceiling of INR 2 Crore)
quantified_benefits.conditions: Application must be placed within 12 months from the date of commencement of commercial operations; disbursed annually up to INR 2 Crore.
quantified_benefits.description: One-time capital subsidy on Value of Fixed Assets (excluding land and building) disbursed over 5 years
quantified_benefits.source_text: One-time 7% Capital subsidy on Value of Fixed Assets (VFA) excluding land and building, shall be provided to Data Centre entities outside Bengaluru Urban district. This shall be disbursed within 5 years with an annual ceiling of INR 2 Crore. Cap on the maximum amount of Capital subsidy shall be limited to 7% of the VFA (excluding land and building) or INR 10 Crore, whichever is less.
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: Eligible New Data Centre Entities outside Bengaluru Urban district

incentive_details.application_deadline: Within 12 months from date of commencement of commercial operations
incentive_details.application_authority: Karnataka Innovation and Technology Society (KITS) / Executive Committee
incentive_details.incentive_specific_eligibility: Available only to New Data Centre units located outside Bengaluru Urban district.

incentive_name: Capital Subsidy on Value of Fixed Assets (VFA)

policy_goals: Give the necessary impetus to the electric mobility sector in the State and attract investments
Update incentives in line with investor expectations and accelerate the adoption of EV uptake in Karnataka
Encourage further investments and establish Karnataka as the most competitive and attractive state for potential investors in the EV sector
policy_details.policy_summary: Government of Karnataka approved amendments to the Karnataka Electric Vehicle & Energy Storage Policy 2017 via Government Order No. CI 357 SPI 2020 (e) dated 01.06.2021 to address limitations in previous incentives (such as zero capital subsidy for EV assembly, restricted eligibility, and low caps). The amendment introduces a 15% capital subsidy on the Value of Fixed Assets (VFA) payable over 5 equal annual installments and a production-linked subsidy of 1% on turnover for 5 years for Large, Mega, Ultra, and Super Mega enterprises in EV assembly/manufacturing, component manufacturing, cell/battery pack manufacturing, and charging/swapping infrastructure equipment manufacturing.
policy_details.benefit_headline: 15% capital subsidy on Value of Fixed Assets over 5 years plus 1% production-linked turnover subsidy for 5 years for Large, Mega, Ultra, and Super Mega EV enterprises in Karnataka.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Commerce & Industries Department, Government of Karnataka

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: Applicable to Large/Mega/Ultra/Super Mega EV assembly/manufacturing, EV Component manufacturing, EV Cell manufacturing, EV Battery Pack/module manufacturing, EV charging infrastructure equipment manufacturing/Battery swapping equipment manufacturing enterprises. A technical committee shall be constituted to define/certify EV components claiming incentives and concessions under the policy. Total quantum of incentives sanctioned to a manufacturing/assembly unit under this policy shall not exceed 100% of the Value of Fixed Assets (VFA) created by the unit.

policy_goals: To make Karnataka a preferred investment destination for manufacturing of Electric Vehicles (EVs) by leveraging advantages and opportunities available for sustained development of this promising segment
To maintain the lead share of Karnataka as a preferred destination for attracting investments in manufacture of Electric Vehicles
To attract investments of Rs 31,000 crore and create employment opportunities to 55,000 persons both from supply and demand side
To create a conducive environment for transition to Electric Vehicle environment from Internal Combustion (IC) engines
To provide opportunities for developing R&D in Electric Mobility
To achieve 100% electric mobility by 2030 in Bengaluru across auto rickshaws, cab aggregators, corporate fleets, school buses/vans, mini goods vehicles, and delivery fleets
policy_details.policy_summary: Provides a comprehensive package of fiscal and operational incentives for enterprises engaged in manufacturing Electric Vehicles (EVs) and EV components such as motors, powertrains, and power electronics kits across Karnataka. Incentives include capital subsidies (investment promotion subsidies), production-linked subsidies, stamp duty exemptions, concessional registration charges, land conversion fee reimbursement, electricity duty exemptions, and effluent treatment plant subsidies. Under the 2021 amendment, Large, Mega, Ultra Mega, and Super Mega enterprises receive a 15% capital subsidy on Value of Fixed Assets and a 1% production-linked turnover subsidy.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to 25% capital subsidy, 1% production-linked turnover subsidy for 5 years, and 100% stamp duty exemption for EV and EV component manufacturing in Karnataka.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Commerce & Industries Department, Government of Karnataka

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: All the EV manufacturing Enterprises will be eligible for the incentives and concessions. Manufacturing Enterprises of components required for Electric Vehicles such as Motors, Power Trains, Power Electronics kits etc. will be eligible for incentives and concessions as per the policy subject to approval of the Technical Committee which would be constituted & mandated to define/certify EV component manufacturing enterprises. The incentives and concessions under this policy will be available to all new investments both for establishment of new Enterprises or for expansion, diversification and modernization of existing industries. To be eligible for considering as expansion/diversification/modernization, enterprises shall make an additional investment of at least 50% of the original investment of the existing unit. All new EV Enterprises shall create maximum possible employment opportunities and provide a minimum 70% of employment to the local people on overall basis [100% employment to local people in case of Group D category will be insisted]. Total quantum of incentives sanctioned to a manufacturing/assembly unit under this policy shall not exceed 100% of the Value of Fixed Assets (VFA) created by the unit.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Enterprises failing to provide 70% local employment (100% in Group D) are subject to recovery of incentives.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Components require certification by the Technical Committee. Total incentives cannot exceed 100% of VFA.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Entire State of Karnataka is classified as a single zone; incentives are applicable equally across all parts of the State.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Approval/certification by Technical Committee for component manufacturers; Project approval by DLSWCC/SLSWCC/SHLCC as applicable.

incentive_details.description: Full exemption of duty/tax on electricity tariff for MSME manufacturing units for the first five years of operation.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: 100% electricity duty exemption for 5 years for MSME manufacturers.
incentive_details.application_process: Submit application to the jurisdictional ESCOM accompanied by DIC eligibility certificate.

quantified_benefits.value_raw: 100% exemption for initial period of Five years
quantified_benefits.description: Exemption from electricity duty/tax
quantified_benefits.source_text: 100% exemption of duty/tax on electricity tariff for the initial period of Five years.

parent_policy_name: Karnataka Electric Vehicle & Energy Storage Policy-2017
policy_name: Incentives and Concessions to Electric Vehicle & its Components Manufacturing Enterprises
incentive_name: Stamp Duty Exemption and Concessional Registration

policy_goals: To make Karnataka a preferred investment destination for manufacturing of Electric Vehicles (EVs) by leveraging advantages and opportunities available for sustained development of this promising segment
To maintain the lead share of Karnataka as a preferred destination for attracting investments in manufacture of Electric Vehicles
To attract investments of Rs 31,000 crore and create employment opportunities to 55,000 persons both from supply and demand side
To create a conducive environment for transition to Electric Vehicle environment from Internal Combustion (IC) engines
To provide opportunities for developing R&D in Electric Mobility
To achieve 100% electric mobility by 2030 in Bengaluru across auto rickshaws, cab aggregators, corporate fleets, school buses/vans, mini goods vehicles, and delivery fleets
policy_details.policy_summary: Provides a comprehensive package of fiscal and operational incentives for enterprises engaged in manufacturing Electric Vehicles (EVs) and EV components such as motors, powertrains, and power electronics kits across Karnataka. Incentives include capital subsidies (investment promotion subsidies), production-linked subsidies, stamp duty exemptions, concessional registration charges, land conversion fee reimbursement, electricity duty exemptions, and effluent treatment plant subsidies. Under the 2021 amendment, Large, Mega, Ultra Mega, and Super Mega enterprises receive a 15% capital subsidy on Value of Fixed Assets and a 1% production-linked turnover subsidy.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to 25% capital subsidy, 1% production-linked turnover subsidy for 5 years, and 100% stamp duty exemption for EV and EV component manufacturing in Karnataka.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Commerce & Industries Department, Government of Karnataka

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: All the EV manufacturing Enterprises will be eligible for the incentives and concessions. Manufacturing Enterprises of components required for Electric Vehicles such as Motors, Power Trains, Power Electronics kits etc. will be eligible for incentives and concessions as per the policy subject to approval of the Technical Committee which would be constituted & mandated to define/certify EV component manufacturing enterprises. The incentives and concessions under this policy will be available to all new investments both for establishment of new Enterprises or for expansion, diversification and modernization of existing industries. To be eligible for considering as expansion/diversification/modernization, enterprises shall make an additional investment of at least 50% of the original investment of the existing unit. All new EV Enterprises shall create maximum possible employment opportunities and provide a minimum 70% of employment to the local people on overall basis [100% employment to local people in case of Group D category will be insisted]. Total quantum of incentives sanctioned to a manufacturing/assembly unit under this policy shall not exceed 100% of the Value of Fixed Assets (VFA) created by the unit.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Enterprises failing to provide 70% local employment (100% in Group D) are subject to recovery of incentives.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Components require certification by the Technical Committee. Total incentives cannot exceed 100% of VFA.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Entire State of Karnataka is classified as a single zone; incentives are applicable equally across all parts of the State.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Approval/certification by Technical Committee for component manufacturers; Project approval by DLSWCC/SLSWCC/SHLCC as applicable.

incentive_details.description: 100% exemption from stamp duty on loan agreements, hypothecation deeds, lease deeds, lease-cum-sale, and absolute sale deeds for industrial plots/sheds executed by government agencies or approved private parks. Registration charges are reduced to a concessional rate of Rs 1.00 per Rs 1,000.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: 100% stamp duty exemption and registration charges at just Rs 1 per Rs 1,000.
incentive_details.application_process: Claimed at the time of execution of loan or lease/sale deed upon approval from SLSWCC/DLSWCC/SHLCC.

quantified_benefits.description: Exemption from Stamp Duty
quantified_benefits.source_text: 100 % Stamp duty to be paid in respect of (i) loan agreements, credit deeds, mortgage and hypothecation deeds... and (ii) for lease deeds, lease-cum-sale, sublease and absolute sale deeds... shall be exempted.
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: All EV and EV component manufacturing enterprises

quantified_benefits.description: Concessional registration charges
quantified_benefits.source_text: registration charges shall be at a concessional rate of Rs.1.00 per Rs.1,000.
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: All EV and EV component manufacturing enterprises

policy_goals: To make Karnataka a preferred investment destination for manufacturing of Electric Vehicles (EVs) by leveraging advantages and opportunities available for sustained development of this promising segment
To maintain the lead share of Karnataka as a preferred destination for attracting investments in manufacture of Electric Vehicles
To attract investments of Rs 31,000 crore and create employment opportunities to 55,000 persons both from supply and demand side
To create a conducive environment for transition to Electric Vehicle environment from Internal Combustion (IC) engines
To provide opportunities for developing R&D in Electric Mobility
To achieve 100% electric mobility by 2030 in Bengaluru across auto rickshaws, cab aggregators, corporate fleets, school buses/vans, mini goods vehicles, and delivery fleets
policy_details.policy_summary: Provides end-user vehicle tax exemptions and capital equipment subsidies for service providers establishing public charging and battery swapping stations. EV non-transport and transport vehicles (including e-rickshaws and e-carts) are 100% exempted from motor vehicle taxes under the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act 1957. Service providers receive a 25% capital subsidy on charging machinery and equipment for early-stage network rollouts, accompanied by BESCOM operational guidelines ensuring streamlined LT/HT grid power connectivity, sub-metering, and dedicated EV tariffs.
policy_details.benefit_headline: 100% road tax exemption on all EVs and 25% capital subsidy up to ₹10 lakh per fast charging or bus swapping station.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Commerce & Industries Department, Government of Karnataka

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: Government of Karnataka has exempted from payment of taxes on all electric nontransport and transport vehicles including e-rickshaws and e-carts under Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act 1957 with effect from 01/04/2016 vide Notification No. SARIE 76 SAEPA 2016 dtd 31/03/2016. Service providers for EV mobility setting up fast charging stations and battery switching/swapping stations in Karnataka are eligible for equipment capital subsidy for specified numbers of initial stations (first 100 fast charging stations, first 100 2W/3W swapping stations, first 50 car swapping stations, first 50 bus swapping stations). Compliance with ARAI/BIS standards and CEA/KERC regulations is required.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Stations beyond the quota limits (first 100 or first 50 units) do not qualify for the capital subsidy.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Fast charging stations must comply with ARAI/BIS standards. Technical safety and wiring must meet CEA/KERC guidelines.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Throughout Karnataka; power connectivity guidelines regulated by BESCOM/MESCOM/HESCOM/GESCOM/CESCOM across residential, commercial, and fuel station premises.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Connection sanction and registration with respective power distribution licensee (e.g. BESCOM).

policy_goals: Offer ecosystem support and various incentives and concessions to ESDM companies of Karnataka
Promote manufacturing and design of electronics products, intermediates, EMS, and design/IP/software services
Encourage domestic value addition in electronics within the State of Karnataka
Promote export of ESDM products and build brand equity of KESDM companies internationally
policy_details.policy_summary: The Operational Guidelines for the Karnataka Electronics System Design & Manufacturing (KESDM) Policy 2017-2022 provide comprehensive ecosystem support and financial assistance to registered KESDM companies in Karnataka. The policy covers units engaged in electronics product manufacturing/design, intermediate components (PCBs, semiconductors, ICs), electronics manufacturing services (EMS), and embedded software/IP design services. To be eligible, companies must be registered under the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishment Act, 1961, employ at least 50% of their workforce in Karnataka, and meet yearly progressive domestic value addition targets (25% in Year 1 increasing to 45% in Year 5). Benefits include capital subsidies for anchor units in greenfield clusters, R&D grants, patent filing reimbursements, international marketing support, quality certification and prototyping reimbursements, interest subsidies, PF/ESI reimbursements, stamp duty exemption, concessional registration fees, land conversion fee reimbursements, industrial power tariff concessions, and ETP setting up subsidies. Financial support per company is capped at INR 3 Crore per year and INR 10 Crore over the policy period.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to 10% capital subsidy (up to ₹10 Cr), 25% R&D grant (up to ₹2 Cr/yr), and comprehensive fiscal incentives for ESDM units in Karnataka.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Department of Information Technology, Biotechnology and Science & Technology, Government of Karnataka
special_focus_areas: Women-led delegations / female team members for international marketing
Anchor units in greenfield electronics manufacturing clusters

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: To avail these incentives/concessions, an ESDM company must be registered with DIT/KBITS as a KESDM company. Companies which are already registered under KESDM Policy need not register again under the new policy. Nature of business: The company or entity should be engaged in one of the following businesses: Manufacturing and or design of electronics products such as Telecom Systems / Mobiles / IT Systems And Hardware / Consumer Electronics / Medical Electronics / Avionics / Industrial Electronics / Defence & Strategic Electronics / Automotive Electronics / Information & Broadcasting Equipment / etc.; Manufacturing of intermediates such as PCBs / semiconductors / chip components / ICs / components; Electronics Manufacturing Services (EMS); Design / IP / Software services for electronics products; Any other electronics verticals / products covered by the National Policy on Electronics (NPE) / National Manufacturing Policy (NPM) and related notifications, as issued by the Govt. of India from time to time. Location: The company or entity should be registered in Karnataka under the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishment Act, 1961. Employment: The company or entity employs at least 50 percent of its total workforce in Karnataka, which should not include contract employees. Value Addition: The company or entity should do value addition within the state, in-line with the formulae: Year 1: 25%, Year 2: 30%, Year 3: 35%, Year 4: 40%, Year 5: 45%. For those companies who may have multiple offices in India/abroad, they must have their 60% workforce residing in Karnataka and if Karnataka design centre is directly involved in claimed activity (patent development/marketing/R&D/quality certification/prototyping), would they be considered as eligible for that particular incentive/concession.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Contract employees are not counted toward the 50% Karnataka workforce requirement. Common incentives cannot be dual-claimed across Karnataka Industrial Policy or Karnataka Start-up Policy; misrepresentation leads to disqualification.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Must be registered in Karnataka under the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishment Act, 1961.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Registration with DIT/KBITS as a KESDM company; registration under the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishment Act, 1961.
special_category_benefits: Women members receive preference for International Marketing Incentive reimbursement

incentive_details.description: Government of Karnataka provides up to 10% capital subsidy on fixed asset investment, up to a maximum of INR 10 Crores to registered KESDM companies, applicable to the first two anchor units in each Greenfield cluster. This subsidy is available for Large and Mega Enterprises and is not applicable to Startups and MSMEs.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: Up to 10% capital subsidy capped at ₹10 Crores for the first two anchor units in each Greenfield cluster.
incentive_details.application_process: Submit application Form 4 online via itbt.karnataka.gov.in / email to esdmcell@karnataka.gov.in and send hard copy to KBITS. quantified_benefits.description: Stamp duty exemption for Startups and MSMEs

quantified_benefits.description: Stamp duty exemption for Large and Mega Enterprises
quantified_benefits.source_text: Large and Mega Enterprises: 75% Available Exemption (as percentage of expenses)

quantified_benefits.description: Concessional registration charge rate

incentive_details.application_deadline: Prior to execution/registration of deeds or within policy timelines
incentive_details.incentive_specific_eligibility: Applies to industrial plots/sheds from state agencies or converted land approved by SLSWCC/SHLCC/DLSWCC.

incentive_details.description: Interest subsidy of up to 6% per annum on term loans taken during the policy period for loans up to INR 50 Lakh, provided for a duration of 5 years. quantified_benefits.description: Interest subsidy rate per annum on eligible term loans
quantified_benefits.source_text: Interest subsidy of up to 6% per annum on term loans taken during the policy period will be provided to registered KESDM Startups and MSMEs, for a period of five years for loans of up to INR 50 Lacs.

incentive_details.application_deadline: Within six months from the end of each half year

incentive_details.description: Reimbursement of 50% of actual costs incurred for international marketing, conferences, trade show participation, stall rentals, economy travel, boarding, and lodging. Capped at INR 5 Lakh per company per year. Limited to 2 employees and up to 2 international events per company per year. Daily Allowance (DA) is capped at $100 per day.

incentive_details.application_process: Submit Form 2 with invitation letter, exhibition invoice, boarding passes, visa stamping, business development report, and expense bills.

quantified_benefits.description: Percentage of actual costs reimbursed for international marketing
quantified_benefits.source_text: Govt. of Karnataka will provide reimbursements of 50% of the actual cost incurred in - Registration, economy class travel, boarding and lodging expenses for international marketing, events, and conferences; Trade show participation and exhibition stall rentals

incentive_details.application_deadline: Within six months of the expense incurred on a half-yearly basis
incentive_details.incentive_specific_eligibility: Maximum 2 employees and up to 2 international events per company per year. Economy air travel only; DA capped at $100/day. Preference given to women members.

Covers filing fees, attorney fees, search fees, and maintenance fees. 75% is reimbursed post-filing, and the remaining 25% upon grant (or 100% claimed post-grant). Maximum of five reimbursements per company during the policy period.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: Reimbursement up to ₹2 Lakh for domestic patents and ₹10 Lakh for international patents, up to 5 claims.
incentive_details.application_process: Submit Form 1 along with patent filing receipts, invoices, bank statements, and power of attorney. Each patent requires a separate application.

quantified_benefits.description: Maximum reimbursement for filing domestic patent
quantified_benefits.source_text: Registered KESDM companies will be reimbursed the actual costs, up to a maximum of INR 2 Lac for filing a domestic patent
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: All registered KESDM companies filing Indian patents

quantified_benefits.description: Maximum reimbursement for filing international patent
quantified_benefits.source_text: and up to a maximum of INR 10 Lacs for filing an international patent, provided such patent is filed or granted within the policy period.
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: All registered KESDM companies filing international patents

incentive_details.application_deadline: Relaxed from the general 6-month half-yearly deadline; patent must be filed or granted within policy period
incentive_details.incentive_specific_eligibility: Patents must be for technology-based products/services or enhance functionality. Provisional patents are not eligible. Maximum of 5 claims per company.

incentive_details.benefit_headline: Reimbursement of ₹2,000 per employee/month for 2 years up to ₹12 Lakh for new employment in new setups.

quantified_benefits.description: Monthly PF/ESI reimbursement per eligible new employee
quantified_benefits.source_text: Registered KESDM Startups and MSMEs will be reimbursed Provident Fund (PF) / Employee’s State Insurance (ESI) of INR 2,000 per employee per month for two years subject to total reimbursement of up to INR 12 Lacs.

incentive_details.application_deadline: Within six months from the end of each half year
incentive_details.incentive_specific_eligibility: Company/setup must be less than 2 years old on application date. Employment must be newly created during the policy period and continuous for at least 2 years. Only for Startups and MSMEs.

incentive_details.description: Reimbursement of expenses incurred on research and development for ESDM products (not services). Startups and MSMEs receive 25% of eligible expenses, while Large and Mega Enterprises receive 10%. The grant is available to companies less than 7 years old from incorporation, capped at INR 2 Crores per company per year, and can be claimed only twice during the policy period. quantified_benefits.description: R&D expense reimbursement for Startups and MSMEs
quantified_benefits.source_text: Startups and MSME: 25% Available Grant (as percentage of expenses).

quantified_benefits.description: R&D expense reimbursement for Large and Mega Enterprises
quantified_benefits.source_text: Large and Mega Enterprises: 10% Available Grant (as percentage of expenses).

incentive_details.application_deadline: Within six months from the end of each half year

quantified_benefits.description: Reimbursement percentage of testing/certification charges

incentive_details.application_deadline: Within six months from the end of each half year
incentive_details.incentive_specific_eligibility: Exclusively available to Startups and MSMEs with fixed asset investments under INR 10 Crore.

policy_goals: Attract establishment of 500 new GCCs in Karnataka achieving a total of 1,000 GCCs by 2029
Support creation of 3.5 lakh new jobs in Karnataka by 2029
Generate economic output of US$50 billion in Karnataka through the GCCs established by 2029
Promote balanced regional growth through the 'Beyond Bengaluru' initiative across clusters including Mysuru, Mangaluru, Hubballi-Dharwad-Belagavi, Kalaburagi, Tumakuru, and Shivamogga
Position Karnataka as a global leader in Artificial Intelligence with a comprehensive AI R&D ecosystem tailored for GCCs
policy_details.policy_summary: The Karnataka Global Capability Centre (GCC) Policy 2024-2029 is India's first policy specifically designed to support the establishment, growth, and expansion of Global Capability Centres. Structured across four foundational pillars—Ease of Doing Business/Regulatory Easing, Talent Development and Skilling, Infrastructure Innovation and Ecosystem, and Industry Collaboration—the policy offers comprehensive fiscal reimbursements, capex grants, and institutional handholding via KATALYST. Special enhanced packages are provided for 'Beyond Bengaluru' regions (Mysuru, Mangaluru, Hubballi-Dharwad-Belagavi, Kalaburagi, Tumakuru, Shivamogga), Mega Projects (>5,000 jobs in Bengaluru or >1,000 jobs Beyond Bengaluru), and Nano GCCs (5 to 50 employees).
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to 75% capex grant for CoEs, rent subsidies up to ₹2 crore, ₹7 crore recruitment assistance, and 100% electricity duty exemption for GCCs in Karnataka.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Department of Electronics, Information Technology, Biotechnology, and Science & Technology, Government of Karnataka
special_focus_areas: Beyond Bengaluru Cluster Development (Mysuru, Mangaluru, Hubballi-Dharwad-Belagavi, Kalaburagi, Tumakuru, Shivamogga)
Artificial Intelligence and Deep Tech Innovation
Mega GCC Projects (5,000+ jobs in Bengaluru or 1,000+ jobs Beyond Bengaluru)

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: Eligible GCC Unit means a GCC located or being setup in Karnataka and engaged in servicing its parent organisation and/or group affiliates. If GCC is engaged in providing services directly to third parties, other than group affiliates, then such GCCs shall also be eligible to apply for incentives under the policy provided the value of services provided to third parties does not exceed 10% of GCC's revenue in a financial year. Must be registered with KITS. New GCC Unit means a GCC Unit in Karnataka which has commenced or will commence commercial operations after the date of notification of the Policy (03.12.2024). For Beyond Bengaluru specific packages, units must locate outside Bengaluru Urban District and meet minimum 100 employee thresholds (not applicable to Nano GCCs with 5-50 employees).
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: GCCs providing more than 10% of total revenue in services directly to third parties other than parent/group affiliates. Cross-charged or recovered operational/rent/internet expenses from non-GCC activities.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Registration with Karnataka Innovation and Technology Society (KITS) is mandatory. Audited accounts, GST registration, Shops & Commercial Establishment certification, and PF/ESIC compliances required.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Applicable across Karnataka, with differentiated incentive tiers for Bengaluru Urban District versus Beyond Bengaluru Areas (including Mysuru, Mangaluru, Hubballi-Dharwad-Belagavi, Kalaburagi, Tumakuru, and Shivamogga).
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: KITS Registration Certificate, Incorporation Certificate under Companies Act 2013 / LLP / Partnership Act, GSTIN, Shops and Commercial Establishment Certificate, and EPFO/ESIC registrations.
special_category_benefits: Nano GCCs (5-50 employees exempt from minimum 100 headcount threshold)
Mega Projects (>5,000 jobs in Bengaluru or >1,000 jobs Beyond Bengaluru)
Women candidates prioritized for internship incentives

incentive_details.description: Operational expense support for co-working facility developers establishing spaces in Beyond Bengaluru clusters.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: Vacant seat reimbursement up to ₹6,000 per seat/month (max ₹2.16 crore over 3 years) for Beyond Bengaluru co-working spaces.
incentive_details.application_process: Submit application online with floor layout (minimum 7,500 sq. ft, 50 seats), lease agreements, and occupancy logs.

quantified_benefits.description: 75% of vacant seat costs in Year 1, 50% in Year 2, and 25% in Year 3 capped at INR 6,000/seat/month.
quantified_benefits.source_text: Reimbursement capped at INR 6,000 per seat per month, which shall be maximum up to INR 2.16 Crores per applicant over 3 years. Year 1: Capped at 75% of the cost of vacant seats. Year 2: Capped at 50%. Year 3: Capped at 25%.
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: Co-working space developers in Beyond Bengaluru

incentive_details.application_deadline: Annually for up to 3 years from commencement of operations
incentive_details.incentive_specific_eligibility: Minimum 40% occupancy achieved; vacant seat defined as un-invoiced for continuous 6 months. Capped at 30 new spaces.

policy_name: Karnataka Industrial Policy 2025-30 - Comprehensive Incentives and Concessions Package
incentive_name: Affordable Industrial Dormitory Subsidy

policy_goals: Attract investments of INR 7,50,000 Crore across sectors during the policy period
Generate approximately 20,00,000 new jobs by 2030
Achieve an accelerated annual growth rate of 12% for the manufacturing sector
Position Karnataka as the #1 destination for High-technology manufacturing investments in Asia through equitable and sustainable development
Attain leadership in sunrise and new age innovation-driven sectors such as ESDM, Advanced Manufacturing, Aerospace and Defence, Future Mobility, and AR/VR
Promote balanced and inclusive regional development through differential regional incentives and employment boosters
Incentivize green, sustainable industrial practices and transition towards green industrial areas
policy_details.policy_summary: The Karnataka Industrial Policy 2025-30 provides a competitive framework structured around four key pillars (Flexible Financial Incentives, World-Class Infrastructure, Ease of Doing Business, and Human Capital) and four key enablers (Sustainability, Innovation, Inclusive Development, and Governance). For Large, Mega, and Ultra-Mega enterprises, it offers flexibility between Capital Expenditure Subsidy (up to 25% of VFA over 5 years) and Production Linked Incentives (PLI up to 2.5% of net sales turnover for 7 years), along with boosters for extra employment generation, women participation, and R&D co-location. For MSMEs, it provides generous investment promotion capital subsidies (up to 35% of VFA), power subsidies, electricity tariff exemptions, stamp duty and land conversion fee waivers, quality certification support, and dedicated sustainability-linked grants.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Flexible options of up to 25% capital subsidy or 2.5% turnover-based PLI for large enterprises, up to 35% capital subsidy for MSMEs, plus full stamp duty and land conversion exemptions across Karnataka.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Commerce and Industries Department, Government of Karnataka

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: This policy shall be valid for a period of five years from the date of issue of the Government Order or till such time that a new policy is introduced by the Government of Karnataka. Further, the policy is valid for New Manufacturing Investments in Karnataka with the categories defined below. To calculate incentives, the following classification will be considered: Micro (Investment in Plant & Machinery up to INR 1 Cr), Small (>INR 1-10 Cr), Medium (>INR 10-50 Cr), Large (>INR 50-300 Cr), Mega (>INR 300-1000 Cr), Ultra Mega (>INR 1000 Cr). Further, investments for expansion of capacity will be considered for capital expenditure of new manufacturing facilities set up by an existing enterprise for manufacturing a product that is already being manufactured with / without up-gradation of technology or process, provided the enterprise increases capital expenditure by at least 25% of existing fixed investment. Manufacturing entities eligible under sectoral policies can claim incentives under either Industrial Policy 2025-30 or Sectoral Policy. All new industrial investment projects shall create maximum possible direct employment opportunities with a minimum employment of 70% to Kannadigas on an overall basis and 100% in the case of Group D employees.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Enterprises listed in Annexure 5 are not eligible for incentives and concessions (including Breweries & Distilleries for human consumption, uncertified Khandasari/jaggery with investment <1 Cr, photo studios, Xerox/data entry, fertilizer mixing, sawmills without particle/fiber board, tobacco products, reactive dyes, firecrackers, ozone-depleting substances, power laundries, traditional brick-making, poultry/hatcheries, popcorn manufacturing, small coffee roasting <2MT/day, watch/mobile repair, cyanide manufacturing, mining activity, lime kilns, diagnostic labs/X-ray clinics, mobile industries, asbestos, saloons/spas, hotels/resorts/amusement parks, vermicompost, rooftop solar power, bottling of LPG, and bio-fuel aggregators). However, new investments in ETPs by these units remain eligible.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Minimum 70% direct employment to Kannadigas overall and 100% for Group D employees. Compliance with CSR obligations under Section 135 of the Companies Act 2013 where applicable. Separate GST registration for manufacturing eligible products.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Incentives vary by Zonal classification (Zone 1, Zone 2, and Zone 3). Financial incentives for Zone 3 are restricted strictly to Bengaluru Rural (Bengaluru Urban is excluded). Special enhancements apply to Most Backward and More Backward Taluks as per Dr. D.M. Nanjundappa Committee Report.

incentive_details.description: Incentive for Ultra Mega Investors constructing industrial worker dormitories within <5 km of manufacturing investment in KIADB areas.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: Subsidy of up to ₹1 Crore per 1,000 workers accommodation for Ultra Mega Investors.

quantified_benefits.description: Subsidy for industrial worker dormitory construction
quantified_benefits.source_text: Same capex subsidy under Base Subsidy extended on construction cost with a limit of INR 1 Crore per 1,000 people’s accommodation (Capex option) / One-time subsidy up to a limit of INR 1 Crore per 1,000 people’s accommodation (PLI option)

For MSMEs, it provides generous investment promotion capital subsidies (up to 35% of VFA), power subsidies, electricity tariff exemptions, stamp duty and land conversion fee waivers, quality certification support, and dedicated sustainability-linked grants.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Flexible options of up to 25% capital subsidy or 2.5% turnover-based PLI for large enterprises, up to 35% capital subsidy for MSMEs, plus full stamp duty and land conversion exemptions across Karnataka.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Commerce and Industries Department, Government of Karnataka

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: This policy shall be valid for a period of five years from the date of issue of the Government Order or till such time that a new policy is introduced by the Government of Karnataka. Further, the policy is valid for New Manufacturing Investments in Karnataka with the categories defined below. To calculate incentives, the following classification will be considered: Micro (Investment in Plant & Machinery up to INR 1 Cr), Small (>INR 1-10 Cr), Medium (>INR 10-50 Cr), Large (>INR 50-300 Cr), Mega (>INR 300-1000 Cr), Ultra Mega (>INR 1000 Cr). Further, investments for expansion of capacity will be considered for capital expenditure of new manufacturing facilities set up by an existing enterprise for manufacturing a product that is already being manufactured with / without up-gradation of technology or process, provided the enterprise increases capital expenditure by at least 25% of existing fixed investment. Manufacturing entities eligible under sectoral policies can claim incentives under either Industrial Policy 2025-30 or Sectoral Policy. All new industrial investment projects shall create maximum possible direct employment opportunities with a minimum employment of 70% to Kannadigas on an overall basis and 100% in the case of Group D employees.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Enterprises listed in Annexure 5 are not eligible for incentives and concessions (including Breweries & Distilleries for human consumption, uncertified Khandasari/jaggery with investment <1 Cr, photo studios, Xerox/data entry, fertilizer mixing, sawmills without particle/fiber board, tobacco products, reactive dyes, firecrackers, ozone-depleting substances, power laundries, traditional brick-making, poultry/hatcheries, popcorn manufacturing, small coffee roasting <2MT/day, watch/mobile repair, cyanide manufacturing, mining activity, lime kilns, diagnostic labs/X-ray clinics, mobile industries, asbestos, saloons/spas, hotels/resorts/amusement parks, vermicompost, rooftop solar power, bottling of LPG, and bio-fuel aggregators). However, new investments in ETPs by these units remain eligible.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Minimum 70% direct employment to Kannadigas overall and 100% for Group D employees. Compliance with CSR obligations under Section 135 of the Companies Act 2013 where applicable. Separate GST registration for manufacturing eligible products.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Incentives vary by Zonal classification (Zone 1, Zone 2, and Zone 3). Financial incentives for Zone 3 are restricted strictly to Bengaluru Rural (Bengaluru Urban is excluded). Special enhancements apply to Most Backward and More Backward Taluks as per Dr. D.M. Nanjundappa Committee Report.

policy_name: Karnataka Industrial Policy 2025-30 - Comprehensive Incentives and Concessions Package
incentive_name: Sustainability-Linked Incentives and Environmental Infrastructure Support

policy_goals: Attract investments of INR 7,50,000 Crore across sectors during the policy period
Generate approximately 20,00,000 new jobs by 2030
Achieve an accelerated annual growth rate of 12% for the manufacturing sector
Position Karnataka as the #1 destination for High-technology manufacturing investments in Asia through equitable and sustainable development
Attain leadership in sunrise and new age innovation-driven sectors such as ESDM, Advanced Manufacturing, Aerospace and Defence, Future Mobility, and AR/VR
Promote balanced and inclusive regional development through differential regional incentives and employment boosters
Incentivize green, sustainable industrial practices and transition towards green industrial areas
policy_details.policy_summary: The Karnataka Industrial Policy 2025-30 provides a competitive framework structured around four key pillars (Flexible Financial Incentives, World-Class Infrastructure, Ease of Doing Business, and Human Capital) and four key enablers (Sustainability, Innovation, Inclusive Development, and Governance). For Large, Mega, and Ultra-Mega enterprises, it offers flexibility between Capital Expenditure Subsidy (up to 25% of VFA over 5 years) and Production Linked Incentives (PLI up to 2.5% of net sales turnover for 7 years), along with boosters for extra employment generation, women participation, and R&D co-location. For MSMEs, it provides generous investment promotion capital subsidies (up to 35% of VFA), power subsidies, electricity tariff exemptions, stamp duty and land conversion fee waivers, quality certification support, and dedicated sustainability-linked grants.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Flexible options of up to 25% capital subsidy or 2.5% turnover-based PLI for large enterprises, up to 35% capital subsidy for MSMEs, plus full stamp duty and land conversion exemptions across Karnataka.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Commerce and Industries Department, Government of Karnataka

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: This policy shall be valid for a period of five years from the date of issue of the Government Order or till such time that a new policy is introduced by the Government of Karnataka. Further, the policy is valid for New Manufacturing Investments in Karnataka with the categories defined below. To calculate incentives, the following classification will be considered: Micro (Investment in Plant & Machinery up to INR 1 Cr), Small (>INR 1-10 Cr), Medium (>INR 10-50 Cr), Large (>INR 50-300 Cr), Mega (>INR 300-1000 Cr), Ultra Mega (>INR 1000 Cr). Further, investments for expansion of capacity will be considered for capital expenditure of new manufacturing facilities set up by an existing enterprise for manufacturing a product that is already being manufactured with / without up-gradation of technology or process, provided the enterprise increases capital expenditure by at least 25% of existing fixed investment. Manufacturing entities eligible under sectoral policies can claim incentives under either Industrial Policy 2025-30 or Sectoral Policy. All new industrial investment projects shall create maximum possible direct employment opportunities with a minimum employment of 70% to Kannadigas on an overall basis and 100% in the case of Group D employees.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Enterprises listed in Annexure 5 are not eligible for incentives and concessions (including Breweries & Distilleries for human consumption, uncertified Khandasari/jaggery with investment <1 Cr, photo studios, Xerox/data entry, fertilizer mixing, sawmills without particle/fiber board, tobacco products, reactive dyes, firecrackers, ozone-depleting substances, power laundries, traditional brick-making, poultry/hatcheries, popcorn manufacturing, small coffee roasting <2MT/day, watch/mobile repair, cyanide manufacturing, mining activity, lime kilns, diagnostic labs/X-ray clinics, mobile industries, asbestos, saloons/spas, hotels/resorts/amusement parks, vermicompost, rooftop solar power, bottling of LPG, and bio-fuel aggregators). However, new investments in ETPs by these units remain eligible.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Minimum 70% direct employment to Kannadigas overall and 100% for Group D employees. Compliance with CSR obligations under Section 135 of the Companies Act 2013 where applicable. Separate GST registration for manufacturing eligible products.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Incentives vary by Zonal classification (Zone 1, Zone 2, and Zone 3). Financial incentives for Zone 3 are restricted strictly to Bengaluru Rural (Bengaluru Urban is excluded). Special enhancements apply to Most Backward and More Backward Taluks as per Dr. D.M. Nanjundappa Committee Report.

policy_name: Karnataka Information Technology (IT) Policy 2020-2025
incentive_name: Exemption on Stamp Duty

policy_goals: To enable the State's IT industry to contribute ~30% to India's goal of becoming a trillion-dollar digital economy
To achieve generation of 60+ Lakh direct and indirect employment in the State during the policy period
To boost the IT penetration & innovation in the State holistically and strengthen the ecosystem in new regions Beyond Bengaluru
To enable a remote, distributed labour force beyond Bengaluru, required for the IT industry
To evolve a State Cyber Security policy to employ the necessary Data Protection safeguards and create and sustain a safe and resilient ecosystem
policy_details.policy_summary: The Karnataka Information Technology Policy 2020-2025, notified vide Government Order No. ITBT 07 ADM 2019 dated 7th September 2020, aims to retain Karnataka's leadership in technology and innovation while propelling holistic economic development outside Zone 3 (Beyond Bengaluru). Administered by KITS, the policy introduces substantial fiscal and non-fiscal incentives including capital subsidies for IT Hubs/Clusters and Co-working spaces, rental subsidies, stamp duty exemptions, industrial power tariffs, quality and marketing reimbursements, PF/ESI support, patent filing reimbursements, and matching R&D grants for emerging and 5G technologies.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to ₹3 Crore capital subsidy for IT Hubs, ₹2 Crore for co-working spaces, 100% stamp duty exemption, industrial power tariffs, and ₹1 Crore R&D matching grants outside Bengaluru.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Department of Electronics, Information Technology, Biotechnology and Science & Technology, Government of Karnataka

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: To avail the policy incentives and concessions, an Entity must be registered with KITS, Department of Electronics, IT, Bt and S&T as an IT/ITeS Entity or as an Infrastructure Developer. The entity shall be engaged in Information Technology (IT) or IT enabled services (ITeS) or verticals covered under the National IT Policy. The entity must have a registered office in Karnataka as per the Companies Act, 1956/2013 or Partnership Act, 1932 or Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008 or Karnataka Shops & Commercial Establishment Act, 1961. The IT/ITeS entity must employ at least 50% of its total technical workforce (employees) in Karnataka, excluding contract employees (not applicable for Infrastructure Developers or Stamp Duty Exemption). A Unit means office space or branch office with minimum 10 employees on payroll.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Indian subsidiaries of foreign entities are excluded from R&D Support matching grants. Provisional patent application expenses are excluded. Contract employees and external consultants are excluded from technical headcount/grant costs.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Must employ at least 50% of total technical workforce in Karnataka. Non-infrastructure reimbursement incentives to a single applicant are capped at ₹2 Crore per year and ₹10 Crore across the policy period.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Beyond Bengaluru (Taluks in Zone 1 and Zone 2 outside Zone 3 as classified under the prevailing Karnataka Industrial Policy 2020-25).
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Registration with Karnataka Innovation and Technology Society (KITS) / Department of Electronics, IT, Bt and S&T.
special_category_benefits: Women employees (facilitation of night shifts with safety provisions)

incentive_details.description: Exemption on Stamp Duty paid in respect of loan agreements, credit deeds, mortgage/hypothecation deeds, and lease deeds, lease-cum-sale, sub-lease and absolute sale deeds executed for industrial plots/sheds by KIADB, KSSIDC, KEONICS, and industrial co-operatives. Available for IT/ITeS Entities and Infrastructure Developers. 75% exemption in taluks of Mysuru, Hubballi, Dharwad, and Mangaluru; 100% exemption in all other taluks of Zone 1 and Zone 2. Not applicable in Zone 3.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: Up to 100% Stamp Duty exemption (75% in Mysuru, Hubballi-Dharwad, Mangaluru) on land leases, sales, and loan deeds outside Zone 3.
incentive_details.application_process: Obtain Provisional Registration Certificate from KITS, apply online via Form 4.5, obtain Stamp Duty Exemption Certificate, and present to the local Sub-Registrar.

quantified_benefits.description: Stamp duty exemption in Tier-2 city cluster taluks
quantified_benefits.source_text: IT/ ITeS Entities shall be entitled to an exemption of 75% in Mysuru, Hubballi, Dharwad and Mangaluru
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: Land allocated to Unit in taluks of Mysuru, Hubballi, Dharwad, and Mangaluru

quantified_benefits.description: Stamp duty exemption in all other taluks in Zone 1 and Zone 2
quantified_benefits.source_text: and 100% for all other Zones except Zone 3 as per the prevailing Karnataka Industrial Policy.
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: Land allocated to Unit in any other taluks of Zone 1 and Zone 2

incentive_details.application_deadline: Before date of commencement of commercial operations
incentive_details.application_authority: KITS / Sub-Registrar / Department of Stamps and Registration
incentive_details.incentive_specific_eligibility: Must obtain project clearance from SLSWCC/SHLCC/DLSWCC and Provisional Registration Certificate before commercial operations.

Must have at least 15,000 sq. ft. area, owned/leased/rented for at least 7 years with commitment to operate for at least 5 years, allocating at least 60% area to IT/ITeS. Eligible for Infrastructure Developers occupied by multiple IT/ITeS entities (min 60% seat occupancy) or individual/freelance professionals (min 300 seats). quantified_benefits.applicable_to: Co-working spaces in Zones 1 and 2 achieving Phase I milestone

quantified_benefits.description: Phase II subsidy for Co-working/Plug and Play Infrastructure (cumulative 60% occupancy or 300 freelance/IT seats)
quantified_benefits.source_text: Phase II: The Applicant should achieve an additional minimum occupancy rate of 30% (cumulative 60% or 300 individual professionals): Additional 17% of approved FII claimed up to INR 1 Crore, whichever is lower
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: Co-working spaces in Zones 1 and 2 achieving Phase II milestone

incentive_details.incentive_specific_eligibility: Minimum 15,000 sq. ft., 7-year lease/ownership, 5-year operational commitment, 60% area dedicated to IT/ITeS.
