policy_details.policy_summary: The Karnataka Information Technology Policy 2020-2025, notified vide Government Order No. ITBT 07 ADM 2019 dated 7th September 2020, aims to retain Karnataka's leadership in technology and innovation while propelling holistic economic development outside Zone 3 (Beyond Bengaluru). Administered by KITS, the policy introduces substantial fiscal and non-fiscal incentives including capital subsidies for IT Hubs/Clusters and Co-working spaces, rental subsidies, stamp duty exemptions, industrial power tariffs, quality and marketing reimbursements, PF/ESI support, patent filing reimbursements, and matching R&D grants for emerging and 5G technologies.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to ₹3 Crore capital subsidy for IT Hubs, ₹2 Crore for co-working spaces, 100% stamp duty exemption, industrial power tariffs, and ₹1 Crore R&D matching grants outside Bengaluru.

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: To avail the policy incentives and concessions, an Entity must be registered with KITS, Department of Electronics, IT, Bt and S&T as an IT/ITeS Entity or as an Infrastructure Developer. The entity shall be engaged in Information Technology (IT) or IT enabled services (ITeS) or verticals covered under the National IT Policy. The entity must have a registered office in Karnataka as per the Companies Act, 1956/2013 or Partnership Act, 1932 or Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008 or Karnataka Shops & Commercial Establishment Act, 1961. The IT/ITeS entity must employ at least 50% of its total technical workforce (employees) in Karnataka, excluding contract employees (not applicable for Infrastructure Developers or Stamp Duty Exemption). A Unit means office space or branch office with minimum 10 employees on payroll.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Indian subsidiaries of foreign entities are excluded from R&D Support matching grants. Provisional patent application expenses are excluded. Contract employees and external consultants are excluded from technical headcount/grant costs.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Must employ at least 50% of total technical workforce in Karnataka. Non-infrastructure reimbursement incentives to a single applicant are capped at ₹2 Crore per year and ₹10 Crore across the policy period.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Beyond Bengaluru (Taluks in Zone 1 and Zone 2 outside Zone 3 as classified under the prevailing Karnataka Industrial Policy 2020-25).
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Registration with Karnataka Innovation and Technology Society (KITS) / Department of Electronics, IT, Bt and S&T.
special_category_benefits: Women employees (facilitation of night shifts with safety provisions)

policy_name: Karnataka Renewable Energy Policy 2022-2027
incentive_name: Concessions and Incentives under Central MNRE Schemes

policy_goals: Facilitate development of 10 GW of additional RE projects with or without energy storage systems in the State, including up to 1 GW of Rooftop solar PV projects
Attract investment in the RE sector and development of State economy
Tap RE potential in the State and meet RE demand within Karnataka as well as export power outside the State
Achieve Renewable Purchase Obligation (RPO) targets as specified by KERC from time to time
Develop Renewable Energy Parks including hybrid parks in the State
Encourage private sector participation in transmission network/Green Energy Corridor projects
Develop an ecosystem for distributed generation through solarization of agriculture feeders and pumps
Promote adoption of electric vehicles and decarbonize transportation using clean energy
Promote energy storage projects and create an energy storage market for grid integration and support services
Promote development of wind-solar hybrid projects and repowering of wind assets
Promote floating solar development, including hybridization with existing hydro stations
Promote generation of energy through biomass, cogeneration, and waste-to-energy
Promote new initiatives, R&D, and emerging energy technologies such as offshore wind, hydrogen and fuel cells, tidal/wave, and Bio-CNG
policy_details.policy_summary: The Karnataka Renewable Energy Policy 2022-2027 establishes a comprehensive regulatory, infrastructural, and promotional framework to harness 10 GW of additional renewable energy capacity in Karnataka over five years. It covers solar (MW-scale, rooftop, distributed/agricultural, floating, and EV charging), wind energy and repowering, solar-wind hybrid projects, energy storage systems (including pumped hydro and battery storage), biomass, cogeneration, municipal waste-to-energy, mini/small hydro, and emerging clean technologies. policy_name: Karnataka Renewable Energy Policy 2022-2027
incentive_name: Time-Bound Transmission Evacuation Approvals

policy_goals: Facilitate development of 10 GW of additional RE projects with or without energy storage systems in the State, including up to 1 GW of Rooftop solar PV projects
Attract investment in the RE sector and development of State economy
Tap RE potential in the State and meet RE demand within Karnataka as well as export power outside the State
Achieve Renewable Purchase Obligation (RPO) targets as specified by KERC from time to time
Develop Renewable Energy Parks including hybrid parks in the State
Encourage private sector participation in transmission network/Green Energy Corridor projects
Develop an ecosystem for distributed generation through solarization of agriculture feeders and pumps
Promote adoption of electric vehicles and decarbonize transportation using clean energy
Promote energy storage projects and create an energy storage market for grid integration and support services
Promote development of wind-solar hybrid projects and repowering of wind assets
Promote floating solar development, including hybridization with existing hydro stations
Promote generation of energy through biomass, cogeneration, and waste-to-energy
Promote new initiatives, R&D, and emerging energy technologies such as offshore wind, hydrogen and fuel cells, tidal/wave, and Bio-CNG
policy_details.policy_summary: The Karnataka Renewable Energy Policy 2022-2027 establishes a comprehensive regulatory, infrastructural, and promotional framework to harness 10 GW of additional renewable energy capacity in Karnataka over five years. It covers solar (MW-scale, rooftop, distributed/agricultural, floating, and EV charging), wind energy and repowering, solar-wind hybrid projects, energy storage systems (including pumped hydro and battery storage), biomass, cogeneration, municipal waste-to-energy, mini/small hydro, and emerging clean technologies. The policy treats all RE projects as manufacturing industries eligible for industrial concessions (excluding investment promotion subsidies), provides deemed land conversion under Section 109 of the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, streamlines InSTS and ISTS grid connectivity via KPTCL/CTU, permits open access (captive, group captive, third-party sale, power exchange), and allows up to 50% State equity participation in RE Parks under PPP models.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Treatment as manufacturing industry for industrial incentives, deemed land conversion, open access energy sales, and up to 50% State equity participation in Renewable Energy Parks.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Energy Department, Government of Karnataka
special_focus_areas: Rooftop Solar Net/Gross Metering and P2P Trading
Electric Vehicle Charging and Battery Swapping
Emerging Clean Tech (Offshore Wind, Hydrogen, Bio-CNG)

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: All Solar, Wind, Solar-Wind Hybrid, Energy Storage, Mini and Small-Hydro, Biomass, Co-generation, Waste to Energy projects and new initiatives/pilot projects established in the State of Karnataka during the Policy period shall be eligible for benefits under this Policy. Any individual or company or body corporate or association or society or body of individuals, whether incorporated or not shall be eligible for setting up RE projects, either for the purpose of captive use and/or for selling of electricity to the Distribution Licensee or Third Party including under the Renewable Energy Certificate (REC) mechanism subject to provisions of this Policy and in accordance with the Electricity Act 2003. The net worth of the company shall be at least 30% of the total project cost. Capital cost per MW considered by KERC in respective tariff Orders shall be used as reference.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Investment promotion subsidies under the State Industrial Policy are explicitly excluded for RE projects.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Developer net worth must be at least 30% of total project cost (determined by KERC capital cost benchmarks or DPR). Project developers must adhere to land utilization ceilings (e.g. 3.5 acres/MWac for Solar PV, 4 acres/WTG for Wind, 100 sq. ft/kWp for Rooftop Solar) and execute an Implementation Agreement with KREDL within 45 days of Government Order.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Application and project approval via KREDL / State Level Allotment Committee (SLAC) / Energy Department; compliance with ALMM for solar PV modules and RLMM for wind turbine generators.

policy_name: Karnataka Space Technology Policy, 2024-2029
incentive_name: Capital Investment Subsidy

policy_goals: Sustain Karnataka as the number one destination for space technology in India and hold 50% of the national market share (USD 22 billion market by 2033)
Propel Karnataka into a global space technology destination with comprehensive capabilities across the space value chain, targeting five percent of the global market share
Attract and generate cumulative investments of USD 3 billion into the space ecosystem of Karnataka during the policy period
Train and up-skill 5,000 professionals and students, including at least 1,500 women professionals and students, up to industry standards
Support at least 500 space sector Start-Ups and MSMEs to grow and innovate during the policy period
Design, manufacture, assemble, integrate, test, launch, and operate 50+ satellites with substantial indigenization by Karnataka-based NewSpace enterprises
Set up dedicated space manufacturing park(s) with required common infrastructure and ensure testing needs are met across the state
policy_details.policy_summary: The Karnataka Space Technology Policy (2024-2029) establishes a comprehensive strategic and fiscal framework to build, scale, and accelerate the space ecosystem in Karnataka across upstream (launchers, satellites, propulsion, avionics, ground stations, space stations, space tourism, in-orbit servicing) and downstream (earth observation, satellite communications, and positioning/navigation/timing) segments. Centered on five strategic pillars—Skill Development, Investments, Infrastructure and Facilities, Innovation and Facilitation, and Adoption and Awareness—the policy provides capital subsidies, stamp duty and registration concessions, land conversion fee waivers, ETP/STP subsidies, power tariff reimbursements, and electricity duty exemptions for investments up to INR 100 Crore (with customized packages for projects above INR 100 Crore). It also delivers tailored grants and reimbursements up to INR 75 Lakhs each for technology acquisition, quality certifications, testing access, IP registration, and R&D; marketing reimbursements up to INR 1 Crore; a 15% revenue-based incentive for downstream application deployment; PF/ESI subsidies; employee skilling subsidies; private-public space manufacturing park developer incentives; and funding for academic and research institutions.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to 20% capital subsidy on plant & machinery, 25% land subsidy, 100% stamp duty exemption, and multiple grants up to ₹75 Lakhs for space tech MSMEs and Start-Ups in Karnataka.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Department of Electronics, Information Technology, Biotechnology and Science & Technology, Government of Karnataka
special_focus_areas: Women professionals and entrepreneurs in NewSpace
Upstream and downstream space technology indigenization
Deep tech and space electronics manufacturing
Defence space and dual-use space applications
Digital public infrastructure for geospatial technologies

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: 5. Scope and Coverage: 5.1 Unless stated otherwise in this policy, entities and enterprises availing benefits through any other policy of Government of Karnataka, during the period in which this policy is active, will not be eligible to avail any benefits under this policy. 5.2 Companies/Entities/Enterprises should carefully read all the provisions listed in the policy and must comply with the requirements listed in this policy and its operational guidelines to avail benefits through this policy... 5.3 Any company/entity who wishes to avail benefits through this policy shall be registered under The Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishments act, 1961 and or Factories Act, 1948 at the time of applying for benefits. 5.4 Karnataka Innovation and Technology Society (KITS) shall operationalize an online registration mechanism to register all space sector companies and entities in Karnataka. Only companies/entities registered with KITS under this mechanism shall be eligible to avail benefits through this policy. 5.5 Any company/entity who wants to avail benefits through this policy shall be: a. Indian entities authorized as Non-Government Entity by IN-SPACe as defined in the Indian Space Policy, 2023 and its Norms Guidelines and Procedures, 2024 to the Indian Space Policy, 2023; b. Indian entities who are registered vendor to ISRO and should be able provide documentary evidence to support supply of goods/services pertinent to the focus sectors of this policy over the last 5 years; c. Indian entities who are registered vendor to space Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) / System Integrators (SI) to global space agencies and should be able provide documentary evidence to support supply of goods/services pertinent to the focus sectors of this policy over the last 5 years; d. Non-Indian entities who are globally renowned Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) / System Integrators (SI) /component manufacturers in space sector and should be able provide documentary evidence to support supply of goods/services pertinent to the focus sectors of this policy over the last 5 years... e. Indian and Non-Indian entities should be able to demonstrate their relevance to the focus sectors of this policy through Chartered Accountant (CA) certificates, work orders, invoices etc.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Entities and enterprises availing benefits through any other policy of Government of Karnataka during the period in which this policy is active will not be eligible to avail benefits under this policy, unless stated otherwise.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Registration under The Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1961 or Factories Act, 1948; online registration with KITS; and IN-SPACe NGE authorization or 5-year vendor registration with ISRO/global space OEMs/System Integrators.

policy_goals: Sustain Karnataka as the number one destination for space technology in India and hold 50% of the national market share (USD 22 billion market by 2033)
Propel Karnataka into a global space technology destination with comprehensive capabilities across the space value chain, targeting five percent of the global market share
Attract and generate cumulative investments of USD 3 billion into the space ecosystem of Karnataka during the policy period

policy_details.policy_summary: The Karnataka Space Technology Policy (2024-2029) establishes a comprehensive strategic and fiscal framework to build, scale, and accelerate the space ecosystem in Karnataka across upstream (launchers, satellites, propulsion, avionics, ground stations, space stations, space tourism, in-orbit servicing) and downstream (earth observation, satellite communications, and positioning/navigation/timing) segments. Centered on five strategic pillars—Skill Development, Investments, Infrastructure and Facilities, Innovation and Facilitation, and Adoption and Awareness—the policy provides capital subsidies, stamp duty and registration concessions, land conversion fee waivers, ETP/STP subsidies, power tariff reimbursements, and electricity duty exemptions for investments up to INR 100 Crore (with customized packages for projects above INR 100 Crore). It also delivers tailored grants and reimbursements up to INR 75 Lakhs each for technology acquisition, quality certifications, testing access, IP registration, and R&D; marketing reimbursements up to INR 1 Crore; a 15% revenue-based incentive for downstream application deployment; PF/ESI subsidies; employee skilling subsidies; private-public space manufacturing park developer incentives; and funding for academic and research institutions.

policy_details.policy_summary: The Karnataka Space Technology Policy (2024-2029) establishes a comprehensive strategic and fiscal framework to build, scale, and accelerate the space ecosystem in Karnataka across upstream (launchers, satellites, propulsion, avionics, ground stations, space stations, space tourism, in-orbit servicing) and downstream (earth observation, satellite communications, and positioning/navigation/timing) segments. Centered on five strategic pillars—Skill Development, Investments, Infrastructure and Facilities, Innovation and Facilitation, and Adoption and Awareness—the policy provides capital subsidies, stamp duty and registration concessions, land conversion fee waivers, ETP/STP subsidies, power tariff reimbursements, and electricity duty exemptions for investments up to INR 100 Crore (with customized packages for projects above INR 100 Crore). It also delivers tailored grants and reimbursements up to INR 75 Lakhs each for technology acquisition, quality certifications, testing access, IP registration, and R&D; marketing reimbursements up to INR 1 Crore; a 15% revenue-based incentive for downstream application deployment; PF/ESI subsidies; employee skilling subsidies; private-public space manufacturing park developer incentives; and funding for academic and research institutions.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to 20% capital subsidy on plant & machinery, 25% land subsidy, 100% stamp duty exemption, and multiple grants up to ₹75 Lakhs for space tech MSMEs and Start-Ups in Karnataka.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Department of Electronics, Information Technology, Biotechnology and Science & Technology, Government of Karnataka
special_focus_areas: Women professionals and entrepreneurs in NewSpace

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: 5. Scope and Coverage: 5.1 Unless stated otherwise in this policy, entities and enterprises availing benefits through any other policy of Government of Karnataka, during the period in which this policy is active, will not be eligible to avail any benefits under this policy. 5.2 Companies/Entities/Enterprises should carefully read all the provisions listed in the policy and must comply with the requirements listed in this policy and its operational guidelines to avail benefits through this policy... 5.3 Any company/entity who wishes to avail benefits through this policy shall be registered under The Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishments act, 1961 and or Factories Act, 1948 at the time of applying for benefits. 5.4 Karnataka Innovation and Technology Society (KITS) shall operationalize an online registration mechanism to register all space sector companies and entities in Karnataka. Only companies/entities registered with KITS under this mechanism shall be eligible to avail benefits through this policy. 5.5 Any company/entity who wants to avail benefits through this policy shall be: a. Indian entities authorized as Non-Government Entity by IN-SPACe as defined in the Indian Space Policy, 2023 and its Norms Guidelines and Procedures, 2024 to the Indian Space Policy, 2023; b. Indian entities who are registered vendor to ISRO and should be able provide documentary evidence to support supply of goods/services pertinent to the focus sectors of this policy over the last 5 years; c. Indian entities who are registered vendor to space Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) / System Integrators (SI) to global space agencies and should be able provide documentary evidence to support supply of goods/services pertinent to the focus sectors of this policy over the last 5 years; d. Non-Indian entities who are globally renowned Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) / System Integrators (SI) /component manufacturers in space sector and should be able provide documentary evidence to support supply of goods/services pertinent to the focus sectors of this policy over the last 5 years... e. Indian and Non-Indian entities should be able to demonstrate their relevance to the focus sectors of this policy through Chartered Accountant (CA) certificates, work orders, invoices etc.

policy_details.policy_summary: The ELEVATE Grant-in-Aid scheme provides one-time seed funding support of up to INR 50 Lakhs to early-stage startups in Karnataka to develop their ideas to proof-of-concept (PoC) and prototype stage, along with subsidized incubation, mentorship, and government piloting opportunities.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to INR 50 Lakhs one-time grant-in-aid seed funding and subsidized incubation support for early-stage startups.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Karnataka Innovation and Technology Society (KITS), Department of Electronics, IT, Bt and S&T, Government of Karnataka

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: An entity will be considered as a Startup on fulfilling conditions: incorporated as a private limited company (Companies Act, 2013) or registered as a partnership firm (Section 59 of the Partnership Act, 1932) or a limited liability partnership (LLP Act, 2008) in Karnataka. Turnover since incorporation should not have exceeded INR 100 Crores. Considered a startup up to 10 years from incorporation. Entity should be working towards innovation, development or improvement of products or processes or services, or scalable business model. Exclusions: formed by demerger/reconstitution, Section 8 company/trust/society, PPP, franchisee, subsidiary of firm in state. Applicants should have a no-lien account. Beneficiaries under ELEVATE in the last 3 years are ineligible. Founders/Directors/Partners must have minimum 10% stake and remain associated for at least 3 years. For foreign shareholding, Indian entity share must be >50% with Indian Partner majority stake.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Registered with Karnataka Startup Cell / KITS on Startup Karnataka portal; Certificate of Incorporation in Karnataka (Pvt Ltd, OPC, LLP, or Registered Partnership Firm).
special_category_benefits: 10% of ELEVATE Grant-in-Aid Scheme fund earmarked for startups working in Deep Tech, Assistive Technology, and SDGs including Circular Economy, Renewable Energy, Sustainability, and Climate Change

incentive_details.description: One-time seed funding grant of up to INR 50 Lakhs released in two tranches based on milestones agreed in a tripartite MoA between Startup, KITS, and K-tech Innovation Hub/CoE. Includes subsidized incubation support (INR 15,000 earmarked towards incubation/mentoring and INR 10,000 for milestone documentation) and a government department pilot work order of up to INR 1,00,000.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: Up to INR 50 Lakhs grant disbursed in two tranches for PoC development and product validation.
incentive_details.application_process: Apply online through Startup Karnataka portal (www.startup.karnataka.gov.in) within 30 days of call announcement. Four-stage screening process: Stage 1 (Eligibility & data sufficiency), Stage 2 (Pitch deck evaluation), Stage 3 (Multi-City Pitching), Stage 4 (Grand Finale in-person pitching). Sign tripartite MoA upon selection.

quantified_benefits.description: Total seed funding grant-in-aid provided to selected startups
quantified_benefits.source_text: A one-time Grant-in-aid of up to INR 50 lakhs shall be released in tranches as per the Project milestones agreed in the tripartite MoA between the a) Startup b) KITS and c) K-Tech innovation hub/CoE.

quantified_benefits.description: First tranche release upon signing tripartite agreement
quantified_benefits.source_text: Tranche 1: 50% of grant amount is released as tranche 1 once the beneficiary has been identified and tripartite agreement has been signed under the ELEVATE grant-in-aid

quantified_benefits.description: Second tranche release upon milestone review of tranche 1
quantified_benefits.source_text: Tranche 2: 2nd tranche is released subject to the completion and review of milestones of tranche 1 as per the recommendation from the ELEVATE Review Committee

quantified_benefits.description: Pilot work order from Government Department for pilot/adoption of the startup's solution
quantified_benefits.source_text: As a part of the grant allocated, a work order of upto INR 1,00,000/- will be given to innovative startups whose products/solutions can be utilized by the Government Department for pilot/adoption at their end.

quantified_benefits.description: Work order for government department pilot adoption

incentive_details.application_deadline: Within 30 days of announcement of call

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: An entity will be considered as a Startup on fulfilling the below mentioned conditions defined by Government of Karnataka which is in line with the definition of Government of India notification (G.S.R. notification 127 (E) dated 19.02.2019): a. Incorporated as a private limited company (Companies Act, 2013) or registered as a partnership firm (Section 59 of the Partnership Act, 1932) or a limited liability partnership (Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008) in Karnataka. b. Turnover: Turnover of the entity for any of the financial years since incorporation/registration should not have exceeded INR 100 Crores. c. Tenure for startups: An entity shall be considered as a startup up to 10 years from the date of its incorporation. d. eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Entity must register on the Karnataka Startup portal (www.startup.karnataka.gov.in) with KITS. Founders/Co-Founders/Stakeholders must hold a minimum 10% stake in the company. For startups with foreign shareholding, Indian entity share must be >50% and Indian Partner must hold majority stake. Grantees must maintain a separate no-lien bank account.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Incorporated or registered in Karnataka; specific incentives (such as GST reimbursement, Quality Certification reimbursement, and private incubation grants) require operations in Beyond Bengaluru (outside Bengaluru Urban District).
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Registration with Karnataka Innovation and Technology Society (KITS) via Karnataka Startup portal; Certificate of Incorporation / LLP Registration / Partnership Deed in Karnataka.
special_category_benefits: Women-led enterprises (minimum 51% stake held by women founders/co-founders) receive preference in marketing reimbursement, seed funding, venture funding, and 25% of KITVEN Fund-5 corpus is earmarked for women entrepreneurs.

incentive_details.description: Venture capital equity fund with a total corpus of INR 100 Crores (INR 25 Crore from GoK/KITS, INR 75 Crore from other contributors) managed by Karnataka Asset Management Company (KAMCO) to invest in emerging, innovative, and deep tech startups across IT, software, EV, AI/ML, MedTech, Robotics, and Drones. 25% of corpus is earmarked for women entrepreneurs.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: Equity venture capital funding between 2% to 10% of investible corpus per startup (up to 30% equity stake).
incentive_details.application_process: Apply via the KITVEN portal (www.kitven.in) submitting an executive summary (4-5 pages) covering company background, technology, market size, financial projections, and funding requirements.

quantified_benefits.cap_raw: maximum stake of 30% in the company
quantified_benefits.conditions: Must have completed POC and generating revenues. Commercially viable patents/IP encouraged.
quantified_benefits.description: Equity investment range in an eligible startup
quantified_benefits.source_text: Investment range in a company shall be between 2% to 10% of the investible corpus. Investment by the Fund in VCUs shall be limited to a maximum stake of 30% in the company.
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: Startups with completed PoC and generating revenue

incentive_details.application_authority: Karnataka Asset Management Company Private Limited (KAMCO) / KITVEN
incentive_details.incentive_specific_eligibility: Startups whose products have completed Proof of Concept (PoC) and are generating revenues.

quantified_benefits.description: Financial support for Project Monitoring Unit (PMU / Anchor Institute)

quantified_benefits.cap_raw: limit of INR 2 Lakhs per Indian patent awarded

quantified_benefits.conditions: Disbursed 75% after filing and balance 25% after grant on a single subject matter.
quantified_benefits.description: Reimbursement for awarded foreign patent filing and prosecution expenses
quantified_benefits.source_text: Foreign patent awarded: For awarded foreign patents on a single subject matter, upto INR 10 Lakh would be reimbursed.

incentive_details.incentive_specific_eligibility: Startup must be registered with KITS, incubated in GoK supported incubator or CIF, and patent must have been filed within the policy validity period. Cannot be claimed if availed under any other GoI/GoK scheme.

special_category_benefits: 25% of the VC fund of INR 100 crores has been earmarked for women entrepreneurs

policy_goals: To reduce the debt burden of farmers and enable them to achieve sustenance (Swavalambana) and self respect (Swabhimana)
To enhance soil fertility and productivity by increasing life in soil
To reduce dependence of farmers on external inputs like seeds, manures, and plant protection materials by sourcing local natural resources
Judicious use of precious water resources and maintenance of production levels
To improve farmers' income through production of quality produce
To increase food security by encouraging traditional crops and traditional food habits
To increase rural employment opportunities to prevent migration to urban areas
To facilitate farmers' Self Help Groups for most of their requirements
To make the environment safe and pollution free and protect the health of human beings and animals
To equip farmers to effectively mitigate drought situations in rainfed and drought-prone areas
To bring about suitable institutional changes in teaching and research on organic farming
policy_details.policy_summary: The Karnataka State Policy on Organic Farming (2004) establishes a comprehensive framework to transform Karnataka's agriculture into sustainable, eco-friendly, and economically viable organic farming systems. The policy pools financial allocations under an integrated approach across multiple state departments, guided by a State Level Empowered Committee and a Mini Mission on Organic Farming. It focuses on converting at least one village in each hobli (200-500 acres) into an organic village, supporting Farmer Companies, Cooperatives, and SHGs, subsidizing critical organic inputs, certification costs, on-farm processing machinery, and transport. It also extends industrial policy incentives, electricity tax exemptions, concessional power tariffs, APMC market fee exemptions, and subsidized interest on credit for organic cultivation.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Comprehensive state support for organic farming including 5% additional capital subsidy, electricity tax exemptions, subsidized interest credit, and 3-year certification fee support.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Commissionerate of Agriculture, Government of Karnataka
special_focus_areas: Farm women and women farmer groups
Tribal Self Help Groups in forest areas

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: Farmers practicing organic farming, individual organic farmers, Farmer Groups, Farmers' Associations, Farmers Clubs, Farmer's Co-operatives, Farmer's Companies (FC), Self Help Groups (SHGs), NGOs, organic produce processing units, and industries producing organic farming inputs in Karnataka.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: For Farmer Companies, must be incorporated under Amendment IX A of the Companies Act of Dec 2002 with one vote per member to protect small and marginal farmers. For processing units, primary grading at farm level or direct purchase on contract farming basis.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: State of Karnataka, with special emphasis on rainfed and drought-prone areas, as well as selected hobli villages (200-500 acres).
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Registration as SHG, Society, Farmers' Association, Co-operative, or Farmer's Company under Companies Act Amendment IX A; certification under NSOP/IFOAM standards for organic status.
special_category_benefits: Tribal SHGs living in forest areas

incentive_details.description: Industries manufacturing critical inputs required for organic farming are eligible for an additional capital subsidy over and above the standard industrial policy subsidies.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: Additional 5% subsidy over and above subsidies available under the Industrial Policy 2001-06.

quantified_benefits.conditions: Units engaged in producing organic inputs within Karnataka
quantified_benefits.description: Additional subsidy for industries producing inputs required for organic farming
quantified_benefits.source_text: Industry producing inputs required for Organic Farming are eligible for an additional subsidy of 5% over and above the subsidies available under the Industrial Policy 2001-06.

incentive_details.application_authority: Department of Industries and Commerce / Agriculture Department
incentive_details.incentive_specific_eligibility: Manufacturing units producing inputs required for organic farming.

policy_details.policy_summary: The Karnataka State Policy on Organic Farming 2004 seeks to transform agricultural practices across Karnataka by promoting sustainable, eco-friendly farming systems, reducing reliance on chemical fertilizers and pesticides, and restoring soil fertility and biodiversity. The policy adopts an integrated approach coordinating developmental departments, agricultural universities, and government bodies overseen by a State Level Empowered Committee and a Mini Mission on Organic Farming. Major strategic interventions include developing Organic Villages (200-500 acres per hobli), supporting Farmer Companies, Cooperatives, and SHGs, subsidizing inputs and bio-mass/manure production, underwriting certification charges for the first three years, extending concessional credit and interest subsidies, providing transport subsidies for domestic and export marketing, and offering fiscal incentives (including 5% extra capital subsidy, APMC fee exemption, and electricity concessions) to organic input manufacturing and processing industries.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to 5% additional capital subsidy, interest subvention on credit, APMC fee exemption, and 3-year certification fee support for organic farming and processing enterprises in Karnataka.

parent_policy_name: Karnataka State Policy on Organic Farming
policy_name: Karnataka State Policy on Organic Farming (Savayava Krishi)
incentive_name: Transport and Marketing Subsidy for Organic Produce

policy_goals: To reduce the debt burden of farmers and to enable them to achieve sustenance (Swavalambana) and self respect (Swabhimana)
To enhance the soil fertility and productivity by increasing life in soil
To reduce the dependence of farmers for most of the inputs like seeds, manures, and plant protection materials by sourcing local natural resources thereby reducing the cost of cultivation
Judicious use of precious water resources and maintenance of production level
To improve farmer's income through production of quality produce
To increase food security by encouraging traditional crops and traditional food habits
To increase rural employment opportunities to prevent migration to urban areas
To facilitate farmer's Self Help Groups for most of their requirements
To make the environment safe and pollution free and also to protect health of human beings and animals
To equip the farmers to effectively mitigate drought situations in rainfed and drought-prone areas
To bring about suitable institutional changes in teaching and research on organic farming
policy_details.policy_summary: The Karnataka State Policy on Organic Farming 2004 seeks to transform agricultural practices across Karnataka by promoting sustainable, eco-friendly farming systems, reducing reliance on chemical fertilizers and pesticides, and restoring soil fertility and biodiversity. The policy adopts an integrated approach coordinating developmental departments, agricultural universities, and government bodies overseen by a State Level Empowered Committee and a Mini Mission on Organic Farming. Major strategic interventions include developing Organic Villages (200-500 acres per hobli), supporting Farmer Companies, Cooperatives, and SHGs, subsidizing inputs and bio-mass/manure production, underwriting certification charges for the first three years, extending concessional credit and interest subsidies, providing transport subsidies for domestic and export marketing, and offering fiscal incentives (including 5% extra capital subsidy, APMC fee exemption, and electricity concessions) to organic input manufacturing and processing industries.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to 5% additional capital subsidy, interest subvention on credit, APMC fee exemption, and 3-year certification fee support for organic farming and processing enterprises in Karnataka.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Commissionerate of Agriculture, Government of Karnataka
special_focus_areas: Tribal Self Help Groups in forest areas

incentive_details.description: Transport subsidies are provided to Farmers' Associations, Farmer Clubs, Farmer Co-operatives, Farmer Companies, and SHGs/NGOs for transporting organic produce from production points to consumers and for export logistics.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: Transport subsidies for domestic distribution and export of certified organic produce.

quantified_benefits.value_raw: Transport of produce from point of production to customers will be subsidised
quantified_benefits.description: Subsidy on transportation of organic produce from production points to customers and for exports

policy_name: Capital Investment Subsidy for Tourism Projects
incentive_name: Additional Capital Investment Subsidy for Priority Categories and Regions

policy_goals: Position Karnataka as the most preferred tourism destination that provides a safe and memorable experience for tourists through diverse high-quality tourism offerings developed in collaboration with tourism stakeholders and local communities to create sustainable and inclusive socio-economic development for all.
policy_details.policy_summary: Under the Karnataka Tourism Policy 2020-26 (Volume 1 - Subsidies), the Department of Tourism provides a Capital Investment Subsidy to New and Expansion Tourism Projects covering specified eligible project types: Adventure Tourism, Caravan Park, Caravan Tourism, Budget Hotel (1/2-star), Premium Hotel (3-star and above), Houseboat, Wayside Amenities, and Wellness Centre. The subsidy is calculated as a percentage (15% to 25%) of the Eligible Project Cost (EPC) up to defined ceiling caps ranging from ₹1 Crore to ₹5 Crore, with an additional 5% subsidy available for Women, SC, ST, or differently-abled entrepreneurs, or for Premium Hotels in the Kalyan Karnataka region. Projects must obtain In-Principle Approval prior to starting civil construction and must register with the Department upon commercial commencement.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to 25% capital investment subsidy with ceilings up to ₹5 Crore (plus 5% extra for priority categories) on Eligible Project Cost for eligible tourism projects in Karnataka.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Department of Tourism, Government of Karnataka

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: 1. New Tourism Projects and Expansion Tourism Projects for the following Eligible Tourism Projects shall be eligible for availing Capital Investment Subsidy under Karnataka Tourism Policy 2020-26: Adventure Tourism Project, Caravan Park Project, Caravan Tourism Project, Hotel Project – Budget, Hotel Project – Premium, Houseboat Project, Wayside Amenities, Wellness Centre. 2. The above list of Tourism Projects eligible for Capital Investment Subsidy may be reviewed and revised from time to time by the Department of Tourism. 3. Tourism Project must be undertaken on land owned by the Applicant to be eligible for Capital Investment Subsidy. However, Adventure Tourism Project and Wayside Amenities may be undertaken on leased land as well (minimum 10 years lease as on date of application for In-Principle Approval). 4. Land details must be provided for all applicable Eligible Tourism Projects except Caravan Tourism Project and Houseboat. 5. A Tourism Project availing Capital Investment Subsidy shall not be entitled to claim Interest Subsidy and vice-versa. 6. No tourism project is eligible for Capital Investment Subsidy within Bengaluru Urban district. 7. To be eligible for the Additional Capital Investment Subsidy where Tourism Project is undertaken by Women, SC, ST or differently abled entrepreneur, the Project must be established exclusively by an entrepreneur from one of these categories.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: No tourism project is eligible for Capital Investment Subsidy within Bengaluru Urban district. Tourism projects that have commenced construction work prior to obtaining In-Principle Approval are ineligible. A project availing Capital Investment Subsidy cannot claim Interest Subsidy. Total quantum of subsidies and concessions availed under multiple policies shall not exceed 30% of EPC. Project must not go out of commercial operation for >6 months during the Policy Period.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Expansion Tourism Project must undertake expansion of more than 50% of existing capacity in built-up area and/or EPC, maintaining separate books of accounts. Must operate for at least 3 years after receiving the first instalment.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Focus Tourism Destinations across Karnataka districts (specific to project category) or all of Karnataka; excluding Bengaluru Urban district and municipal corporation limits of Bengaluru, Hubli-Dharwad, Mangaluru, and Mysuru for Hotel projects.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Registration with Department of Tourism, Government of Karnataka; Trade License/permissions from competent local authorities.
special_category_benefits: Hotel Project – Premium in Kalyan Karnataka region (Ballari, Bidar, Kalaburagi, Koppal, Raichur, Vijayanagara, Yadgir)

incentive_details.description: An additional 5% investment subsidy against Eligible Project Cost for projects exclusively undertaken by Women, SC, ST, or Differently abled entrepreneurs, or for Hotel Project – Premium undertaken at a Focus Tourism Destination in Kalyan Karnataka region.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: Additional 5% capital investment subsidy against EPC for Women, SC/ST, differently-abled entrepreneurs, or Premium Hotels in Kalyan Karnataka.

quantified_benefits.description: Additional 5% subsidy on EPC for enterprises established exclusively by Women, SC, ST, or differently-abled entrepreneurs.
quantified_benefits.source_text: Tourism Project is undertaken by Women, SC, ST, or differently abled Entrepreneur: Additional Percentage Subsidy against EPC of the Tourism Project: 5%. The maximum ceiling amount of Capital Investment Subsidy for the respective Tourism Project shall remain unchanged.
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: Enterprises exclusively owned by Women, SC, ST, or Differently Abled Entrepreneurs

quantified_benefits.applicable_to: Premium Hotels in Kalyan Karnataka Focus Tourism Destinations

policy_name: Interest Subsidy for Tourism Projects
incentive_name: Interest Subsidy on Term Loan for Fixed Capital Investment

policy_goals: Position Karnataka as the most preferred tourism destination that provides a safe and memorable experience for tourists through diverse high-quality tourism offerings developed in collaboration with tourism stakeholders and local communities to create sustainable and inclusive socio-economic development for all.
policy_details.policy_summary: Under Section 14.2.2 of the Karnataka Tourism Policy 2020-26, New Tourism Projects and Expansion Tourism Projects in designated categories (Agri Tourism, Cultural Tourism including Cultural Village and Museum/Gallery, Heritage Tourism including Heritage Hotel and Sound & Light Show, and Safety and Hygiene Tourism including Mobile Toilet Van) are eligible to receive an interest subsidy of 5% per annum on term loans taken for fixed capital investment from scheduled Banks, SFCs, SIDCs, or equivalent state-level financial institutions. The subsidy is capped at ₹7.5 Lakh per annum and a cumulative maximum of ₹25 Lakh over a 5-year period, payable on a reimbursement basis upon timely loan repayment.
policy_details.benefit_headline: 5% interest subsidy per annum on term loans up to ₹7.5 Lakh per year and maximum ₹25 Lakh over 5 years for eligible tourism projects.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Department of Tourism, Government of Karnataka

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: 1. Interest Subsidy shall be applicable only for loans taken from Banks, State Financial Corporations, State Industrial Development Corporations and equivalent State-level financial institutions. 2. A Tourism Project availing Interest Subsidy shall not be entitled to claim Capital Investment Subsidy and vice-versa. 3. Components considered under Eligible Project Cost for the respective Tourism Project shall only be considered for the interest subsidy. 4. Interest Subsidy shall be reimbursed only after timely payment of loan instalment along with interest. 5. New Tourism Projects and Expansion Tourism Projects for only the following Eligible Tourism Projects shall be eligible for availing Interest Subsidy under the Policy: Agri Tourism Project, Cultural Tourism Project (Cultural Village, Museum & Gallery), Heritage Tourism Project (Heritage Hotel, Sound & Light Show), Safety and Hygiene Tourism Project (Mobile Toilet Van Project). 6. Tourism Project must be undertaken on land owned by the Applicant to be eligible for Interest Subsidy. 8. The Interest Subsidy shall be reimbursed to the Tourism Project who pays regular loan instalments and interest thereof. If the Applicant / Tourism Project defaults for any period, it will not be eligible for reimbursement of interest subsidy for that default period. The default period will be deducted from the eligible period of 5 years.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Projects availing Capital Investment Subsidy cannot avail Interest Subsidy. Default periods are excluded and deducted from the 5-year eligible period. Construction commenced prior to sanction of In-Principle Approval disqualifies the project.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Must maintain regular repayment of loan instalments. Loan must be taken from Banks, State Financial Corporations, State Industrial Development Corporations, or equivalent State-level financial institutions.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Anywhere in Karnataka on land owned by the applicant for eligible project categories.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Registration with Department of Tourism, Government of Karnataka; relevant local authority approvals and licenses.

incentive_details.description: Interest subsidy at 5% per annum on term loan taken on fixed capital investment for Agri Tourism, Cultural Village, Museum & Gallery, Heritage Hotel, Sound & Light Show, and Mobile Toilet Van projects, reimbursed annually for up to 5 years subject to timely debt service.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: 5% per annum interest subsidy on term loans up to ₹7.5 Lakh/year and max ₹25 Lakh over 5 years.
incentive_details.application_process: Phase 1: Apply online/offline for In-Principle Approval before starting civil works. Phase 2: Register with Department of Tourism upon completion and apply for Final Approval within 1 year of commercial operations. Phase 3: Sign Subsidy Agreement and apply for annual disbursals after completion of each 12 months with bank repayment certification.

policy_goals: Position Karnataka among the top 3 States in India for domestic tourist visits and top 5 States for international tourist visits by 2029
Support Karnataka in becoming a USD 1 trillion economy by 2032 through sustainable tourism development
Generate gainful employment and entrepreneurial opportunities across urban and rural regions of Karnataka
Develop world-class sustainable tourism infrastructure, circuits, and high-quality tourism offerings
Attract private sector investments and encourage Public-Private Partnerships in the tourism sector
Promote inclusive, community-centric, and climate-resilient tourism practices
policy_details.policy_summary: The Capital Investment Subsidy scheme provides financial assistance as a percentage of the Eligible Project Cost (EPC) for newly established or expanding eligible tourism projects in Karnataka. The subsidy ranges from 15% to 25% of the EPC, subject to prescribed investment thresholds and maximum ceiling limits between INR 50 Lakh and INR 10 Crore depending on the project category. An additional 5% subsidy on EPC is available for enterprises owned by Women, SC/ST, or Differently-abled entrepreneurs, or for eligible hotel projects located in prioritized regions such as Kalyana Karnataka and Kittur Karnataka.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to 25% capital investment subsidy with ceilings up to INR 10 Crore for eligible tourism projects across Karnataka.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Department of Tourism, Government of Karnataka

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: New Tourism Projects and Expansion Tourism Projects registered with the Department of Tourism are eligible for Capital Investment Subsidy under the Policy. An Expansion Tourism Project must undertake an expansion of more than 50% of its existing capacity in terms of built-up area and/or EPC. Only one expansion project of an Existing Tourism Project will be eligible. Tourism projects must be undertaken on land owned by the applicant, except Adventure Tourism and Wayside Amenities which may be on leased land with a minimum 10-year term. No tourism project is eligible for Capital Investment Subsidy within Bengaluru Urban district or within the Municipal Corporation limits of Bengaluru. For Agri Tourism Projects, subsidy is provided only to projects undertaken by a Farmer, a Farmer Producer Organisation, or a Farmer Producer Society. Projects must obtain in-principle approval prior to commencement of construction work and must operate for at least 3 years after receiving the first instalment of subsidy.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: All of Karnataka, excluding Bengaluru Urban district and Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP) municipal limits.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Registration under Karnataka Tourism Trade (Facilitation and Regulation) Act 2015 with the Department of Tourism, Government of Karnataka.
special_category_benefits: Projects located in Kalyana Karnataka and Kittur Karnataka

incentive_details.description: An extra 5% subsidy against Eligible Project Cost for enterprises owned by Women, SC, ST, or Differently-abled entrepreneurs, or for hotel projects located in Kalyana Karnataka and Kittur Karnataka districts.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: Additional 5% capital subsidy on Eligible Project Cost for special categories and focus regions.

quantified_benefits.description: 5% additional capital investment subsidy against EPC.
quantified_benefits.source_text: Tourism Project is undertaken by Women, SC, ST, or differently-abled Entrepreneur: Additional Percentage Subsidy against EPC of the Tourism Project is 5%. Project is a Hotel Project - Budget or Hotel Project - Premium undertaken in districts of Kalyana Karnataka or Kittur Karnataka: 5%.

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: New Tourism Projects and Expansion Tourism Projects registered with the Department of Tourism are eligible for Capital Investment Subsidy under the Policy. An Expansion Tourism Project must undertake an expansion of more than 50% of its existing capacity in terms of built-up area and/or EPC. Only one expansion project of an Existing Tourism Project will be eligible. Tourism projects must be undertaken on land owned by the applicant, except Adventure Tourism and Wayside Amenities which may be on leased land with a minimum 10-year term. No tourism project is eligible for Capital Investment Subsidy within Bengaluru Urban district or within the Municipal Corporation limits of Bengaluru. For Agri Tourism Projects, subsidy is provided only to projects undertaken by a Farmer, a Farmer Producer Organisation, or a Farmer Producer Society. Projects must obtain in-principle approval prior to commencement of construction work and must operate for at least 3 years after receiving the first instalment of subsidy.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: All of Karnataka, excluding Bengaluru Urban district and Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP) municipal limits.

policy_details.policy_summary: Provides fiscal concessions including 50% exemption on stamp duty, 100% exemption on registration charges, 100% reimbursement of agricultural land conversion fees for eligible tourism projects, and motor vehicle tax reimbursement/exemption for tourist vehicles and caravans.

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: Eligible New Tourism Projects and Expansion Tourism Projects will qualify for 50% exemption of Stamp Duty and 100% exemption of registration charges on loan agreements, credit deeds, mortgage deeds, lease deeds, and absolute sale deeds. quantified_benefits.source_text: New Caravan vehicles of transport category, i.e., commercial vehicles for tourism, shall be exempted from the payment of Motor Vehicle Tax for a period of up to 3 (three) years from the date of registration of the vehicle.

policy_details.policy_summary: New and Expansion Tourism Projects in specific categories such as Cultural Village, Heritage Hotel, Museum & Gallery, and Sound & Light Show are eligible for an interest subsidy of 5% per annum on term loans taken on fixed capital investment for up to five years, subject to an annual cap of INR 7.5 Lakh and an aggregate cap of INR 25 Lakh.
policy_details.benefit_headline: 5% annual interest subsidy up to INR 25 Lakh over 5 years for cultural and heritage tourism projects.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Department of Tourism, Government of Karnataka

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: New Tourism Projects and Expansion Tourism Projects for only the following Eligible Tourism Projects shall be eligible for availing Interest Subsidy under the Policy: Cultural Village, Heritage Hotel, Museum & Gallery, Sound & Light Show. Interest Subsidy shall be applicable only for loans taken from Banks, State Financial Corporations, State Industrial Development Corporations, and equivalent State-level financial institutions. A Tourism Project availing Interest Subsidy shall not be entitled to claim Capital Investment Subsidy and vice-versa. The interest subsidy shall be provided only for timely repayment of loan instalment along with interest.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Projects availing Capital Investment Subsidy cannot avail Interest Subsidy. Loan defaults result in forfeiture of subsidy for the default period.

incentive_details.description: 5% interest subvention per annum on term loans taken for fixed capital investment for a duration of up to 5 years, capped at INR 7.5 Lakh per annum and INR 25 Lakh in total.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: 5% interest subvention per annum up to INR 7.5 Lakh annually and INR 25 Lakh total over 5 years.

quantified_benefits.description: 5% interest subsidy per annum on term loan on fixed capital investment.
quantified_benefits.source_text: New Tourism Projects and Expansion Tourism Projects shall be eligible to get interest subsidy at 5% per annum on the term loan taken on the fixed capital investment for the Tourism Project, subject to a maximum of INR 25 Lakh for a period of five years. The interest subsidy shall not exceed INR 7.5 Lakh per annum.

policy_details.policy_summary: The Infrastructure Development (ID) component covers setting up of new notified Industrial Estates / Flatted Factory Complexes as well as the upgradation of infrastructure in existing Industrial Estates/Clusters. Permissible items include boundary walls, roads, water supply, overhead tanks, drainage, power substations, street lighting, common effluent treatment, water harvesting, flatted factories, raw material storage, and common utilities.
policy_details.benefit_headline: GoI grant ranging from 50% to 70% up to ₹15 crore project cost for development of new or upgraded industrial estates and flatted factory complexes.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Office of the Development Commissioner (MSME), Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises, Government of India

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: For ID projects, the land should be in the name of State Govt./State Implementing Agency (IA) with Clear Title and complying with zoning regulations and non-agricultural conversion etc. The State/UT Governments will provide suitable land for the Projects. In estimated cost to set up a project under Infrastructure Development projects of Rs. 10.00 crore / 15.00 crore (excluding cost of land), Central Government will provide grant-in-aid. The remaining amount may be loan from SIDBI/Banks/Financial Institutions or equity from State/UT Government. Construction of sheds/structures shall not be taken up under the scheme, except Flatted Factory Complexes.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Land cost is excluded from the eligible project cost for GoI grant. Individual sheds/structures for private units are not funded.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Land must have clear title in possession of State Government/Implementing Agency, located near highways/railway stations with access to power, water, and telecom.
special_category_benefits: Industrial estates with more than 50% micro, women owned, or SC/ST units

incentive_details.description: GoI grant of 60% (standard) or 70% (special category areas) for project cost between ₹5.00 crore and ₹15.00 crore for setting up new Industrial Estates / Flatted Factory Complexes.

incentive_details.application_process: State/UT government agency submits DPR appraised by SIDBI/bank to MSME-DI and SLSC; after recommendation by SLSC, final approval is granted by NPAC. Funds released in three installments (50:40:10).

policy_goals: Enhance the sustainability, competitiveness, and growth of MSEs by addressing common issues such as technology upgradation, skills, quality, and market access
Build capacity of MSEs and Startups for common supportive action through integration of self-help groups, consortia, and district industry associations
Create and upgrade infrastructural facilities in new and existing Industrial Areas and Clusters of MSEs
Set up Common Facility Centres in industrial areas for testing, training, raw material depot, effluent treatment, and complementing production processes
Promote green and sustainable manufacturing technology for clusters to enable units to transition to sustainable and green production processes and products
policy_details.policy_summary: The Common Facility Centers (CFCs) component under MSE-CDP provides grant assistance for establishing tangible shared infrastructure and common facilities such as common production/processing centers, testing and quality certification, design and incubation centers, R&D centers, training facilities, effluent treatment plants, raw material banks, logistics centers, plug-and-play setups, and sustainable waste/energy infrastructure. The project is implemented via a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) registered as a Section 8 Company (except in Sikkim where societies/cooperatives are allowed) comprising minimum 10 to 20 MSEs/Startups/FPOs.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to 80% GoI financial grant (capped at ₹24 crore) for setting up Common Facility Centers costing between ₹5 crore and ₹30 crore.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Office of the Development Commissioner (MSME), Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises, Government of India

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: There shall be a SPV for the projects for CFC, which would be a Company registered under Section 8 of the Company Act except for the State of Sikkim. For Sikkim, SPV can be a Society registered under the Societies Registration Act, or a Co-operative Society under an appropriate statute. Farmer Producer Organisation (FPO)/ Farmer Producer Company (FPC) registered under Section 8 of the Company Act with minimum number of MSEs as their member as provisioned in the guidelines of the Scheme shall also be allowed as the SPV. Minimum 20 MSEs/Startups/Green Field MSEs/FPOs for CFC with project cost of above Rs 10 crore and above; Minimum 10 MSEs/Startups/Green Field MSEs/FPOs for CFCs with project cost of below Rs 10 crore. No single unit will hold more than 10 per cent in the equity capital (or equivalent capital contribution) of the SPV. Evidence should be furnished with regard to SPV members ability to utilize at least 60% of installed capacity. Cost of project includes cost of Land (subject to max. of 25% of Project Cost), building, pre-operative expenses, preliminary expenses, machinery & equipment, miscellaneous fixed assets, support infrastructure such as water supply, electricity and margin money for working capital.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: SPV or firms should not take any grant from other schemes / GoI for this project. Lease shall not be allowed for any property owned by members or their family members. Consultants, service providers and suppliers should not be related to the SPV in terms of ownership or management.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Located in an identifiable and contiguous industrial area/cluster. Priority given to gram panchayats, municipal areas, NER, Hill States, Island territories, and Aspirational Districts.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: SPV registered as a Section 8 Company (or Society/Cooperative in Sikkim); member enterprises onboarded on Udyam registration portal.
special_category_benefits: Clusters with more than 50% micro/village units
Clusters with more than 50% women owned units
Clusters with more than 50% SC/ST owned units

incentive_details.description: Bank loan obtained by the SPV (term loan as well as working capital) for setting up CFC or future upgradation/replacement is eligible for credit guarantee coverage under CGTMSE.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: Credit guarantee coverage under CGTMSE for SPV bank loans and working capital.

quantified_benefits.conditions: Preference is given to projects with bank loan component of at least 10% of project cost; bank borrowings should not exceed 50% of the total SPV contribution.
quantified_benefits.description: Credit guarantee coverage on bank loan obtained by the SPV
quantified_benefits.source_text: Bank loan may be eligible for credit guarantee to SPV under the umbrella of CGTMSE. Such guarantee would be available to term loan as well as working capital to the SPV.

parent_policy_name: Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development (MSMED) Act, 2006
policy_name: MSME SAMADHAAN - Delayed Payments to Micro and Small Enterprises
incentive_name: Statutory Compound Interest on Delayed Payments

policy_goals: Facilitate dispute resolution and settlement of delayed payments to Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs) through Micro and Small Enterprise Facilitation Councils (MSEFC)
Mandate payment from buyers for goods or services supplied by MSEs within 45 days of acceptance
Penalize defaulting buyers with compound interest with monthly rests at three times the bank rate notified by the Reserve Bank of India
Ensure timely adjudication of delayed payment references within 90 days by State/UT MSEFCs
Provide a transparent online monitoring system (MSME Samadhaan) for filing and tracking applications
policy_details.policy_summary: MSME SAMADHAAN is an initiative by the Ministry of MSME under the MSMED Act, 2006 (Sections 15-24) to address delayed payments owed to Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs). The policy empowers State/UT Micro and Small Enterprise Facilitation Councils (MSEFCs) to adjudicate disputes between supplier MSEs and buyer units. Buyers failing to pay within 45 days of acceptance of goods or services are legally obligated to pay compound interest with monthly rests at three times the RBI bank rate. The MSME Samadhaan portal enables online filing and tracking of delayed payment cases, which must be decided within 90 days of referral.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Recovery of pending dues with compound interest at 3 times the RBI bank rate with monthly rests for delayed payments exceeding 45 days.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Government of India

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: Any Micro or small enterprise having valid Udyam Registration can apply. Under MSMED Act, 2006 (Section 15-24), MSEs who have supplied goods or services to buyers and have not received payment within 45 days of acceptance of goods/services are eligible to file a reference before the concerned MSEFC.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Medium enterprises and enterprises lacking a valid Udyam Registration or Udyog Aadhaar are not eligible to file cases under MSEFC provisions.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Valid Udyam Registration Number or Udyog Aadhaar Number

incentive_details.description: If a buyer fails to make payment to an MSE supplier for goods or services rendered within 45 days of acceptance, the buyer is legally obligated under Section 16 of the MSMED Act, 2006 to pay compound interest with monthly rests on the outstanding amount at three times the bank rate notified by the Reserve Bank of India.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: Mandatory compound interest at 3 times the RBI bank rate with monthly rests for payments delayed beyond 45 days.
incentive_details.application_process: Supplier MSE units file an online application against buyer units on the MSME Samadhaan Portal using their Udyog Aadhaar or Udyam Registration Number. The case is reviewed by the State/UT MSEFC, visible to central/state authorities for proactive action, and decided within 90 days.

quantified_benefits.value_raw: Three times of the bank rate notified by RBI with monthly rests
quantified_benefits.conditions: Applicable when payment is not made to the supplier within 45 days of the acceptance of goods or services rendered
quantified_benefits.description: Compound interest with monthly rests payable by buyer on overdue amounts at three times the bank rate notified by RBI
quantified_benefits.source_text: The buyer is liable to pay compound interest with the monthly rests to the supplier on the amount at the three times of the bank rate notified by RBI in case he does not make payment to the supplier for his supplies of goods or services within 45 days of the acceptance of the goods/service rendered. (Section 16)

quantified_benefits.description: Appeals by buyers against MSEFC awards require mandatory deposit of 75% of the award amount before any court can entertain the application
quantified_benefits.source_text: If the Appellant (not being the supplier) wants to file an appeal, no application for setting aside any decree or award by the MSEFC shall be entertained by any court unless the appellant (not being supplier) has deposited with it, the 75% of the award amount. (Section 19)

incentive_details.application_deadline: Every reference made to MSEFC must be decided within 90 days from the date of reference
incentive_details.application_authority: Micro and Small Enterprise Facilitation Council (MSEFC) of the concerned State/UT, chaired by Director of Industries

policy_name: MSME Innovative Scheme
incentive_name: Financial Assistance for Design Projects

policy_goals: To promote all forms of innovations in the complete value chain from developing ideas into innovative applications through incubation and design interventions.
To provide appropriate facilities and support for development of concept to market, design competitiveness and protection & commercialization of intellectual creations of MSME sector.
To promote a culture of innovation and creative problem solving through knowledge sharing and collaboration amongst industry, academia, government institutions, research laboratories etc.
To serve as a connecting link between industrial/academia leaders and innovators, in order to encourage new product development and hand-holding.
To focus on developing affordable innovations that can benefit a large number of people and at the same time being commercially viable and sustainable.
policy_details.policy_summary: MSME Innovative Scheme is an amalgamation and convergence of three erstwhile schemes of the Ministry of MSME: Incubation, Design intervention, and Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) protection, combined with a Seed Capital Support facility managed by SIDBI. It aims to support MSMEs across the entire innovation lifecycle—from proof-of-concept idea validation, design enhancement, and IP registration to commercialization and venture debt/equity support. The scheme provides up to ₹15 lakh financial assistance per approved idea, up to ₹1 crore grant to Host Institutes for plant and machinery, design project support up to ₹40 lakh, student design project support up to ₹2.5 lakh, 100% reimbursement on IP filings (up to ₹5 lakh for foreign patents), and up to ₹1 crore equity seed capital support.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to ₹15 lakh idea incubation grant, ₹40 lakh design subsidy, 100% IPR filing reimbursement up to ₹5 lakh, and ₹1 crore seed capital equity support.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Office of Development Commissioner (MSME), Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Government of India

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: The beneficiary unit(s) must typically be a registered micro, small or medium enterprises as per the definition in MSMED and should have a valid UAM or Udyam Registration. The manufacturing MSMEs may be a profitable entity preferably in the at least one year out of last three financial years, PMAC can relax the criteria. The designer that a unit employs in this scheme should be qualified Industrial designers having a relevant experience in that field. All MSMEs registered with the UDYAM registration portal (of the MoMSME) will be eligible. However, those MSMEs registered under UAM (Udyog Aadhaar Memorandum) which has been obtained till 30.06.2020 will also be eligible to participate till 31.12.2021, or till the revised deadline (whichever is later), after which they would need to migrate to UDYAM. For Seed Capital: All the MSMEs/others who will be the Grantees of the Seed Capital Support must be existing beneficiaries under the MSME Innovative Scheme for Incubation/Design/IPR (Patents) Schemes (whose idea has been approved and supported under the Incubation Scheme; whose design projects have been approved under the Design Scheme; or whose patents domestic/international have been granted and have already applied for/got reimbursement under the IPR scheme). For Host Institutes (HIs): Technical Colleges, Universities, other Professional Colleges/Institutes, R&D Institutes, NGOs involved in incubation activities, MSME-DIs/Technology Centres or any Institute/Organization of Central/State Government.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Valid Udyam Registration (or UAM obtained till 30.06.2020 migrated to Udyam). Host Institutes must be registered on the MIS portal.
special_category_benefits: Students receive 100% GoI financial assistance (up to ₹15 lakh) for idea incubation without required co-contribution.

Preference for Seed Capital given to solutions in social impact, environment management, Green/Clean Energy, waste management, water management, financial inclusion, education, agriculture, food processing, biotechnology, healthcare, mobility, defence, space, railways, oil and gas, textiles.

incentive_details.description: Financial support to MSMEs for engaging expert design consultants and meeting prototype/product development costs. Grant disbursed across 3 stages: Stage 1 (Strategy & Concept - 40%), Stage 2 (Detail Design - 30%), Stage 3 (Successful Completion & Final Report - 30%). Project must be completed within one year.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: Up to ₹40 lakh subsidy (75% for Micro, 60% for Small & Medium) for MSME design and product development projects.
incentive_details.application_process: MSME submits project proposal online via scheme portal. Assessed by Project Assessment Panel (PAP) of IA, recommended to PMAC for final approval.

quantified_benefits.description: GoI contribution for design projects approved for Micro enterprises
quantified_benefits.source_text: For the design projects approved for any MSME, 75% (Micro) and 60% (Small & Medium) of the total project cost will be contributed by GoI up to a maximum of Rs. 40 lakh and the remaining project cost will be borne by MSMEs and deposited to the IA.

quantified_benefits.description: GoI contribution for design projects approved for Small and Medium enterprises
quantified_benefits.source_text: For the design projects approved for any MSME, 75% (Micro) and 60% (Small & Medium) of the total project cost will be contributed by GoI up to a maximum of Rs. 40 lakh and the remaining project cost will be borne by MSMEs and deposited to the IA.

policy_details.policy_summary: MSME Innovative Scheme is an amalgamation and convergence of three erstwhile schemes of the Ministry of MSME: Incubation, Design intervention, and Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) protection, combined with a Seed Capital Support facility managed by SIDBI. eligibility_criteria.raw_text: The beneficiary unit(s) must typically be a registered micro, small or medium enterprises as per the definition in MSMED and should have a valid UAM or Udyam Registration. The manufacturing MSMEs may be a profitable entity preferably in the at least one year out of last three financial years, PMAC can relax the criteria. The designer that a unit employs in this scheme should be qualified Industrial designers having a relevant experience in that field. special_category_benefits: Students receive 100% GoI financial assistance (up to ₹15 lakh) for idea incubation without required co-contribution.

policy_goals: Promote all forms of innovations in the complete value chain from developing ideas into innovative applications through incubation and design interventions

policy_details.policy_summary: The Design Component aims to bring the Indian manufacturing sector and design fraternity onto a common platform to provide expert advice and cost-effective solutions for real-time design problems, new product development, continuous improvement, and value addition. It provides financial assistance for MSME design projects up to Rs. 40 lakh and student design projects up to Rs. 2.5 lakh, implemented through premier institutes like IISc, IITs, and NITs.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to 75% project cost subsidy (max Rs. 40 lakh) for MSME design projects and up to Rs. 2.5 lakh for student design projects.
policy_details.issuing_authority: O/o Development Commissioner (MSME), Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises, Government of India

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: The beneficiary unit(s) must typically be a registered micro, small or medium enterprises as per the definition in MSMED and should have a valid UAM or Udyam Registration. The manufacturing MSMEs may be a profitable entity preferably in the at least one year out of last three financial years (or last 1 year of its operations), PMAC can relax the criteria. incentive_details.description: Financial assistance for engagement of design consultants and expenses pertaining to development of prototype/product. Provided as grant in 3 stages: Stage 1 (Strategy & Concept) - 40%, Stage 2 (Detail Design) - 30%, Stage 3 (Completion & Final Report) - 30%.

incentive_details.application_process: MSME submits design project application online through the portal (innovative.msme.gov.in) via nominated IA. IA conducts screening, evaluates through Project Assessment Panel (PAP), and forwards recommendation to PMAC for final approval.

quantified_benefits.description: Contribution by GoI for Micro enterprises
quantified_benefits.source_text: For the design projects approved for any MSME, 75% (Micro) and 60% (Small & Medium) of the total project cost will be contributed by GoI up to a maximum of Rs. 40 lakh and the remaining project cost will be borne by MSMEs and deposited to the IA.
