It operates via Host Institutes (HIs) acting as Business Incubators (BIs), providing financial assistance up to Rs. 15 lakh per approved idea for developing prototypes/products, and capital support up to Rs. 1.00 crore for plant and machinery to HIs.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to Rs. 15 lakh grant per idea (up to 85% for MSMEs, 100% for students) and up to Rs. 1 crore capital assistance for Host Institutes.
policy_details.issuing_authority: O/o Development Commissioner (MSME), Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises, Government of India

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: Any person as individual or MSME, having the innovative ideas are eligible to avail the benefits of this scheme. The person should have innovative sort of idea which can be converted into prototype and further in business activity. There is no qualification bar to become incubatee. However, MSME should have valid Udyam Registration (UM) and individual should have Aadhar card number. Host Institutes: Institutions such as Technical Colleges, Universities, other Professional Colleges/Institutes, R&D Institutes, NGOs involved in incubation activities, MSME-DIs/Technology Centres or any Institute/Organization of Central/State Government may apply for registration as an HI and act as a Business Incubator (BI).
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Valid Udyam Registration for MSMEs, Aadhaar card for individuals.
special_category_benefits: Students receive 100% financial assistance up to Rs. 15 lakh without paying any matching contribution.
Institutes in the North East Region are given priority for supporting Business Incubators.

incentive_details.description: Financial assistance up to Rs. 1.00 crore provided to Host Institutes for procurement and installation of relevant plant and machinery including hardware and software in Business Incubators for R&D activities and common facilities.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: Up to Rs. 1.00 crore grant for plant and machinery procurement for Business Incubators.
incentive_details.application_process: HIs submit proposals via MIS portal of DC MSME website. Implementing Agencies (MSME-DIs/TCs) scrutinize within 15 days, followed by DESC review and final sanction by PMAC.

quantified_benefits.conditions: Applicable to HIs having minimum two or more approved ideas under the Incubation Scheme.
quantified_benefits.description: Grant for procurement and installation of relevant plant and machinery for Business Incubators
quantified_benefits.source_text: Financial Assistance for Plant and Machinery to HI up to Rs. 1.00 cr. (max) shall be provided for procurement and installation of relevant plant and machines including hardware and software etc. in BI for R&D activities and common facilities for incubatees of BI.

incentive_details.application_authority: Project Monitoring and Advisory Committee (PMAC), O/o DC-MSME

incentive_details.benefit_headline: Financial assistance up to Rs. 15 lakh per idea (85% GoI contribution for MSMEs, 100% for students).

quantified_benefits.description: Government of India contribution for approved ideas of MSMEs/others
quantified_benefits.source_text: For the ideas approved of any MSME/others, 15% of the total approved cost will be borne by them and deposited to the HIs. The remaining 85% will be contributed by MoMSME up to a maximum of Rs. 15 lakh per idea.

quantified_benefits.description: Government of India contribution for approved ideas of students
quantified_benefits.source_text: However, students will not be required to pay any amount and the entire cost of idea will be borne by Ministry of MSME up to a maximum of Rs. 15 lakhs per idea.

policy_details.policy_summary: The IPR Component promotes intellectual property awareness and culture among MSMEs. It provides 100% reimbursement of actual costs incurred for registration of patents, trademarks, designs, and Geographical Indications (GI). It also funds the establishment of Intellectual Property Facilitation Centres (IPFCs) with grants up to Rs. 1 crore to provide IP advisory, search, and commercialization services.
policy_details.benefit_headline: 100% reimbursement for IP registration up to Rs. 5 lakh for Foreign Patents, Rs. 1 lakh for Domestic Patents, and up to Rs. 1 crore for setting up IPFCs.

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: For Patent, Trademark and Design Reimbursement: The applicant/entity/unit must have a valid Udyam Registration. Patents/Trademarks/Designs registered in the name of individuals are also eligible for reimbursement subject to holding a Udyam Registration in their name and have full ownership of the enterprise. In case of partnership firm, applicant has to provide proof of ownership of at least 51% shareholding in the enterprise. Applicant has to submit a self-declaration for not claiming funding from any Central/State Government for the same patent/trademark/design. For Geographical Indication Reimbursement: All agencies, institutions, associations, institutes, non-profit bodies, NGOs, societies, trust, or similar other non-commercial bodies having valid incorporation/establishment documents, PAN number etc.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Cannot claim funding if already claimed under any other Central or State Government scheme for the same patent/trademark/design/GI.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Valid Udyam Registration Certificate

incentive_details.description: Grant of up to Rs. 1 crore provided to eligible agencies to set up and operate an Intellectual Property Facilitation Centre (IPFC) to provide free professional IP services to MSMEs.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: Up to Rs. 1.00 crore grant for establishing Intellectual Property Facilitation Centres.
incentive_details.application_process: Eligible agencies (MSME-DIs, TCs, Industry Associations, Universities, NGOs with 2 years operation) apply through MSME DIs to PMAC.

quantified_benefits.description: Milestone-based grant for setting up and operating IPFC
quantified_benefits.source_text: A Grant of up to Rs. 1 crore would be provided to an IPFC in milestone-based three (or) more instalments. The exact quantum of grant and instalments for each IPFC will be decided by the PMAC based on evaluation of proposals.

The fund is managed by SIDBI with an 80:20 funding ratio, where up to 80% is contributed by GoI and the remainder by the beneficiary MSME.

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: All the MSMEs/others who will be the Grantees of the Seed Capital Support must be existing beneficiaries under the MSME Innovative Scheme for Incubation/Design/IPR (Patents) Schemes, which is as follows: a. whose idea has been approved and supported under the Incubation Scheme b. whose design projects have been approved under the Design Scheme c. whose patents (domestic/international) have been granted and have already applied for/got reimbursement under the IPR scheme. All MSMEs registered with the UDYAM registration portal (of the MoMSME) will be eligible. Beneficiary will not receive seed support more than once or must not have received similar such support from any other GoI/State Government schemes.

eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Valid Udyam Registration (or valid UAM obtained till 30.06.2020 migrated to Udyam).
special_category_benefits: Preference given to beneficiaries creating innovative solutions in social impact, environment management, green/clean energy, waste management, water management, financial inclusion, education, agriculture, food processing, biotechnology, healthcare, mobility, defence, space, railways, oil and gas, textiles.

policy_name: PRomoting and Accelerating Young and ASpiring innovators & startups (NIDHI-PRAYAS)
incentive_name: PRAYAS Centre (PC) & DST PRAYAS SHALA (Fab Lab) Grant

policy_goals: Nurture ideas and innovations (knowledge-based and technology-driven) into successful startups
Build an innovation-driven entrepreneurial ecosystem for socioeconomic development through wealth and job creation
Address the early-stage idea-to-prototype funding and infrastructure gap for young and aspiring innovators (AtmaNirbhar Bharat Mission)
Promote emerging technological and knowledge-based innovative ventures by establishing business incubators across academic and technical institutions
Support incubation of about 1,000 micro and small enterprise ideas across 100 Business Incubators
policy_details.policy_summary: NIDHI-PRAYAS is a pre-incubation program initiated by the Department of Science & Technology (DST) through NSTEDB to address the funding gap from idea to prototype. The scheme supports young and aspiring innovators ('PRAYASEEs') with prototype grant funding of up to ₹10 lakhs to translate technology/knowledge-based ideas into physical product prototypes within 18 months (extendable up to 24 months). Support is routed through approved PRAYAS Centres (PCs) located within recognized non-profit Technology Business Incubators (TBIs) / STEPs. The program provides financial support to establish dedicated digital and mechanical fabrication laboratories known as 'DST PRAYAS SHALA' (Fab Labs) with grants up to ₹1.00 crore for capital equipment and ₹20.00 lakhs annually for operating costs.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Prototype grant of up to ₹10 lakhs per innovator along with access to cutting-edge Fab Lab infrastructure and mentorship.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Department of Science & Technology (DST) and Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (MoMSME), Government of India

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: Any individual applying for PRAYAS has to be an Indian Citizen with a government approved proof of nationality such as a valid passport, voter's id etc. The applicant should be in the age group of minimum of 18 years, as on date of application. Applicants can be individual innovators or early stage startups. Individual Innovator OR Team of Innovators: The innovator should have the knowhow of the PRAYAS project. For team of innovators there has to be an agreement among the team about the lead innovator who would apply, and funds will be transferred to the lead innovator's account. IP generated would vest with the innovator / team. Co-founders of Startups: Startup incorporated in India with minimum 51% equity held by Indian citizens, period of existence not exceeding 7 years from incorporation, wanting to develop prototype for a new product with no similar prior support, and annual turnover not exceeding Rs. 25 lakhs for any financial year since inception. Innovators in employment or students with R&D organisation/Academic institution must obtain NOC providing sufficient time and stating IP vests with innovator. Prototype must be a physical product capable of completion within 18 months.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Projects related to Pure Software development, e-Commerce, Service solutions, App based solutions; Funding research or student internship in Academic institutions or R&D organisations; Innovators/teams already supported once under NIDHI-PRAYAS; Parallel support under NIDHI-EIR; Products having already crossed the prototype level; Innovators not owning the project know-how or IP.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Valid proof of Indian nationality (Passport, Voter ID, etc.); For startups, incorporation certificate in India with at least 51% Indian citizen shareholding; NOC from employer/institution for students/employees.
special_category_benefits: Innovators who have bootstrapped or secured co-investment commitments

incentive_details.description: Financial grant allocated to eligible non-profit STEPs/TBIs to set up and operate a PRAYAS Centre and digital/mechanical fabrication lab (DST PRAYAS SHALA). Provides up to ₹1.00 crore capital grant for rapid prototyping equipment and up to ₹20.00 lakhs per year for five years towards operational and administrative costs, plus ₹1.00 crore per year for prototype grants to support 10 innovators per year.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: Up to ₹7.00 crores total funding over 5 years per PRAYAS Centre including ₹1.00 crore Fab Lab capital support.
incentive_details.application_process: STEPs/TBIs with at least 3 years of existence and minimum 20 incubatees submit proposals online on PMU portal upon calls for proposals issued by DST.

quantified_benefits.description: One-time capital grant for setting up Fab Lab equipment and infrastructure/refurbishing (infrastructure capped at 10%)
quantified_benefits.source_text: Rs. 1.00 Cr grant as one-time support under capital for setting up a Fab Lab with the required equipment shall be provided to the PC based on recommendation of PMC in the first year of establishment of PC.

quantified_benefits.value_raw: Rs. 20.00 lakhs per year for five years
quantified_benefits.description: Annual operational and administrative grant for managing PRAYAS program and Fab Lab
quantified_benefits.source_text: For annual operations, management of Fab Lab including a dedicated team, technical experts etc, furnishing costs, I.P databases, consumables, utilities and administrative costs for management of PRAYAS program by PC, an amount of Rs. 20.00 lakhs per year for five years shall be provided to PC.

quantified_benefits.value_raw: Rs. 1.00 crore per year for five years
quantified_benefits.description: Annual prototype grant disbursement pool per PRAYAS Centre (for 10 innovators at up to ₹10 lakhs each)
quantified_benefits.source_text: Thus, a support of Rs. 1.00 crore per year for five years shall be provided as prototyping grant to each PC based on recommendation of PMC.

policy_details.policy_summary: A flagship component scheme under the National Manufacturing Competitiveness Programme (NMCP) by the Ministry of MSME, Government of India. The scheme provides financial assistance to establish 100 Business Incubators (BIs) hosted at premier academic and technical institutions (IITs, NITs, engineering colleges, tool rooms, and R&D centers) to nurture and commercialize innovative ideas of students, ex-students, and entrepreneurs. The scheme finances 75% to 85% of project costs up to ₹8.0 lakhs per idea/incubatee (averaging ₹6.25 lakhs, capped at ₹62.5 lakhs per BI for 10 units), requiring 15% contribution from micro enterprises and 25% from small enterprises under a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Financial assistance of ₹4.0 to ₹8.0 lakhs per innovative idea (covering 75% to 85% of cost) through Business Incubators.

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: The scheme supports students, ex-students of science and technology, and entrepreneurs trying out their innovative ideas (processes and products) from conception to 'know-how' and 'do-how' stage. The entrepreneur/incubatee is expected to contribute a minimum of 15% (for micro enterprises) or 25% (for small enterprises) of the total project cost. Business Incubators must be established under recognised Technology (Host) Institutions like IITs, NITs, Engineering Colleges, Technology Development Centres, Tool Rooms, and recognised R&D/Technical Institutes.

incentive_details.application_process: Aspiring incubatees submit business and technical proposals in the prescribed proforma (Appendix-I) to the Host Institution's Business Incubator. The Managing Committee evaluates and forwards vetted proposals for MSME Selection Committee approval.

policy_details.policy_summary: Provides risk protection to livestock farmers against accidental death of animals across all districts in India. Covers indigenous/crossbred milch animals, pack animals, and other livestock (sheep, goat, pig, rabbit, yak, and mithun). Premium subsidy is restricted to 5 animals per beneficiary household (or 5 cattle units where 1 cattle unit = 10 sheep/goat/pigs/rabbits).
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to 80% premium subsidy for livestock insurance covering up to 5 animals (or 50 small ruminants) per household.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: The Risk Management & Insurance is to be implemented in all the Districts of the Country. The indigenous / crossbred milch animals, pack animals (Horses, Donkey, Mules, Camels, Ponies and Cattle/Buffalo Male), and other Livestock (Goat, Sheep, Pigs, Rabbit, Yak and Mithun etc.) will be under the purview of this component. Benefit of subsidy is restricted to 5 animals per beneficiary per household for all animals except for sheep, goat, pig and rabbit, where the benefit will be restricted to 5 cattle units (1 cattle unit = 10 sheep/goat/pig/rabbit). Beneficiaries having less than 5 animals / 1 Cattle Unit can also avail subsidy.

incentive_details.description: Government subsidy towards livestock insurance premiums for 1-year, 2-year, or 3-year policies. The subsidy ratio varies by applicant category and geography, with the balance paid by the beneficiary.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: Premium subsidy ranging from 50% to 80% for BPL/SC/ST farmers and 50% to 60% for APL farmers.
incentive_details.application_process: Farmers apply through local veterinary officers or milk cooperatives; animals are examined, tagged with 12-digit NDDB UID, valued, and insured via designated insurance company.

quantified_benefits.description: Combined Central and State premium subsidy for BPL/SC/ST beneficiaries in Normal Areas

quantified_benefits.applicable_to: BPL / SC / ST in Normal Areas

quantified_benefits.source_text: NORMAL AREAS: APL: Central Share 25%, State Share 25%, Beneficiary Share 50%

quantified_benefits.source_text: NORTH EAST REGION /HIMALAYAN STATES: BPL / SC / ST: Central Share 50%, State Share 30%, Beneficiary Share 20%
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: BPL / SC / ST in NER / Himalayan States

quantified_benefits.applicable_to: BPL / SC / ST in Union Territories

quantified_benefits.source_text: UNION TERRITORIES: APL: Central Share 60%, State Share NIL, Beneficiary Share 40%

policy_details.policy_summary: Under the Sub-mission on Breed Development of Livestock and Poultry, this component establishes rural poultry entrepreneurship units to bring the unorganized poultry farming sector into the organized fold. It supports individual entrepreneurs, SHGs, FPOs, FCOs, JLGs, and Section 8 companies to set up a Parent Farm, Rural Hatchery, and brooder-cum-mother unit with a minimum of 1,000 parent layers of Low Input Technology birds for producing hatching eggs and rearing chicks up to four weeks.
policy_details.benefit_headline: 50% one-time capital subsidy up to ₹25 lakh for establishing rural poultry parent farm, hatchery, and mother units.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India

Entrepreneurs/Eligible Entities either have obtained training or have trained experts or have sufficient experience in the relevant field. Must have got the sanction loan for project by the bank or financial institutions, or furnished bank guarantee from scheduled bank along with appraisal of project for its validity by bank where it is holding the account in case of self-financing. Must have own land or leased land where the project will be established, and all relevant KYC documents.

incentive_details.description: One-time 50% capital subsidy of the total project cost up to ₹25 lakh per unit provided in two equal instalments. policy_name: Up-scaled Design Clinic Scheme for Design Expertise to MSME Manufacturing Sector
incentive_name: Design Project Funding for Final Year Students

policy_goals: Enhance industry understanding and application of design and innovation
Promote design as a value adding activity and integrate it into mainstream business and industrial processes of MSMEs

Help MSME manufacturing industries move up the value chain by switching the production mode from original equipment manufacturing to original design manufacturing and hence original brand manufacturing

Bring Indian manufacturing sector and design expertise on to a common platform to provide expert advice and cost effective solutions on real time design problems, resulting in new product development or continuous improvement and value addition for existing products
policy_details.policy_summary: The Up-scaled Design Clinic Scheme is a component under the National Manufacturing Competitiveness Programme (NMCP) implemented by the Ministry of MSME through the National Institute of Design (NID), Ahmedabad as the Principal Implementing Agency (along with IISc and CSIR). The scheme aims to enhance design capability and competitiveness of MSME manufacturing units. It consists of two major parts: Design Awareness Programmes (seminars, workshops, diagnostic need assessment surveys, and orientation programs) and Design Clinic Projects (collaborative project funding for professional design interventions and student design projects). The total scheme budget is Rs. 149.00 crore, of which Rs. 110.64 crore is Government of India assistance and the balance is contributed by beneficiary MSMEs.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to 75% grant assistance up to ₹25 lakhs for Micro units and 60% up to ₹40 lakhs for SME units for professional design projects, plus up to ₹1.5 lakhs (75%) for student design projects.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Office of Development Commissioner (MSME), Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Government of India
special_focus_areas: Product design and innovation in manufacturing MSMEs
Switching from OEM to Original Design Manufacturing (ODM) and Original Brand Manufacturing (OBM)

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: Assistance under the scheme will be available for the benefits of micro, small and medium enterprises in the manufacturing segments as per the definition of the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act, 2006 (MSMED Act, 2006). The beneficiary unit(s) must typically be micro, small or medium enterprises as per the definition in MSMED Act 2006. It must be new to using design and preferably should not have used internal or external design expertise before. The designer that a unit employs in this scheme should be selected from a pool of qualified Industrial designers empanelled for this scheme. A copy of EM-II shall also be enclosed with proposed Design projects before submitting to the PMAC. Following are the criteria for qualifying the applicant MSME under Design Clinic: The MSME should be a profitable entity in the last 3 years of its operations; The MSME must demonstrate either an export performance or potential to export; PMAC can stipulate/relax criteria for this purpose. The local Industrial designer/ Design Company / academic institution and the local MSME in collaboration are eligible to apply for funding support as co-applicants. Both entities have to be bodies or companies established or incorporated in India under Indian Laws with on-going business.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: The applicant design company/academic institution and the applicant MSME must not be an associate or associated person or agent or employee of the other before submission of the application. Project team members representing the designer/institution must not be directors, shareholders, or management team members of the applicant MSME. Double subvention from other public funding sources is not allowed.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Entrepreneur Memorandum Part-II (EM-II) registration under MSMED Act, 2006

incentive_details.description: Financial reimbursement to sponsor final year design dissertation projects undertaken by full-time students for MSME units under the supervision of parent design institutions.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: Reimbursement of 75% of expenses up to ₹1.5 lakhs per final year student design project (out of ₹2 lakhs estimated admissible cost).
incentive_details.application_process: Students apply in a specified format through their academic institution with the consent of the beneficiary MSME. Funding is reimbursed to students through their institute in 3 stages: Stage 1 (Application approval) - 25%, Stage 2 (Mid Stage / 50% completion) - 25%, Stage 3 (Final Report Submission) - 50%.

quantified_benefits.description: Reimbursement percentage of expenses incurred for final year student design project done for MSMEs
quantified_benefits.source_text: The Design Clinic Scheme shall support design work by reimbursing 75% of expenses incurred subject to Rs. 1.5 lakh for final year student project done for MSMEs under the supervision of parent Design Institutions. MSME units contribution shall be 25% of the admissible cost.
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: Final year undergraduate, postgraduate, or diploma students in design

quantified_benefits.description: Maximum GoI funding assistance cap per student project
quantified_benefits.source_text: The Design Clinic Scheme shall support design work by reimbursing 75% of expenses incurred subject to Rs. 1.5 lakh for final year student project done for MSMEs under the supervision of parent Design Institutions.

incentive_details.incentive_specific_eligibility: Students in the final year undergoing full-time undergraduate or postgraduate or diploma programs from institutions recognized by the Design Clinic Centre. Beneficiary MSME must contribute 25% of admissible cost.

policy_goals: Enhance industry understanding and application of design and innovation in the MSME manufacturing sector
Promote design as a value-adding activity and integrate it into mainstream business and industrial processes of MSMEs

Help MSME manufacturing industries move up the value chain by switching production mode from original equipment manufacturing (OEM) to original design manufacturing (ODM) and original brand manufacturing (OBM)

Bring Indian manufacturing sector and design expertise onto a common platform to provide expert advice and cost-effective solutions for real-time design problems, resulting in new product development or continuous improvement and value addition
policy_details.policy_summary: The Design Clinic Scheme provides financial assistance and institutional support to Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in the manufacturing sector to access professional design consultancy, create market-led products, and foster continuous innovation. Implemented through the National Institute of Design (NID), Ahmedabad as the Principal Implementing Agency along with other institutes like IISc and CSIR, the scheme operates through two primary components: Design Awareness Programmes (sensitization seminars, 3-5 day diagnostic cluster workshops, and Design Need Assessment surveys) and Design Clinic Project Funding (financial grants for professional design collaborations and final-year student design projects).
policy_details.benefit_headline: Financial grant of up to 75% (max ₹25 lakhs for Micro groups and ₹40 lakhs for SME groups) for professional design consultancy projects and ₹1.5 lakhs for student design projects.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Office of the Development Commissioner (Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises), Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Government of India
special_focus_areas: Original Design Manufacturing (ODM) and Brand Creation

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: Assistance under the scheme will be available for the benefits of micro, small and medium enterprises in the manufacturing segments as per the definition of the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act, 2006 (MSMED Act, 2006). The beneficiary unit(s) must typically be micro, small or medium enterprises as per the definition in MSMED Act 2006. It must be new to using design and preferably should not have used internal or external design expertise before. The MSME should be a profitable entity in the last 3 years of its operations. The MSME must demonstrate either an export performance or potential to export. The Industrial designer/ design company / academic institution and the applicant MSME have to be bodies or companies established or incorporated in India under the Indian Laws with on-going business.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: The applicant design company/academic institution and the applicant MSME in a project application must not be an associate or associated person or agent or employee of the other before submission of the application. The project team members representing the designer/design company/academic institution must not be directors, shareholders, or management team members of the applicant MSME. Double subvention from other public funding sources is not allowed.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Entrepreneur Memorandum Part-II (EM-II) / MSME Registration under MSMED Act, 2006.

incentive_details.description: Government assistance of 75% of the cost for organizing focused 3-5 day design workshops and diagnostic Design Need Assessment surveys in industrial clusters.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: 75% GoI contribution up to ₹3.75 Lakhs for 3-5 day cluster workshops and diagnostic design need assessment surveys.
incentive_details.application_process: Proposals submitted to Design Clinic Centre with prior approval of PMAC; executed in coordination with MSME-DIs.

quantified_benefits.conditions: Maximum admissible cost is ₹5,00,000. Balance ₹1,25,000 contributed by participating MSMEs/implementing agency. Released in 2 tranches (50% upfront, 50% post-completion against audited expenditure).
quantified_benefits.description: GoI contribution for workshop conduct and Design Need Assessment Survey Report preparation.
quantified_benefits.source_text: The GoI contribution for the conduct of a workshop (including preparation of the Design Need Assessment Survey Report) will be to the extent of 75 percent of the cost incurred, the admissible cost being restricted to Rs. 5,00,000/- (Rs. Five Lakh Only), (i.e. maximum assistance being restricted to Rs. 3,75,000/- only). The remaining amount of Rs. 1,25,000/- will be contributed by the participating MSMEs/implementing agency.
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: Participating MSME clusters and organizing agencies

incentive_details.application_authority: Project Monitoring and Advisory Committee (PMAC) / NID
incentive_details.incentive_specific_eligibility: Requires participation and matching contribution from cluster MSMEs.

policy_name: Up-scaled Design Clinic Scheme for Design Expertise to MSME Manufacturing Sector
incentive_name: Study / Exposure of Global Best Practices and Design Clinic Programme of Other Countries

policy_goals: Enhance industry understanding and application of design and innovation
Promote design as a value adding activity and integrate it into mainstream business and industrial processes of MSMEs

Help MSME manufacturing industries move up the value chain by switching the production mode from original equipment manufacturing to original design manufacturing and hence original brand manufacturing

Bring Indian manufacturing sector and design expertise on to a common platform to provide expert advice and cost effective solutions on real time design problems, resulting in new product development or continuous improvement and value addition for existing products
policy_details.policy_summary: The Up-scaled Design Clinic Scheme is a component under the National Manufacturing Competitiveness Programme (NMCP) implemented by the Ministry of MSME through the National Institute of Design (NID), Ahmedabad as the Principal Implementing Agency (along with IISc and CSIR). The scheme aims to enhance design capability and competitiveness of MSME manufacturing units. It consists of two major parts: Design Awareness Programmes (seminars, workshops, diagnostic need assessment surveys, and orientation programs) and Design Clinic Projects (collaborative project funding for professional design interventions and student design projects). The total scheme budget is Rs. 149.00 crore, of which Rs. 110.64 crore is Government of India assistance and the balance is contributed by beneficiary MSMEs.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to 75% grant assistance up to ₹25 lakhs for Micro units and 60% up to ₹40 lakhs for SME units for professional design projects, plus up to ₹1.5 lakhs (75%) for student design projects.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Office of Development Commissioner (MSME), Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Government of India
special_focus_areas: Product design and innovation in manufacturing MSMEs
Switching from OEM to Original Design Manufacturing (ODM) and Original Brand Manufacturing (OBM)

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: Assistance under the scheme will be available for the benefits of micro, small and medium enterprises in the manufacturing segments as per the definition of the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act, 2006 (MSMED Act, 2006). The beneficiary unit(s) must typically be micro, small or medium enterprises as per the definition in MSMED Act 2006. It must be new to using design and preferably should not have used internal or external design expertise before. The designer that a unit employs in this scheme should be selected from a pool of qualified Industrial designers empanelled for this scheme. A copy of EM-II shall also be enclosed with proposed Design projects before submitting to the PMAC. Following are the criteria for qualifying the applicant MSME under Design Clinic: The MSME should be a profitable entity in the last 3 years of its operations; The MSME must demonstrate either an export performance or potential to export; PMAC can stipulate/relax criteria for this purpose. The local Industrial designer/ Design Company / academic institution and the local MSME in collaboration are eligible to apply for funding support as co-applicants. Both entities have to be bodies or companies established or incorporated in India under Indian Laws with on-going business.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: The applicant design company/academic institution and the applicant MSME must not be an associate or associated person or agent or employee of the other before submission of the application. Project team members representing the designer/institution must not be directors, shareholders, or management team members of the applicant MSME. Double subvention from other public funding sources is not allowed.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Entrepreneur Memorandum Part-II (EM-II) registration under MSMED Act, 2006

incentive_details.description: Support for international exposure visits for MSME beneficiaries, implementing agency members, and Ministry of MSME officials to study best design practices abroad.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: GoI contribution of ₹50.00 lakhs for each international study tour with a minimum delegation of 20 MSME participants.
incentive_details.application_process: Organized through coordinating agencies with approval of PMAC.

quantified_benefits.description: GoI contribution per international study visit
quantified_benefits.source_text: A provision has been made for organizing 6 nos. of study of global best practices and Design Clinic Programme of other Countries with GoI contribution of Rs. 50.00 lakh ( Rs. Fifty Lakh Only) each.
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: Delegations comprising MSME beneficiaries and officials

incentive_details.incentive_specific_eligibility: Delegation of minimum 20 participants from MSME units, one member from coordinating agency, and two officers from O/o DC(MSME).

policy_name: Building Awareness on Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
incentive_name: Assistance for Setting up IP Facilitation Centre (IPFC) for MSME

policy_goals: To enhance the awareness of Intellectual Property Rights (IPRs) amongst the MSMEs to encourage creative intellectual endeavour in the Indian economy
To take suitable measures for the protection of ideas, technological innovation and knowledge-driven business strategies developed by MSMEs
To provide appropriate facilities and support for protection and commercialization of Intellectual Property (IP) for the benefit of the MSME sector
To assist SMEs in effective utilization of IPR tools for technology up-gradation, market and business promotion, and competitiveness enhancement
policy_details.policy_summary: The Scheme for Building Awareness on Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) for MSMEs, implemented under the National Manufacturing Competitiveness Programme by the Ministry of MSME, aims to enhance IPR awareness, facilitate IP registration, and protect innovative concepts. Key interventions include financial reimbursements for domestic and foreign patent grants, trademark registrations, and GI registrations; grants-in-aid of up to Rs. 100 Lakhs over five years for establishing IP Facilitation Centres (IPFCs); and financial assistance for pilot studies, sensitization programmes, interactive seminars, specialized capacity-building training, and international agency collaborations.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to ₹5 lakh reimbursement for foreign patents, ₹1 lakh for domestic patents, and ₹100 lakh grant for establishing IP Facilitation Centres.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Office of Development Commissioner (MSME), Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Government of India

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: For Patent, Geographical Indication and Trademark Reimbursement: For reimbursement of actual costs or expenses incurred towards registration of Patents or Trademarks, from the Office of Development Commissioner (MSME), Ministry of MSME, Government of India, the applicant/entity/unit must have a valid Udyog Aadhar/UAM and registered at MSME-Data bank. Patents/Trademarks filed/registered in the name of individuals are also eligible for reimbursement subject to holding a valid Udyog Aadhar/UAM. For reimbursement of actual costs or expenses incurred towards registration of GI, the agency, institutions, associations, Institutes, non-profit bodies, NGOs, societies, trusts, or similar other non-commercial bodies, other entity which might not have Udyog Aadhar, should provide relevant incorporation/establishment documents, PAN number of entity. For IPFC and other activities: MSME Development Institutes, Technology Centres, Quasi-Government/Government Bodies/Departments/Autonomous Organisations, MSME Industry Associations, Societies/Cooperatives/Firms/Trusts, NGOs representing or working for MSMEs, Research/Technical & Educational Institutions, Universities/colleges with a track record of assisting MSMEs.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Government assistance is only for organisational expenses and eligible reimbursement costs; it cannot be used for meeting previous liabilities or debts, or capital assets like equipment/construction unless explicitly sanctioned.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Implementing agencies for centres and activities must contribute at least 10% of the total project cost from their own or other sources, except for MSME-DIs / Branch DIs where no contribution is required.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Valid Udyog Aadhaar Memorandum (UAM) / Udyam Registration and registration at MSME Databank (for units and individuals claiming Patent/Trademark reimbursement); or relevant incorporation documents and PAN (for GI applicants).
special_category_benefits: Efforts will be made to encourage SC, ST, OBC, PH, Women & Minority categories of MSMEs, while organising programmes.

incentive_details.description: Grant-in-aid support for establishing IP Facilitation Centres to provide search/mapping, IP filing assistance, commercialization support, and legal guidance to MSMEs.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: Financial grant-in-aid of up to ₹100 Lakhs spread over 5 years for setting up an IP Facilitation Centre.
incentive_details.application_process: Proposals must be submitted through the online MSME portal (my.msme.gov.in) and are appraised and approved by the PMAC.

quantified_benefits.conditions: Implementing agency must contribute at least 10% of total project cost (except MSME-DIs). Assets and operations must become self-sustainable after 5 years.
quantified_benefits.description: Total grant-in-aid support for establishing an approved IP Facilitation Centre spread over 5 years
quantified_benefits.source_text: The Government of India will provide a total financial grant-in-aid support of maximum up to Rs. 100 Lakhs (Indian Rupees one Hundred Lakhs) to each approved centre; the grant for establishing these centres will be spread over a period of five (5) years.
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: Approved implementing agencies (MSME-DIs, Technology Centres, Universities, Industry Associations, etc.)

incentive_details.application_authority: Project Monitoring and Advisory Committee (PMAC), O/o DC (MSME)
incentive_details.incentive_specific_eligibility: Eligible agencies include MSME-DIs, Technology Centres, Government/Autonomous Bodies, Industry Associations, Societies, Cooperatives, Trusts, Technical & Educational Institutions, and Universities with a track record of assisting MSMEs.

incentive_details.application_process: Application via online portal my.msme.gov.in.

quantified_benefits.description: Funding provision for organizing sensitization and awareness programmes
quantified_benefits.source_text: Funding Provision of Rs. 70000/- (Indian Rupees seventy thousands) per programme is being provided for organizing these sensitization/awareness programmes under the scheme.

policy_name: Building Awareness on Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
incentive_name: Support for Interactive Seminars, Workshops, Conclaves, and Conferences

policy_goals: To enhance the awareness of Intellectual Property Rights (IPRs) amongst the MSMEs to encourage creative intellectual endeavour in the Indian economy
To take suitable measures for the protection of ideas, technological innovation and knowledge-driven business strategies developed by MSMEs
To provide appropriate facilities and support for protection and commercialization of Intellectual Property (IP) for the benefit of the MSME sector
To assist SMEs in effective utilization of IPR tools for technology up-gradation, market and business promotion, and competitiveness enhancement
policy_details.policy_summary: The Scheme for Building Awareness on Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) for MSMEs, implemented under the National Manufacturing Competitiveness Programme by the Ministry of MSME, aims to enhance IPR awareness, facilitate IP registration, and protect innovative concepts. Key interventions include financial reimbursements for domestic and foreign patent grants, trademark registrations, and GI registrations; grants-in-aid of up to Rs. 100 Lakhs over five years for establishing IP Facilitation Centres (IPFCs); and financial assistance for pilot studies, sensitization programmes, interactive seminars, specialized capacity-building training, and international agency collaborations.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to ₹5 lakh reimbursement for foreign patents, ₹1 lakh for domestic patents, and ₹100 lakh grant for establishing IP Facilitation Centres.

Patents/Trademarks filed/registered in the name of individuals are also eligible for reimbursement subject to holding a valid Udyog Aadhar/UAM. policy_name: Digital MSME - Scheme for Promotion of Information and Communication Technology (ICT) in MSME Sector
incentive_name: Cloud Computing Services at Ultra Low Cost (Non-Subsidy Category)

policy_goals: Carry out diagnostic mapping of potential clusters and motivate MSMEs to adopt ICT tools and applications for their production and business processes
Improve competitiveness of MSMEs in national and international markets and enhance export potential
Standardize business processes, reduce delivery cycle time, lower inventory carrying costs, and improve productivity and quality
Promote an ecosystem of cost-effective and all-inclusive ICT applications for MSMEs through cloud computing and common e-Readiness Centres
Enable MSMEs to access markets and value chains through B2B interactions, e-catalogues, and national portals
policy_details.policy_summary: Digital MSME is the modified ICT promotion scheme under NMCP that shifts the model from CAPEX (in-house infrastructure) to OPEX through Cloud Computing. The scheme provides subsidies on cloud user/subscription charges for two years for common business applications (Mini ERP, Accounting, Manufacturing/Design, and Compliances). Subsidies are offered at 60% for general category MSEs and 70% for special categories (NER, SC/ST, Women, Divyang), with a maximum subsidy of Rs. 1 lakh per unit over two years disbursed via Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT). Cloud services without subsidy at ultra-low cost are also made available to all MSMEs.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to 60% to 70% subsidy (up to Rs. 1 lakh per unit over 2 years) on cloud computing subscription and user charges for Micro and Small Enterprises.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Office of the Development Commissioner (Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises), Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Government of India

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: The Scheme is open to only Micro and Small Enterprises for subsidy category and for all Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises for non-subsidy category throughout the country. The units should have valid UAM.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Valid Udyog Aadhaar Memorandum (UAM).
special_category_benefits: Micro and Small Enterprises belonging to NER, SC/ST, Women, and Divyang receive an additional 10% subsidy over the standard rate (total 70% subsidy) up to Rs. 1.00 lakh per unit.

incentive_details.description: Provision of enterprise cloud computing services negotiated at ultra-low utility rates for MSMEs that do not qualify for or opt out of the subsidy window.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: Access to enterprise-grade cloud tools (ERP, accounting, design, compliance) at negotiated ultra-low tariff rates.
incentive_details.application_process: Open registration on National MSME Cloud Portal.

quantified_benefits.description: Pay-as-you-use cloud services offered at ultra-low cost without upfront CAPEX investment.
quantified_benefits.source_text: Without Subsidy - Services through Cloud at ultra low cost will be offered to the desirous Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises.
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: All Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises

policy_name: Marketing Assistance and Technology Up-gradation (MATU) Scheme
incentive_name: Assistance for State/District Level Local Exhibitions/Trade Fairs

policy_goals: Encourage manufacturing Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs) in tapping and developing domestic and overseas markets
Encourage adoption of bar coding on products to increase marketability in national and international markets
Facilitate marketing linkages in view of Public Procurement Policy for MSEs Order 2012
Create consciousness and educate MSMEs on modern packaging technology, import-export procedures, and international trade developments
Support skill upgradation on modern marketing techniques, e-marketing, and branding
Enhance competitiveness through corporate governance and quality certification adoption (ISO 18000/22000/27000)
policy_details.policy_summary: The Marketing Assistance & Technology Up-gradation (MATU) Scheme provides institutional and financial support to manufacturing Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises to address information asymmetries, lack of marketing resources, and competition. The scheme provides financial assistance for participation in domestic and international trade fairs/exhibitions, adoption of bar coding through GS1 India, vendor development programmes for linkages with CPSUs, packaging upgradation, competition studies, corporate governance adoption, setting up MSME marketing hubs, and reimbursement for obtaining specialized ISO certifications (ISO 18000/22000/27000).
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to 100% reimbursement on stall rent and airfare for trade fairs, 75% subsidy for GS1 bar coding and ISO certifications, and up to ₹45,000 for corporate governance adoption.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Office of the Development Commissioner (MSME), Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Government of India

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: The applicant Micro/Small Enterprise should suitably be registered through EM part II/Udyog Aadhaar Memorandum (UAM) for availing financial benefits. Assistance under the scheme will be available for the benefits of micro, small and medium enterprises in the manufacturing segments as per the definition of the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act, 2006 (MSMED Act).
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: A person cannot represent more than one MSE in a financial year for international fairs. Units claiming financial assistance from any other Ministry/Department of Government of India or State Government for the same component cannot claim double benefits.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Registration through EM Part II or Udyog Aadhaar Memorandum (UAM). For international exhibitions, ISO 9000/14000 certification is preferable.

incentive_details.description: Reimbursement of space rent and travel fare for manufacturing MSMEs participating in State/District level exhibitions.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: 50% to 80% reimbursement of space and travel charges up to ₹20,000 for general units and ₹30,000 for SC/ST/Women/PH units.

quantified_benefits.description: Space and travel cost reimbursement for General category units
quantified_benefits.source_text: Pavilion/stall/space charges upto 6.0 sq mtr. – 50% cost will be reimbursed by GOI. To and fro actual fare by shortest distance/direct train (limited to AC II tier class) from the nearest railway station /bus fare to place of exhibition for one person- 50% of fare will be reimbursed by GOI... while for the other units the max. limit will be Rs.20,000/- per unit.

quantified_benefits.description: Space and travel cost reimbursement for SC/ST/Women/PH entrepreneurs
quantified_benefits.source_text: For SC/ST/Women/Physically Handicapped entrepreneurs the assistance will be up to 80% for the items (a) & (b) above. The total reimbursement will be max. Rs.30,000/- per unit for the SC/ST/Women/Physically Handicapped entrepreneurs

policy_name: Technology and Quality Upgradation Support to Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (TEQUP)
incentive_name: Assistance for Cluster-Level Energy Audits and Model DPRs

policy_goals: Sensitize the manufacturing MSME sector in India to the use of energy efficient technologies and manufacturing processes to reduce production costs and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions
Enable MSMEs to derive Clean Development Mechanism (CDM) benefits and tradable carbon credits through cluster-based Carbon Credit Aggregation Centres (CCAs)
Improve product quality of MSMEs and encourage global competitiveness through National and International Product Quality Certification
Reduce energy consumption by at least 15% in implementing units through bankable energy efficient projects
policy_details.policy_summary: The TEQUP scheme is a key component of the National Manufacturing Competitiveness Programme (NMCP) with a total budget of Rs. 140.98 crore (including Government of India contribution of Rs. 65.73 crore). It aims to enhance competitiveness in the MSME manufacturing sector through two primary pillars: Energy Efficiency and Product Quality Certification. The scheme supports capacity building and cluster energy audits, provides capital subsidy for implementing Energy Efficient Technologies (EET), funds the establishment of cluster-level Carbon Credit Aggregation Centres (CCAs) to facilitate CDM carbon credit trading, and provides reimbursement subsidies for acquiring national (BIS, BEE) and international (CE, UL, ANSI) product standard certifications.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to 25% capital subsidy (max Rs. 10 lakh) for implementing Energy Efficient Technologies and up to 75% subsidy (up to Rs. 2 lakh) for national/international product quality certification.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Office of the Development Commissioner (Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises), Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Government of India

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: Any MSME unit who has filed an Entrepreneurial Memorandum with the appropriate authority or who has erstwhile DIC registration will be eligible for support under the Scheme. The general eligibility conditions are: (i) The MSME should have been audited for energy consumption and have developed a Detail Project Report on EETs. (ii) The DPR should be prepared by a qualified Energy Manager/Auditor. (iii) Enterprises in the clusters intervened under the Activity 1 or identified by PCRA/BEE or any other expert agency will be given preference for support under this Activity. (iv) The project should primarily focus on energy efficiency for the applicant MSME units and must lead to at least 15% reduction in the energy consumption by the enterprise. For this purpose the baseline and the projected energy consumption reflected in the approved DPR will be taken into consideration. (v) Investments in new plant, machinery and equipments focused towards enhancing energy efficiency shall only be eligible for subsidy under the scheme. All the Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises in the manufacturing sector who have submitted valid Entrepreneur Memoranda (EM) and who are first time applicants for National/International Product Standard Licenses are eligible to apply. Licensing of only one product as per the definition of the relevant standards will be subsidized under the Activity. policy_goals: Enable adoption of modern marketing techniques and technology upgradation by MSMEs consistent with global market requirements
Enhance marketing capabilities and competitiveness of MSMEs against international competition and trade liberalization (WTO/FTAs)
Provide marketing platforms and exposure through participation in state, national, and international trade fairs and exhibitions
Facilitate vendor development, business-to-business (B2B) networking, and interaction with large institutional buyers
Support quality improvement, modern packaging standards, good corporate governance, and international quality certifications
policy_details.policy_summary: Administered by the Ministry of MSME through the National Small Industries Corporation (NSIC), the Marketing Assistance Scheme provides institutional marketing support to micro, small, and medium enterprises. Key components include organizing and participating in international technology exhibitions in foreign countries, domestic trade fairs and exhibitions, the annual Techmart exhibition during IITF, co-sponsoring MSME-focused exhibitions organized by third parties, conducting Buyer-Seller Meets for large institutional and government procurement, running intensive marketing promotion campaigns, and maintaining promotional web portals and trade directories. The scheme provides substantial space rent subsidies, airfare assistance, and freight reimbursements, with preferential slabs for micro enterprises, women, SC/ST, and NER units.

policy_details.policy_summary: Administered by the Ministry of MSME through the National Small Industries Corporation (NSIC), the Marketing Assistance Scheme provides institutional marketing support to micro, small, and medium enterprises. Key components include organizing and participating in international technology exhibitions in foreign countries, domestic trade fairs and exhibitions, the annual Techmart exhibition during IITF, co-sponsoring MSME-focused exhibitions organized by third parties, conducting Buyer-Seller Meets for large institutional and government procurement, running intensive marketing promotion campaigns, and maintaining promotional web portals and trade directories. The scheme provides substantial space rent subsidies, airfare assistance, and freight reimbursements, with preferential slabs for micro enterprises, women, SC/ST, and NER units.

incentive_name: Adoption of Corporate Governance Practices

policy_goals: Enable adoption of modern marketing techniques and technology upgradation by MSMEs consistent with global market requirements
Enhance marketing capabilities and competitiveness of MSMEs against international competition and trade liberalization (WTO/FTAs)
Provide marketing platforms and exposure through participation in state, national, and international trade fairs and exhibitions
Facilitate vendor development, business-to-business (B2B) networking, and interaction with large institutional buyers
Support quality improvement, modern packaging standards, good corporate governance, and international quality certifications
policy_details.policy_summary: Implemented under the National Manufacturing Competitiveness Programme (NMCP) by the Office of the Development Commissioner (DC-MSME), this scheme aims to enhance the competitiveness of manufacturing MSMEs through modern marketing techniques and technology upgradation. It provides financial assistance across eight sub-components: awareness and intervention for packaging technology upgradation, skill development in modern marketing (e-commerce, branding, online marketing), competition studies countering international threats, special exposure and travel reimbursement for North Eastern Region (NER) MSMEs, participation subsidies for state and district-level exhibitions, financial support to adopt corporate governance or Limited Liability Partnership (LLP) structures, establishment of dedicated MSME marketing hubs, and reimbursement for obtaining ISO 18000, ISO 22000, and ISO 27000 certifications.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to 80% GoI financial assistance for packaging, skill development, and domestic exhibitions, and up to ₹1 lakh reimbursement (75%) for ISO certifications.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Government of India

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: Assistance under the scheme will be available for the benefits of micro, small and medium enterprises in the manufacturing segments as per the definition of the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act, 2006 (MSMED Act).
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Non-manufacturing enterprises / non-MSMED Act compliant units.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Valid MSME/SSI status, Entrepreneurs Memorandum (EM) number from State Directorate of Industries/DIC.

incentive_details.description: Reimbursement of legal and consultancy expenses incurred by MSMEs to transform their organizational framework into a corporate or Limited Liability Partnership (LLP) structure.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: Reimbursement of 50% of expenditure up to ₹45,000 per MSME unit for adopting corporate governance or LLP structure.

quantified_benefits.description: Reimbursement of total expenditure towards consultancy and legal/statutory fees for corporate/LLP conversion
quantified_benefits.source_text: The GoI assistance will be in the form of reimbursement up to 50% of the total expenditure subject to max. Rs. 45,000/- per MSME unit, who would acquire company’s structure by adopting corporate governance or Limited liability Partnership (LLP) framework.

policy_name: Incentives and Concessions for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) under Industrial Policy 2020-25
incentive_name: Exemption from Stamp Duty and Concessional Registration Charges

policy_goals: To attract investments worth INR 5 Lakh crore
To create employment opportunities for 20 Lakh people
To reach 3rd position in merchandise exports in the next five years
To maintain an industrial growth rate of 10 per cent per annum
To provide an enabling ecosystem for technology adoption and innovation
policy_details.policy_summary: Introduced by the Government of Karnataka under G.O. No. CI 199 SPI 2018 dated 13.08.2020, this policy aims to accelerate inclusive industrial growth across Karnataka, categorizing taluks into Zone 1, Zone 2, and Zone 3. It provides a comprehensive package of fiscal incentives for MSMEs, including investment promotion subsidies, complete stamp duty exemption, concessional registration charges, land conversion fee reimbursements, power tariff subsidies, interest subsidies on technology loans, quality certification support, and grants for green/sustainable manufacturing interventions.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to 35% investment promotion subsidy on Value of Fixed Assets (VFA), 100% stamp duty exemption, and power subsidies up to ₹1.00/unit for MSMEs in Karnataka.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Commerce & Industries Department, Government of Karnataka

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: Incentives and concessions under this policy will be available to all new and additional investments made during the policy period for establishment of new enterprises and expansion / diversification / modernisation. Primarily available for Manufacturing Enterprises / Industries and specified categories of service enterprises as listed in Annexure 3. Eligible MSMEs shall commence commercial production within 3 years from the date of approval from DLSWCC / SLSWCC or from the date of taking possession of land / building plan approval. Application for sanction of Investment Promotion subsidy must be submitted within one year from the date of commercial production. All new industrial investment projects shall create minimum employment of 70% to Kannadigas on an overall basis and 100% in case of Group D employees.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Enterprises listed in Annexure 4: Breweries & Distilleries (excluding winery & ethanol in sugar industry), Khandasari/jaggery, Photo studios, Photocopying, Fertilizer mixing, Saw mills (excluding particle/fiber boards), Tobacco/Gutka/Beedies, Azoic/Reactive dyes, Firecrackers, Ozone depleting industries, Laundries, standard Brick making, Poultry/hatcheries, Popcorn/ice candy, small Coffee roasting units (<2MT/day), Mobile/computer repair, Cassette recording, Cyanide, Mining & Mining equipment, Lime kiln, Mobile plants (asphalt/concrete), Chrysolite asbestos, Saloons/spas, Hotels/resorts, Vermicompost, Rooftop solar power, LPG bottling, and Bio-fuel supply chain aggregators.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Categorized by taluks into Zone 1 (most industrially backward), Zone 2 (more industrially backward), and Zone 3 (industrially developed areas including Bengaluru Urban and Rural).
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Udyam Registration / GST Act registration for manufacturing eligible products.

incentive_details.description: 100% exemption from payment of stamp duty on loan agreements, credit deeds, mortgage deeds, lease deeds, and sale deeds for land/sheds purchased or leased in industrial areas or under Section 109 KLR Act.

policy_details.policy_summary: Policy framework supporting private developers in establishing integrated, multi-sectoral, or logistics industrial parks and flatted factories across Karnataka. It provides capital subsidies on building and infrastructure facilities, complete stamp duty exemption, and dedicated capital subsidies for common effluent and sewage treatment plants.
policy_details.benefit_headline: 5% investment promotion subsidy on infrastructure, 100% stamp duty exemption, and up to ₹5 crore CETP subsidy for private industrial park developers.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Commerce & Industries Department, Government of Karnataka

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: Government proposes to encourage establishment of industrial areas and estates in the State either by private investors or through PPP mode. Minimum acreage requirements: Knowledge Based Industries / Flatted Factories: 5 Acres; Logistics: 50 Acres; Multi / Sector Specific Industrial Parks: 75 Acres; Integrated Industrial Parks: 250 Acres. Approval by SHLCC / SLSWCC required.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: All Zones across Karnataka.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Approval from SLSWCC or SHLCC; layout approval from KIADB.

incentive_details.description: Financial assistance for creating environment and pollution control infrastructure within private industrial parks.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: 50% capital subsidy up to ₹5 crore for CETPs and up to ₹1 crore for STPs.

quantified_benefits.description: Subsidy for CETP / Industrial Hazardous Waste disposal project
quantified_benefits.source_text: One-time capital subsidy up to 50% of the cost of Common Effluent Treatment Plant (CETP) subject to a ceiling of INR 500 Lakh in all Zones.

quantified_benefits.description: Subsidy for Secondary Treatment Plants (STP)
quantified_benefits.source_text: One-time capital subsidy up to 50% of the cost of Secondary Treatment Plants (STPs), subject to a ceiling of INR 1.00 crore in all Zones.

policy_details.policy_summary: Comprehensive set of sector-specific and innovation-driven incentives outlined in Sections 9.4, 9.5, and 9.6 of the Industrial Policy 2020-25. It provides dedicated financial assistance for clinical trials, pharma parks, medical device parks, patent registration, establishment of IP cells, R&D centers, Industry 4.0 direct digital manufacturing, and vocational training/skilling initiatives.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to ₹5 crore subsidy for Pharma/Medical Device Parks, ₹1 crore for clinical trials, ₹5 crore for R&D centers, and ₹100 crore for Industry 4.0 CoE.

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: Eligible industrial enterprises in designated focus sectors (Automotive, Pharma, Medical Devices, Machine Tools, Electronics, Export Industries) approved by DLSWCC/SLSWCC/SHLCC. Exporters must export >50% of production. Clinical trials must be for bio-availability and bio-equivalence in Zones 1 and 2.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Zones 1 and 2 for Pharma Parks and Clinical Trials; all Zones for Medical Device Parks, Industry 4.0, R&D, and IPR.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: IEC for export benefits; recognized trade body / university affiliation for IP cells; regulatory compliance for clinical trials.

incentive_details.description: 50% capital subsidy on equipment and machinery for exclusive R&D centers supporting MSMEs, limited to the first 3 centers in Automotive, Pharma, Medical Devices, and Machine Tools.

quantified_benefits.description: R&D center equipment subsidy
quantified_benefits.source_text: Exclusive R&D centers coming up in all Zones through industry / industry associations supporting MSMEs will be eligible for a 50% subsidy on equipment/ machinery limited to INR 500.00 Lakh.
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: Industry Associations / Consortia (first 3 R&D centers per sector)

policy_name: New Textile and Garment Policy 2019-24
incentive_name: Brownfield Cluster Development

policy_goals: Attract investments worth INR 10,000 crore in the textile and garment sector over the 5-year period (2019 to 2024)
Generate 5,00,000 new employment opportunities across the state over the policy period
Retain Karnataka's pre-eminent position as the Garment Capital of India and transform the textile value chain into a gold mine value chain
Accelerate growth and increase manufacturing cost competitiveness across the entire value chain from fiber to fashion products
Focus on thrust sectors: spinning, weaving (rapier loom, air jet looms, and electronic jacquard), integrated units, processing, and technical textiles
Make Karnataka a skill-rich state in each segment of the textile value chain with high-tech advanced skilling centres
Realize 'Zero Defects; Zero Effect' manufacturing and promote Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) technologies
Increase handloom exports and support designing, product diversification, branding, marketing, and distribution into distinct international markets
Position Karnataka as a significant manufacturing hub and net exporter of Technical Textiles
policy_details.policy_summary: The New Textile and Garment Policy 2019-24 issued by the Government of Karnataka provides a comprehensive incentive and concession framework designed to attract INR 10,000 crore in investments and generate 5 lakh jobs. It covers the entire textile and garment value chain including ginning, spinning, weaving, processing, integrated units, garmenting, technical textiles, handlooms, silk, and wool. Benefits include credit-linked capital subsidies up to 30%, interest subsidies of 5% per annum for large enterprises, subsidized power tariffs, employer ESI/EPF reimbursements up to 75%, wage subsidies for garment manufacturing up to INR 1,500/employee/month, 100% stamp duty exemptions, infrastructure grants for Greenfield/Brownfield parks and CETPs up to INR 40 crore, and extensive capacity building and training support across four classified zones.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to 30% capital subsidy, 5% interest subvention, INR 1,500/month garment wage subsidy, and 100% stamp duty exemption across Karnataka.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Commerce & Industries Department, Government of Karnataka

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: The Textile and Garment industry to be covered under this policy will include all units, which are engaged in various value chain activities of the industry such as Spinning, Weaving (Power loom and Handloom) including pre loom activities, Knitting, Processing, Integrated Units, Garmenting, Technical Textiles, Textile machinery manufacturing and all other ancillary activities. Enterprise classified as micro, small, medium (MSME), large, mega and anchor units during the policy period have been defined separately for textiles and garments. New Project shall mean unit which undertake to invest on fixed assets on or after the announcement of this Policy. Existing Project: Any project existing prior to the announcement of this policy and any project coming under expansion / diversification / modernization during the period of this policy. Zonal classification: Zone 1: Entire Kalyana Karnataka Region; Zone 2: All areas other than Municipal Corporations, District Headquarters in Non Kalyana Karnataka region; Zone 3: All Municipal Corporations and District Headquarters in Non Kalyana Karnataka region; Zone 4: Bangalore Urban & Bangalore Rural Districts.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Zone 4 (Bangalore Urban & Bangalore Rural Districts) is ineligible for capital subsidies, interest subsidies, power subsidies, wage subsidies, and stamp duty concessions under this policy.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Anchor units require a minimum investment of INR 100 crore with 200 direct employees (Textiles) or INR 50 crore with 1000 direct employees (Garments) as the first of their kind in a taluka where no other unit exists. Total incentives drawn across provisions capped at 40% of FCI in Non-Kalyana Karnataka and 50% of FCI in Kalyana Karnataka (with extra 5% allowances for thrust sectors, anchor units, and SC/ST/minority/women/disabled/ex-servicemen).
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Classified into 4 zones: Zone 1 (Kalyana Karnataka), Zone 2 (Non-Kalyana Karnataka excluding Municipal Corporations/District HQs), Zone 3 (Municipal Corporations and District HQs in Non-Kalyana Karnataka), and Zone 4 (Bangalore Urban and Rural).

parent_policy_name: Performance & Credit Rating Scheme for Small Industries
policy_name: Performance & Credit Rating Scheme for Small Industries
incentive_name: Rating Fee Reimbursement / Subsidy

policy_goals: Create awareness amongst Small-Scale Units about the strengths and weaknesses of their existing operations and provide them an opportunity to enhance their organizational strengths
Encourage SSI sector in improving its contribution to the economy by way of increasing their productivity
Enhance market acceptability of SSI units and make access to credit quicker and cheaper, helping economize the cost of credit
Infuse a sense of confidence amongst buyers for taking decisions on sourcing material from Small Scale Units
policy_details.policy_summary: The Performance & Credit Rating Scheme for Small Industries formulated by the Ministry of Small Scale Industries and implemented via NSIC provides a mechanism for SSI units to obtain independent performance and credit ratings from empanelled rating agencies (such as CRISIL, ICRA, Dun & Bradstreet, ONICRA). The rating methodology evaluates creditworthiness alongside operational, financial, business, and management risks to output a standardized rating prefixing NSIC (e.g., NSIC-ICRA). To encourage adoption, the Ministry reimburses 75% of the rating fee up to prescribed turnover-based caps ranging from Rs. 25,000 to Rs. 40,000. Rating validity is one year from issue.
policy_details.benefit_headline: 75% reimbursement of rating agency fees up to Rs. 40,000 based on turnover slabs for Small Scale Industries.
policy_details.issuing_authority: National Small Industries Corporation (NSIC), Ministry of Small Scale Industries, Government of India

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: The Small Scale Sector occupies an important position in any developing economy the world over... The scheme is titled: PERFORMANCE & CREDIT RATING SCHEME FOR SMALL INDUSTRIES... The Small Scale Unit shall be at liberty to select any of the rating agencies empanelled under the rating scheme with NSIC. The fee to be paid to the rating agencies shall be based on the turnover of the Small-Scale Units which has been categorized into three slabs: Up to Rs.50 lacs, Above Rs.50 lacs to Rs.200 lacs, and Above Rs.200 lacs.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Eligible units must be Small Scale Industries (SSI units) applying to NSIC or empanelled rating agencies in duplicate with required documents. The applicant unit must bear the balance fee (25% plus any excess over the cap) alongside the application.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Small Scale Industry (SSI) registration

incentive_details.description: Reimbursement of 75% of the fee charged by the empanelled rating agency, subject to a prescribed ceiling based on the turnover of the Small Scale Unit. The portion of the fee subsidized by the Ministry is released through NSIC after submission of the Rating Report to NSIC by the Rating Agency. The applicant SSI unit pays its contribution along with the application via pay order/demand draft.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: 75% fee reimbursement up to Rs. 40,000 for obtaining NSIC performance and credit rating.
incentive_details.application_process: The SSI unit submits an application in duplicate to any NSIC office/branch or directly to the chosen empanelled rating agency, along with prescribed documents and its fee contribution (pay order/DD in favour of the rating agency). NSIC forwards a copy to the rating agency or vice versa. The rating agency peruses documents within 15 days, requests shortfall information if any, conducts an onsite meeting with SSI management, and assigns the rating within one month of receiving all information.
