policy_name: Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY)
incentive_name: Governmental Financial Assistance for Beneficiary-Oriented Activities (CSS)

policy_goals: Enhance fish production from 13.75 million metric tons (2018-19) to 22 million metric tons by 2024-25
Achieve a sustained average annual growth rate of about 9% in fish production
Increase the contribution of GVA of fisheries sector to Agriculture GVA from 7.28% in 2018-19 to about 9% by 2024-25
Double export earnings from Rs. 46,589 crores (2018-19) to about Rs. 1,00,000 crores by 2024-25
Enhance aquaculture productivity from 3 tonnes to about 5 tonnes per hectare
Reduce post-harvest losses from 20-25% to about 10%
Double the incomes of fishers and fish farmers
Generate about 55 lakhs gainful employment opportunities (15 lakhs direct and 40 lakhs indirect)
Enhance domestic fish consumption from about 5 kg to about 12 kg per capita
Facilitate private investment and growth of entrepreneurship in the fisheries sector
policy_details.policy_summary: Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) is a flagship umbrella scheme launched in May 2020 with an estimated investment of Rs. 20,050 crores to bring about a Blue Revolution through sustainable and responsible development of the fisheries sector in India. It consists of two components: Central Sector Scheme (CS) and Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS). The scheme covers enhancement of production and productivity, modernizing infrastructure and post-harvest management, cold chains, market access, technology infusion (Biofloc, RAS, Aquaponics), deep-sea fishing vessel support, disease management, regulatory frameworks, insurance coverage for fishers and vessels, and social security during fishing ban/lean periods.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to 40% capital subsidy for General category and 60% for SC/ST/Women beneficiaries across fisheries and aquaculture projects with total investment of ₹20,050 crores.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India
special_focus_areas: Women-led enterprises and fisherwomen self-help groups
Aspirational Districts and Left Wing Extremism affected areas

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: The intended beneficiaries under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana are: (i) Fishers, (ii) Fish farmers, (iii) Fish workers and Fish vendors, (iv) Fisheries Development corporations, (v) Self Help Groups (SHGs)/Joint Liability Groups (JLGs) in fisheries sector, (vi) Fisheries cooperatives, (vii) Fisheries Federations, (viii) Entrepreneurs and private firms, (ix) Fish Farmers Producer Organizations/Companies (FFPOs/Cs), (x) SCs/STs/Women/Differently abled persons, (xi) State Governments/UTs and their entities including (xii) State Fisheries Development Boards (SFDB), (xiii) Central Government and its entities. Upper ceiling on area eligible for support in case of individual beneficiary projects/activities will be 2 hectares per beneficiary. In case of groups of fishers and fish farmers (SHGs, JLGs, Cooperatives), the upper ceiling is restricted to 2 ha multiplied by the number of members of the group with a ceiling of 20 ha per group/society.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Applicants who have already availed subsidies or governmental financial assistance for the same activity under any other Central or State Government scheme/agency are not eligible.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Land required for projects must be owned or on registered lease for not less than 10 years for infrastructure projects and not less than 7 years for non-infrastructure projects. Necessary statutory clearances and licenses must be obtained.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: All States and Union Territories across India. Special differential unit costs and higher central shares are applicable for North Eastern & Himalayan States and UTs.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Registration under ReALCraft and valid fishing license for marine fishing vessel activities; Biometric ID / QR coded Aadhaar card for fishers.

incentive_details.description: Financial assistance provided for individual or group beneficiary-oriented activities under Centrally Sponsored Scheme components covering aquaculture, hatcheries, rearing ponds, biofloc, RAS, cages, cold chain, marketing infrastructure, transport, and deep sea fishing vessels.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: 40% subsidy for General category and 60% subsidy for SC/ST/Women beneficiaries on approved unit costs.
incentive_details.application_process: Submission of Detailed Project Report (DPR) or Self Contained Proposal (SCP) approved by District Level Committee (DLC) and State Level Approval and Monitoring Committee (SLAMC) to NFDB and Department of Fisheries (DoF).

quantified_benefits.source_text: the Government financial assistance of both Centre and State/UTs governments together will be limited to 40% of the project/unit cost for General category and 60% of the project/unit cost for SC/ST/Women.

quantified_benefits.source_text: the Government financial assistance of both Centre and State/UTs governments together will be limited to 40% of the project/unit cost for General category and 60% of the project/unit cost for SC/ST/Women.

incentive_details.incentive_specific_eligibility: Beneficiary must submit land ownership or registered lease agreement of minimum 7 to 10 years, and bank consent or self-declaration for funding non-subsidy component.

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: The intended beneficiaries under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana are: (i) Fishers, (ii) Fish farmers, (iii) Fish workers and Fish vendors, (iv) Fisheries Development corporations, (v) Self Help Groups (SHGs)/Joint Liability Groups (JLGs) in fisheries sector, (vi) Fisheries cooperatives, (vii) Fisheries Federations, (viii) Entrepreneurs and private firms, (ix) Fish Farmers Producer Organizations/Companies (FFPOs/Cs), (x) SCs/STs/Women/Differently abled persons, (xi) State Governments/UTs and their entities including (xii) State Fisheries Development Boards (SFDB), (xiii) Central Government and its entities. Upper ceiling on area eligible for support in case of individual beneficiary projects/activities will be 2 hectares per beneficiary. In case of groups of fishers and fish farmers (SHGs, JLGs, Cooperatives), the upper ceiling is restricted to 2 ha multiplied by the number of members of the group with a ceiling of 20 ha per group/society.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Applicants who have already availed subsidies or governmental financial assistance for the same activity under any other Central or State Government scheme/agency are not eligible.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Land required for projects must be owned or on registered lease for not less than 10 years for infrastructure projects and not less than 7 years for non-infrastructure projects. Necessary statutory clearances and licenses must be obtained.

policy_name: Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY)
incentive_name: Collateral-Free Credit Guarantee & Lending Security Exemption

policy_goals: Funding the unfunded by extending formal financial and credit support to non-corporate small businesses and micro-enterprises
Attaining inclusive and sustainable growth by nurturing an ecosystem of micro-enterprises in rural and interior regions
Providing collateral-free credit to prevent exploitation and debt-traps caused by informal moneylenders
Achieving a credit disbursement target of Rs. 1,22,188 crore for banks and financial institutions during FY 2015-16
policy_details.policy_summary: Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY), launched on 8th April 2015, is designed to extend formal institutional credit for non-farm, income-generating activities to micro and small business units up to Rs. 10 lakhs. Delivered through Banks, NBFCs, and MFIs via MUDRA refinance and supported by a Credit Guarantee Scheme, the loans are categorized into three development stages: Shishu (up to Rs. 50,000), Kishor (Rs. 50,000 to Rs. 5 lakhs), and Tarun (Rs. 5 lakhs to Rs. 10 lakhs). In line with RBI mandates, loans up to Rs. 10 lakhs require no collateral security, and borrowers can access working capital conveniently via the MUDRA Card debit card alongside an overdraft facility of Rs. 5,000.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Collateral-free institutional micro-finance loans up to Rs. 10 lakhs under Shishu, Kishor, and Tarun categories with MUDRA Card facility.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Government of India
special_focus_areas: Youth entrepreneurs (up to 30 years of age)
Shopkeepers, artisans, street vendors, and small transport operators

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: The scheme includes all loans to finance micro enterprises by banks/financial institutions for income generating and non-farm activities upto Rs. 10 lakhs. ... The category of persons covering shopkeepers, fruits/vegetable vendors, taxi operators, food-service units, repair shops, machine operators, artisans, food processors, street vendors etc. There is special encouragement for first time entrepreneurs, youth (upto the age of 30 years) and women entrepreneurs.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Farm/agricultural activities (the scheme covers non-farm activities only)
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Loans must be used for income-generating non-farm micro and small business activities such as trading, manufacturing, retail, and allied small-scale activities.
special_category_benefits: Youth (up to the age of 30 years)

incentive_details.description: Reserve Bank of India mandate directing lending institutions not to demand collateral security for micro and small enterprise loans up to Rs. 10 lakhs, backed by MUDRA's Credit Guarantee Scheme.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: 100% collateral-free borrowing for MSME loans up to Rs. 10 lakhs.

quantified_benefits.description: Exemption from furnishing collateral security for micro enterprise loans
quantified_benefits.source_text: The Reserve Bank of India has also issued a circular on lending to MSMSE sector which mandates banks not to insist for collateral security in the case of loans upto Rs. 10.00 lakh extended to these units.
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: All PMMY loan applicants up to Rs. 10 lakhs

policy_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) - 2nd Loan for Upgradation of Existing PMEGP/REGP/MUDRA Units
incentive_name: Margin Money Subsidy for Upgradation (2nd Loan)

policy_goals: To generate employment opportunities in rural as well as urban areas of the country through setting up of new self-employment ventures/projects/micro enterprises.
To bring together widely dispersed traditional artisans and rural and urban unemployed youth and give them self-employment opportunities to the extent possible, at their place.

To provide continuous and sustainable employment to a large segment of traditional and prospective artisans and rural and urban unemployed youth in the country, so as to help arrest migration of rural youth to urban areas.
To increase the wage-earning capacity of workers and artisans and contribute to increase in the growth rate of rural and urban employment.
To set up about 4 lakh micro enterprises with creation of about 30 lakh jobs over the 15th Finance Commission cycle (2021-22 to 2025-26) with an approved outlay of Rs. 13,554.42 Crore.
policy_details.policy_summary: Under the 15th Finance Commission cycle, PMEGP includes a dedicated provision for expanding and upgrading well-performing existing units previously funded under PMEGP, REGP, or MUDRA. The scheme provides a second credit-linked loan with a uniform 15% government margin money subsidy (20% for NER and Hill States) on project costs up to Rs. 1.00 Crore for manufacturing units and Rs. 25 Lakhs for service/business units.
policy_details.benefit_headline: 15% to 20% margin money subsidy on 2nd loan up to Rs. 1.00 crore for manufacturing and Rs. 25 lakhs for service units.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Government of India

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: 4.2 For up-gradation of existing PMEGP/REGP/MUDRA units: i. Margin Money (subsidy) claimed under PMEGP has to be successfully adjusted on the completion of lock in period of 3 years. ii. First loan under PMEGP/REGP/MUDRA has to be successfully repaid in stipulated time. (COVID years i.e., FY2020-21 and FY2021-22 have been exempted while considering profitability). iii. The unit is profit making with good turnover and having potential for further growth in turnover and profit with modernization/upgrading the technology. Units would be selected uniformly from all over the country, about 10 from each district.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Units that defaulted on first loan or where margin money was not adjusted; units operating activities in the negative list.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: First loan must be fully repaid in stipulated time; unit must be profit making.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: All districts across India (approx. 10 units per district per year).
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Mandatory Udyam Portal registration.

incentive_details.description: Credit-linked margin money subsidy for existing well-performing PMEGP/REGP/MUDRA units seeking modernization or expansion. Government provides a uniform subsidy of 15% (or 20% for units in North Eastern Region and Hill States) with a 10% promoter contribution. Maximum subsidy admissible is Rs. 15 lakh (Rs. 20 lakh for NER/Hill States) for manufacturing and Rs. 3.75 lakh (Rs. 5 lakh for NER/Hill States) for service/business.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: 15% to 20% capital subsidy up to Rs. 20 lakhs for upgrading existing manufacturing units and up to Rs. 5 lakhs for service units.
incentive_details.application_process: Existing unit submits simplified online application through PMEGP e-Portal. Preliminary scrutiny by district agency, forwarded to financing bank for technical and economic appraisal and credit decision. Margin money is deposited in TDR/SRF for 3 years and adjusted following successful third-party verification.

quantified_benefits.conditions: Unit must have successfully repaid first loan and completed 3-year lock-in period.

policy_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) - Setting up of New Micro Enterprises
incentive_name: Collateral-Free Bank Financing Support

policy_goals: To generate employment opportunities in rural as well as urban areas of the country through setting up of new self-employment ventures/projects/micro enterprises.
To bring together widely dispersed traditional artisans and rural and urban unemployed youth and give them self-employment opportunities to the extent possible, at their place.

To provide continuous and sustainable employment to a large segment of traditional and prospective artisans and rural and urban unemployed youth in the country, so as to help arrest migration of rural youth to urban areas.
To increase the wage-earning capacity of workers and artisans and contribute to increase in the growth rate of rural and urban employment.
To set up about 4 lakh micro enterprises with creation of about 30 lakh jobs over the 15th Finance Commission cycle (2021-22 to 2025-26) with an approved outlay of Rs. 13,554.42 Crore.
policy_details.policy_summary: PMEGP is a major central credit-linked subsidy programme administered by the Ministry of MSME and implemented nationally by KVIC. The scheme facilitates credit linked margin money subsidies for setting up new micro-enterprises in non-farm sectors across rural and urban locations. Financial assistance includes bank financing ranging from 90% to 95% of project cost, with government margin money subsidy ranging from 15% to 35% depending on location (urban/rural) and beneficiary category (general/special). Beneficiaries contribute 5% to 10% own equity. Mandatory requirements include online portal application, EDP training, and Udyam portal registration before physical verification and margin money adjustment.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to 35% margin money capital subsidy on project costs up to Rs. 50 lakhs for manufacturing and Rs. 20 lakhs for service units.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Government of India

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: 4.1 For PMEGP new enterprises (Units): (i) Any individual, above 18 years of age. (ii) There will be no income ceiling for assistance for setting up projects under PMEGP. (iii) For setting up of project costing above Rs.10 lakh in the Manufacturing sector and above Rs. 5 lakh in the Business /Service sector, the beneficiaries should possess at least VIII standard pass educational qualification. (iv) Assistance under the scheme is available only for new projects sanctioned specifically under the PMEGP. (v) Existing Units (under PMRY, REGP or any other scheme of Government of India or State Government) and the units that have already availed Government Subsidy under any other scheme of Government of India or State Government are not eligible. Other eligibility conditions: Projects without Capital Expenditure are not eligible. Cost of land not included in project cost; ready built shed/workshop lease or rental cost includible for maximum 3 years. PMEGP is applicable to all new viable microenterprises except activities indicated in negative list. All new units setup under PMEGP will be mandatorily registered under Udyam Portal before Physical Verification of the Unit and the adjustment of Margin Money in beneficiary loan account. Only one person from one family (self and spouse) is eligible.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Existing units (under PMRY, REGP or any other Central/State scheme) or units that have already availed government subsidy; units without capital expenditure; businesses connected with slaughtered meat processing/canning/serving; intoxicants and tobacco manufacturing/sales; hotels/dhabas serving liquor; polythene carry bags under 75 microns; recycled plastic bags for food stuff; cultivation of crops/plantations like tea, coffee, rubber; sericulture, horticulture, floriculture, animal husbandry farming (except allowed value-addition, dairy, poultry, aquaculture, and insects/beekeeping).
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Mandatory completion of EDP training (at least 5 days for projects up to Rs. 5 lakh, at least 10 days for projects above Rs. 5 lakh; exempt for projects up to Rs. 2 lakh or individuals who already underwent at least 10 days/60 hours EDP/SDP/ESDP/VT). Fixed capital investment per head of a full-time worker/artisan not to exceed Rs. 3 lakh in plain areas and Rs. 4.5 lakh in hilly areas/A&N/Lakshadweep.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Rural and urban areas across India. Rural areas defined as revenue village or areas falling under Panchayati Raj Institutions.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Mandatory registration under Udyam Portal before physical verification and margin money adjustment; Aadhaar number authentication.

incentive_details.description: Financing banks provide term loans for capital expenditure and cash credit for working capital. In line with RBI guidelines, no collateral security is insisted upon for loans up to Rs. 10 lakh (enhanced from Rs. 5 lakh). Balance project cost (after subsidy and owner contribution) is funded as bank credit.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: Collateral-free bank financing for project loans up to Rs. 10 lakhs with normal interest rates and repayment over 3 to 7 years.
incentive_details.application_process: Appraised and sanctioned directly by the chosen financing bank following referral from implementing agencies through PMEGP portal.

quantified_benefits.conditions: 3 to 7 years repayment schedule after an initial moratorium.
quantified_benefits.description: Bank loan financing covering project cost balance
quantified_benefits.source_text: The Bank will sanction 90% of the project cost in case of General Category of beneficiary and 95% in case of Special Category of the beneficiary and disburse full amount suitably for setting up of the project.

quantified_benefits.description: Collateral security exemption ceiling
quantified_benefits.source_text: No collateral security will be insisted upon by banks in line with the guidelines of RBI for projects involving loan up to Rs.10 lakh in respect of the projects forwarded to them by the agencies.
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: All eligible projects up to Rs. 10 lakh loan

incentive_details.application_authority: Financing Banks (Public Sector Banks, RRBs, approved Cooperative & Private Commercial Banks, SIDBI)
incentive_details.incentive_specific_eligibility: Loan application sanctioned based on technical and financial viability.

policy_details.policy_summary: PM SVANidhi is a Central Sector Scheme launched on 1 June 2020 by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) in collaboration with the Department of Financial Services (DFS) and SIDBI as the technical implementation partner. The scheme facilitates collateral-free working capital micro-loans to urban, peri-urban, and rural street vendors who were operational on or before 24 March 2020. policy_goals: Enhance the marketability and competitiveness of products and services produced by Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in domestic and international markets
Promote adoption of modern marketing techniques, packaging technologies, bar coding, and corporate governance among MSMEs
Facilitate market linkages and public procurement access through trade fairs, exhibitions, and vendor development programmes
Assist MSMEs in obtaining international quality certifications such as ISO 18000, ISO 22000, and ISO 27000

policy_details.policy_summary: Financial assistance program operated by Office of DC (MSME) to encourage MSEs to adopt international Bar Coding standards through GS1 India. Reimburses 75% of the one-time registration fee (effective 1st January 2002 under SSI-MDA Scheme) and 75% of annual recurring fees for the first three years (effective 1st June 2007 under NMCP Scheme) paid by MSEs to GS1 India. Implementation has been decentralized to field MSME-Development Institutes.
policy_details.benefit_headline: 75% reimbursement of one-time registration fee and annual recurring fee for the first three years paid to GS1 India for Bar Code usage.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Office of the Development Commissioner (Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises), Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Government of India

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: Those MSEs who have Entrepreneurial Memorandum Part-II acknowledgement number from Directorate of Industries/District Industries Centres and also have registration with GS1 India for use of Bar Codes are eligible for 75% reimbursement of one-time registration fee and annual recurring fee (for first three years) paid by them to GS1 India. Further, 75% reimbursement of one-time registration fee paid by MSEs to GS1 India is provided to those MSEs who have got registration from GS1 India for use of Bar-Codes on or after 1st January, 2002. In addition, 75% reimbursement of annual recurring fee paid by MSEs to GS1 India is provided to only those MSEs who have paid above fee for the period from 1st June, 2007 and thereafter.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Any other charges like service taxes, etc. are not reimbursable. Units that have already claimed full reimbursement under another scheme cannot claim again.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Must be functional and in production at the time of Bar Code registration and on the date of application.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Entrepreneur's Memorandum Part-II acknowledgement number from State Directorate of Industries/DICs; Bar Code registration license from GS1 India.

incentive_details.description: Reimbursement of 75% of one-time registration fee paid to GS1 India (on or after 01-01-2002) and 75% of annual recurring fees paid for the first 3 years (for period from 01-06-2007 onwards).

policy_goals: Enhance the marketability and competitiveness of products and services produced by Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in domestic and international markets
Promote adoption of modern marketing techniques, packaging technologies, bar coding, and corporate governance among MSMEs
Facilitate market linkages and public procurement access through trade fairs, exhibitions, and vendor development programmes

policy_details.policy_summary: The Procurement and Marketing Support (PMS) Scheme aims to promote new market access initiatives and capacity building for MSEs. Key components include: (1) Market Access Initiatives: individual MSE participation in domestic trade fairs/exhibitions with up to 100% space rent subsidy and 100% contingency reimbursement (travel/freight) capped at Rs. 1.50 lakh in Metro/Class A cities and Rs. 0.80 lakh in other cities; organizing domestic/international fairs, virtual trade fairs (up to Rs. 16.45 lakh), and CPSE-level Vendor Development Programmes (up to Rs. 5.0 lakh). (2) Capacity Building: cluster-based modern packaging interventions up to Rs. 15 lakh; adoption of Bar Code with 80% reimbursement up to Rs. 50,650 for micro enterprises; adoption of e-commerce through MSME Global Mart with 75% subsidy up to Rs. 25,000; and national workshops/seminars up to Rs. 5.0 lakh. (3) Infrastructure development of Retail Outlets for GI products with grant-in-aid up to Rs. 15 lakh for Metro/A Class cities and Rs. 10 lakh for other cities.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to 100% space rent subsidy and travel/freight contingency support up to Rs. 1.50 lakh for trade fairs, 80% reimbursement for bar coding up to Rs. 50,650, and 50% grant up to Rs. 15 lakh for GI retail outlets.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Office of the Development Commissioner (Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises), Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Government of India

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: Manufacturing / Service sector MSEs having valid Udyam Registration (UR) Certificate. For Bar Code: Micro enterprises which have UDYAM Registration and also have registration with GS1 India for use of Bar Codes. For e-Commerce: Micro Enterprises with valid Udyam Registration. For GI retail outlets: Only the products with valid Geographical Indications (GI) would be sold at such outlets. The seller must have an MoU / agreement with GI holder. For workshops/seminars: Govt. / Non - Govt. reputed organizations having at least 3 years of experience in organizing subject specific workshops / seminars.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Any expenditure exceeding the prescribed caps or on taxes (like service tax/GST on certain items) not admissible.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: An MSE is allowed reimbursement for a maximum of 2 events in a year. Applicant units must submit their claim online in the prescribed format within 30 days from the date of conclusion of the event.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Valid Udyam Registration (UR) Certificate; GS1 India registration for Bar Code; Valid GI holder MoU/agreement for GI retail outlets.

policy_details.policy_summary: The Marketing Assistance and Technology Upgradation Programme under the National Manufacturing Competitiveness Programme (NMCP) was introduced with a total budget of Rs. 23.0 crore to enhance the competitiveness of manufacturing MSMEs. It covers eight major activities: (1) Technology Upgradation in Packaging (awareness programmes of 1 day up to Rs. 0.50 lakh, cluster studies up to Rs. 10 lakh, and unit interventions up to Rs. 9.0 lakh per group of 10 units with 80:20 GoI-unit sharing); (2) Skill Upgradation for Modern Marketing Techniques (training for min 20 persons/50 trainee-days up to Rs. 6.0 lakh per cluster, 80:20 sharing); (3) Competition Studies against international threats (up to Rs. 8.0 lakh per study, 80:20 sharing); (4) Special Component for North-Eastern Region (80% reimbursement up to Rs. 75,000 per unit for stall space up to 6 sq.m, AC II travel, and freight up to Rs. 15,000); (5) State/District Exhibitions (50% reimbursement up to Rs. 20,000 for general units, and 80% up to Rs. 30,000 for SC/ST/Women/PH units); (6) Corporate Governance Practices (50% reimbursement up to Rs. 45,000 per unit); (7) Setting up 8 Marketing Hubs in MSME-DIs (Rs. 30 lakh infra + Rs. 5 lakh equipment + Rs. 15 lakh 2-year opex); (8) Reimbursement of 75% up to Rs. 1.00 lakh for acquiring ISO 18000, ISO 22000, or ISO 27000 certifications.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to 80% GoI financial assistance for packaging upgradation, skill development, and trade fairs, plus 75% reimbursement up to Rs. 1.0 lakh for ISO certifications and 50% up to Rs. 45,000 for corporate governance.

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: Assistance under the scheme will be available for the benefits of micro, small and medium enterprises in the manufacturing segments as per the definition of the Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises Development Act, 2006 (MSMED Act).
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Hotel and travel expenses and surveillance charges for ISO certifications are excluded from reimbursement.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Manufacturing enterprises must hold valid Entrepreneur Memorandum (EM Part-II) or SSI registration. For ISO reimbursement, unit must be functional and in production at the time of certification and submission.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Entrepreneurial Memorandum (EM Part-II) / SSI Registration; ISO 18000/22000/27000 certificate from accredited certifying body.

policy_goals: Enhance the marketability and competitiveness of products and services produced by Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in domestic and international markets
Promote adoption of modern marketing techniques, packaging technologies, bar coding, and corporate governance among MSMEs
Facilitate market linkages and public procurement access through trade fairs, exhibitions, and vendor development programmes
Assist MSMEs in obtaining international quality certifications such as ISO 18000, ISO 22000, and ISO 27000
Support adoption of e-commerce platforms and promote Geographical Indications (GI) products through dedicated retail outlets
policy_details.policy_summary: The Marketing Assistance and Technology Upgradation Programme under the National Manufacturing Competitiveness Programme (NMCP) was introduced with a total budget of Rs. 23.0 crore to enhance the competitiveness of manufacturing MSMEs. It covers eight major activities: (1) Technology Upgradation in Packaging (awareness programmes of 1 day up to Rs. 0.50 lakh, cluster studies up to Rs. 10 lakh, and unit interventions up to Rs. 9.0 lakh per group of 10 units with 80:20 GoI-unit sharing); (2) Skill Upgradation for Modern Marketing Techniques (training for min 20 persons/50 trainee-days up to Rs. 6.0 lakh per cluster, 80:20 sharing); (3) Competition Studies against international threats (up to Rs. 8.0 lakh per study, 80:20 sharing); (4) Special Component for North-Eastern Region (80% reimbursement up to Rs. 75,000 per unit for stall space up to 6 sq.m, AC II travel, and freight up to Rs. 15,000); (5) State/District Exhibitions (50% reimbursement up to Rs. 20,000 for general units, and 80% up to Rs. 30,000 for SC/ST/Women/PH units); (6) Corporate Governance Practices (50% reimbursement up to Rs. 45,000 per unit); (7) Setting up 8 Marketing Hubs in MSME-DIs (Rs. 30 lakh infra + Rs. 5 lakh equipment + Rs. 15 lakh 2-year opex); (8) Reimbursement of 75% up to Rs. 1.00 lakh for acquiring ISO 18000, ISO 22000, or ISO 27000 certifications.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to 80% GoI financial assistance for packaging upgradation, skill development, and trade fairs, plus 75% reimbursement up to Rs. 1.0 lakh for ISO certifications and 50% up to Rs. 45,000 for corporate governance.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Office of the Development Commissioner (Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises), Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Government of India

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: Assistance under the scheme will be available for the benefits of micro, small and medium enterprises in the manufacturing segments as per the definition of the Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises Development Act, 2006 (MSMED Act).
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Hotel and travel expenses and surveillance charges for ISO certifications are excluded from reimbursement.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Manufacturing enterprises must hold valid Entrepreneur Memorandum (EM Part-II) or SSI registration. For ISO reimbursement, unit must be functional and in production at the time of certification and submission.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Entrepreneurial Memorandum (EM Part-II) / SSI Registration; ISO 18000/22000/27000 certificate from accredited certifying body.

policy_name: Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Pharmaceuticals
incentive_name: Additional Incentive Allocation from Unutilized Pool

policy_goals: Enhance India's manufacturing capabilities by increasing investment and production in the sector
Contribute to product diversification to high value goods in the pharmaceutical sector
Create global champions out of India who have the potential to grow in size and scale using cutting-edge technology and penetrate global value chains
Reduce import dependency and boost adherence to international quality standards
Promote domestic manufacturing, job creation, and support innovation in R&D and critical drug development
policy_details.policy_summary: The Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Pharmaceuticals, notified by the Department of Pharmaceuticals, Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers, provides financial incentives ranging from 3% to 10% on incremental sales of eligible pharmaceutical goods over the base year FY 2019-20. Running from FY 2020-21 to FY 2028-29 with an overall financial outlay of Rs. 15,000 crore, the scheme supports eligible products across three categories: Category 1 (biopharmaceuticals, complex generics, patented drugs, gene therapies, orphan drugs, special capsules, etc.), Category 2 (APIs, KSMs, and DIs not covered in earlier PLI), and Category 3 (repurposed drugs, auto-immune/anti-cancer/anti-diabetic/anti-infective drugs, and in vitro diagnostic medical devices). Participants are categorized into Group A (revenue >= Rs. 5,000 cr), Group B (revenue between Rs. 500 cr and Rs. 5,000 cr), and Group C (revenue < Rs. 500 cr, including a dedicated sub-group for MSMEs). Applicants must fulfill cumulative investment thresholds and minimum sales growth criteria to receive yearly incentive disbursements.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Direct financial incentives of 3% to 10% on incremental sales of eligible pharmaceutical goods for 6 years, with a total scheme outlay of Rs. 15,000 crore.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Department of Pharmaceuticals, Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers, Government of India
special_focus_areas: High value and complex generic drugs

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: Applicant for the purpose of the Scheme shall be any Proprietary Firm or Partnership Firm or Limited Liability Partnership (LLP) or a Company registered in India proposing to manufacture eligible products and making an application for seeking approval under the Scheme. The applicant should not have been declared as bankrupt or wilful defaulter or reported as fraud by any bank or financial institution or non-banking financial company. Group A: Applicants having Global Manufacturing Revenue (FY 2019-20) of pharmaceutical goods and/or in vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices more than or equal to Rs. 5,000 crore. Group B: Applicants having Global Manufacturing Revenue (FY 2019-20) of pharmaceutical goods and/or in vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices between Rs. 500 (inclusive) crore and Rs. 5,000 crore. Group C: Applicants having Global Manufacturing Revenue (FY 2019-20) of pharmaceutical goods and/or in vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices less than Rs. 500 crore (including a sub-group for MSME applicants registered with the Ministry of MSME). Investment must be made on or after April 01, 2020. No second hand/used/refurbished plant, machinery, equipment, utilities or R&D equipment shall be considered. To be eligible for incentives, participants must meet cumulative investment thresholds over 5 years and achieve threshold sales growth (FY 2022-23 threshold sales: > Rs. 50 crore for Group A, > Rs. 10 crore for Group B, > Rs. 1 crore for Group C, and > Rs. 50 lakh for Group C MSME; subsequent years require 7% YoY growth).
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Applicants declared bankrupt, wilful defaulters, or reported as fraud by any bank, financial institution, or NBFC. Second-hand, used, or refurbished plant, machinery, equipment, utilities, or R&D equipment are excluded from eligible investment. Consumables and raw materials, land expenditure, guest houses, recreational facilities, office buildings, and residential colonies are not considered eligible investment. Investments already counted under PLI Scheme for Bulk Drugs or any other PLI Scheme are excluded.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Manufacturing plants must be located in India.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Registration in India as Proprietary Firm, Partnership Firm, LLP, or Company; MSME registration with Ministry of MSME for MSME category; Regulatory approvals such as WHO-GMP compliance certification or CDSCO / SLA manufacturing licenses, or approvals from USFDA, EDQM, UK MHRA, PMDA, Health Canada, TGA, EU (CE).
special_category_benefits: MSME participants (Group C sub-group reserved with a minimum of 20 MSME slots and relaxed committed investment threshold pacing)
In vitro diagnostic medical devices manufacturers (minimum 5 slots reserved in Group C)

incentive_details.description: Incentive unutilized by one or more selected participants during a year may be reallocated as additional incentive to other performing participants within that Group, capped at 40% of the participant's allocated annual incentive and 20% of the total allocated incentive across the scheme tenure.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: Additional incentive up to 40% of annual allocation from unutilized scheme funds.
incentive_details.application_process: Determined annually by DoP based on unutilized incentive savings within the group.

quantified_benefits.description: Maximum additional incentive per participant per year from unutilized funds
quantified_benefits.source_text: no participant shall receive additional incentive more than 40% of the allocated incentive to such participant for that year
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: Selected participants within the same applicant group

quantified_benefits.description: Maximum cumulative additional incentive over entire scheme tenure
quantified_benefits.source_text: no participant shall receive additional incentive more than 20% of the total incentive allocated to such participant over the entire tenure of the scheme
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: Selected participants within the same applicant group

quantified_benefits.source_text: The ceiling for incentive and additional incentive shall be as follows: Group A Incentive Ceiling 1,000, Ceiling of Additional Incentive 200, Total incentive Ceiling 1,200 (in Rs. crore)

policy_details.policy_summary: The Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Pharmaceuticals, notified by the Department of Pharmaceuticals, Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers, provides financial incentives ranging from 3% to 10% on incremental sales of eligible pharmaceutical goods over the base year FY 2019-20. Running from FY 2020-21 to FY 2028-29 with an overall financial outlay of Rs. 15,000 crore, the scheme supports eligible products across three categories: Category 1 (biopharmaceuticals, complex generics, patented drugs, gene therapies, orphan drugs, special capsules, etc.), Category 2 (APIs, KSMs, and DIs not covered in earlier PLI), and Category 3 (repurposed drugs, auto-immune/anti-cancer/anti-diabetic/anti-infective drugs, and in vitro diagnostic medical devices). Participants are categorized into Group A (revenue >= Rs. 5,000 cr), Group B (revenue between Rs. 500 cr and Rs. 5,000 cr), and Group C (revenue < Rs. 500 cr, including a dedicated sub-group for MSMEs). Applicants must fulfill cumulative investment thresholds and minimum sales growth criteria to receive yearly incentive disbursements.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Direct financial incentives of 3% to 10% on incremental sales of eligible pharmaceutical goods for 6 years, with a total scheme outlay of Rs. 15,000 crore.

special_focus_areas: High value and complex generic drugs

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: Applicant for the purpose of the Scheme shall be any Proprietary Firm or Partnership Firm or Limited Liability Partnership (LLP) or a Company registered in India proposing to manufacture eligible products and making an application for seeking approval under the Scheme. The applicant should not have been declared as bankrupt or wilful defaulter or reported as fraud by any bank or financial institution or non-banking financial company. Group A: Applicants having Global Manufacturing Revenue (FY 2019-20) of pharmaceutical goods and/or in vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices more than or equal to Rs. 5,000 crore. Group B: Applicants having Global Manufacturing Revenue (FY 2019-20) of pharmaceutical goods and/or in vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices between Rs. 500 (inclusive) crore and Rs. 5,000 crore. Group C: Applicants having Global Manufacturing Revenue (FY 2019-20) of pharmaceutical goods and/or in vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices less than Rs. 500 crore (including a sub-group for MSME applicants registered with the Ministry of MSME). Investment must be made on or after April 01, 2020. No second hand/used/refurbished plant, machinery, equipment, utilities or R&D equipment shall be considered. To be eligible for incentives, participants must meet cumulative investment thresholds over 5 years and achieve threshold sales growth (FY 2022-23 threshold sales: > Rs. 50 crore for Group A, > Rs. 10 crore for Group B, > Rs. 1 crore for Group C, and > Rs. 50 lakh for Group C MSME; subsequent years require 7% YoY growth).
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Applicants declared bankrupt, wilful defaulters, or reported as fraud by any bank, financial institution, or NBFC. Second-hand, used, or refurbished plant, machinery, equipment, utilities, or R&D equipment are excluded from eligible investment. Consumables and raw materials, land expenditure, guest houses, recreational facilities, office buildings, and residential colonies are not considered eligible investment. Investments already counted under PLI Scheme for Bulk Drugs or any other PLI Scheme are excluded.

policy_details.policy_summary: Scheme Part-1 of the PLI Scheme for Textiles encourages large-scale manufacturing of MMF Apparel, MMF Fabrics, and Technical Textiles. Applicants must form a new company under the Companies Act 2013 and invest a minimum of Rs. 300 crore in plant, machinery, equipment, and civil works (excluding land and administrative building costs) over a two-year gestation period (FY 2022-23 to FY 2023-24). The company becomes eligible for financial incentives starting from Performance Year 1 (FY 2024-25) upon achieving a minimum threshold turnover of Rs. 600 crore from notified products and subsequently maintaining at least a 25% year-on-year incremental turnover growth (capped at 35% admissible incremental growth) for 5 performance years. Required domestic value addition is at least 60% (30% for independent fabric processing).
policy_details.benefit_headline: Incentive ranging from 15% down to 11% on eligible turnover and incremental sales over 5 consecutive performance years for a minimum investment of Rs. 300 crore.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Ministry of Textiles, Government of India

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: Scheme Part- 1: Any person including Company/Firm/LLP/Trust willing to create a separate manufacturing company under Companies Act 2013, and invest minimum Rs. 300 Crore (excluding land and administrative building cost) to manufacture Notified Products. Such company will be eligible to get incentive when they achieve a minimum of Rs. 600 Crore turnover by manufacturing and selling the Notified products by the first Performance Year. The Applicant once selected under the scheme shall form a new company under the Companies Act, 2013 before commencement of investment. Only manufacturing company registered in India will be eligible. Participating company shall have to do minimum value addition as required under the scheme (60% for integrated or fibre/yarn to fabric or fabric to garment and technical textiles; 30% for independent fabrics processing industry) in their own registered factory premises.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Trading and job work / outsourced job work turnover are excluded. Investment in land and administrative buildings (e.g., office and guest houses) and second-hand/used/refurbished plant, machinery, and equipment are ineligible. Entities declared bankrupt, defaulters, reported for fraud, or blacklisted by any government authority are excluded.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Manufacturing must take place in the participant company's registered factory premises in India. Preference points are awarded for investments located in Aspirational Districts and Group 'C' cities, or relocation to PM-MITRA Parks.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Incorporation as a new company under Companies Act, 2013; possession of PAN, GSTIN, and DIN; registration on the Ministry of Textiles PLI portal.
special_category_benefits: Additional marks awarded during selection evaluation for units located in Aspirational Districts and Category C cities

Incentive rates start at 15% in Year 1 on threshold turnover and reduce by 1% each year down to 11% in Year 5. In Year 1, turnover is capped at 2 times investment + 10%. From Year 2 onwards, minimum incremental growth required is 25% over the immediate preceding year, capped at 35% admissible incremental turnover.

policy_goals: Promote manufacturing of Telecom and Networking Products in India

policy_details.policy_summary: The PLI Scheme for Telecom and Networking Products provides financial incentives ranging from 4% to 7% on incremental sales of manufactured goods in target segments over the base year (FY 2019-20) for a period of five years starting from FY 2021-22. Target segments include Core Transmission Equipment, 4G/5G and Next Generation Radio Access Network and Wireless Equipment, Access & Customer Premises Equipment (CPE), IoT Access Devices, and Enterprise Equipment (Switches, Routers). Approvals are granted to 10 eligible applicants in the MSME category and 10 in the non-MSME category (with at least 3 domestic companies). Minimum committed cumulative investment thresholds over 4 years are ₹10 Crores for MSMEs and ₹100 Crores for non-MSMEs, with qualifying base-year global manufacturing revenues exceeding ₹10 Crores (MSMEs), ₹250 Crores (Domestic Non-MSMEs), or ₹10,000 Crores (Global Non-MSMEs).
policy_details.benefit_headline: Incentive of 4% to 7% on net incremental sales of manufactured telecom and networking products over base year FY 2019-20 for 5 years, with total outlay of ₹12,195 Crores.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Department of Telecommunications, Ministry of Communications, Government of India
special_focus_areas: Next generation telecom equipment (5G, IoT, FTTH)

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: Support under the Scheme shall be provided only to companies for manufacturing of goods in India as covered under Scheme Target Segments. Further any foreign (non-resident) investment in the Applicant company shall be in compliance to the FDI Policy 2020. Eligibility shall be subject to qualification criteria for Global Manufacturing Revenue: Global companies must have Global Manufacturing Revenue more than Rs. 10,000 Crore in the base year; Domestic companies must have Global Manufacturing Revenue more than Rs. 250 Crore in the base year; MSMEs must have Global Manufacturing Revenue more than Rs. 10 Crore in the base year. Eligibility shall be subject to thresholds of minimum cumulative Incremental Investment during the year and Incremental Sales of Manufactured Goods over the base year as per Annexure 2. Applicants whose accounts are declared as NPA as per RBI guidelines, wilful defaulters, reported as fraud, or having insolvency proceedings admitted against them in NCLT are ineligible.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Applicants whose accounts are declared as Non-Performing Asset (NPA) as per RBI guidelines or wilful defaulter or reported as fraud by any bank, financial institution or non-banking financial company, or with admitted insolvency proceedings against them in NCLT. Traded goods without value addition/processing are excluded. Land and building expenditure is excluded. Diversion of sales from Group Companies or closure of existing units in India for claiming higher incentives is prohibited. An applicant is ineligible if it has applied/availed benefits under any other Central Government PLI Scheme for the same product.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Manufacturing facilities must be set up at one or more locations in India, prior intimated to DoT.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Company registered in India under the Companies Act 2013; MSMEs must be registered with the Ministry of MSME, Government of India.
special_category_benefits: MSMEs have lower investment threshold (₹10 Crore vs ₹100 Crore) and higher initial incentive rates (7% in Years 1-2 vs 6%)

policy_details.policy_summary: The Market Promotion and Development Assistance (MPDA) Scheme is a unified programme formulated by merging earlier schemes of Market Development Assistance (MDA), Publicity, Marketing and Market Promotion, and Infrastructure. Under Modified MDA (MMDA), financial assistance at 30% of Prime Cost is provided for Khadi and Polyvastra, de-linking pricing from cost charts and apportioning assistance between producing institutions, selling institutions, and artisans/karyakartas through Aadhaar-linked DBT. The scheme also funds domestic and international exhibitions, export incentives, and Marketing Complexes/Plazas (Khadi Plazas).
policy_details.benefit_headline: 30% Modified Market Development Assistance (MMDA) on prime cost of Khadi and Polyvastra, plus up to ₹10 crore grant for Khadi Plazas.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Government of India

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: The Khadi institutions, having valid Khadi certificate and categorised as A+, A, B and C only are eligible to avail MMDA grant from KVIC. Producing institutions shall submit quarterly claims of MMDA on prime cost for the production achieved during the preceding quarter within 15 days of completion of the quarter through online MDA processing system of KVIC. Production of Khadi and Polyvastra products for the purpose of Govt. Supplies under Rate Contract (RC) of DGS&D to be made against the wholesale target approved by Standing Finance Committee of KVIC is not eligible for MMDA.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Institutions without valid Khadi certificate or category below C; Production for Govt. Supplies under Rate Contract (RC) of DGS&D against wholesale target.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Institutions must maintain a separate bank account and furnish quarterly and annual utilization certificates certified by registered Chartered Accountants.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Valid Khadi certificate from KVIC categorized as A+, A, B, or C; 100% Aadhaar-linked bank/post office accounts for artisans.

policy_goals: Generate continuous and sustainable employment opportunities in rural and urban areas through setting up of new self-employment micro enterprises and ventures
Bring together traditional artisans, rural, and urban unemployed youth to arrest rural-to-urban migration and increase wage-earning capacity
Support the rationalization of assistance, modern infrastructure, and market-linked pricing for Khadi and Village Industry products while enhancing earnings of artisans and karyakartas
policy_details.policy_summary: PMEGP is a major credit-linked subsidy central sector scheme administered by the Ministry of MSME and implemented by KVIC as the nodal agency at the national level, along with State KVIBs, DICs, and banks. The scheme facilitates setting up of new self-employment micro-enterprises in non-farm manufacturing and service/trading sectors, as well as second financial assistance for upgrading performing PMEGP/REGP/MUDRA units. Government financial assistance is disbursed in the form of Margin Money subsidy credited into beneficiary loan accounts and kept in a three-year Term Deposit Receipt / Subsidy Reserve Fund before final adjustment following physical verification and mandatory Udyam registration.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to 35% margin money subsidy on project costs up to ₹50 lakhs for new micro enterprises and up to 20% subsidy on upgradation projects up to ₹1 crore.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Government of India

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: Any individual, above 18 years of age. There will be no income ceiling for assistance for setting up projects under PMEGP. For setting up of project costing above Rs.10 lakh in the Manufacturing sector and above Rs. 5 lakh in the Business /Service sector, the beneficiaries should possess at least VIII standard pass educational qualification. Assistance under the scheme is available only for new projects sanctioned specifically under the PMEGP. Existing Units (under PMRY, REGP or any other scheme of Government of India or State Government) and the units that have already availed Government Subsidy under any other scheme of Government of India or State Government are not eligible. Projects without Capital Expenditure are not eligible for Financing under the Scheme. Cost of the land should not be included in the Project cost. Only one person from one family is eligible for obtaining financial assistance for setting up of projects under PMEGP. The family includes self and spouse. All new units setup under PMEGP will be mandatorily registered under Udyam Portal before Physical Verification of the Unit and the adjustment of the Margin Money in the PMEGP beneficiary loan account. For up-gradation of existing PMEGP/REGP/MUDRA units: Margin Money (subsidy) claimed under PMEGP has to be successfully adjusted on the completion of lock in period of 3 years; First loan under PMEGP/REGP/MUDRA has to be successfully repaid in stipulated time; The unit is profit making with good turnover and having potential for further growth in turnover and profit with modernization/upgrading the technology.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Projects without Capital Expenditure; Cost of land; Units that have already availed government subsidy under any other scheme of GoI or State Government; Activities listed under negative list (meat/slaughtered processing, beedi/pan/cigar/cigarette/liquor/tobacco, polythene carry bags <75 microns, crop cultivation/plantation like tea/coffee/rubber except off-farm value addition).
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Beneficiaries must pass at least 8th standard for manufacturing projects above ₹10 lakhs and business/service projects above ₹5 lakhs. Fixed capital investment per full-time worker must not exceed ₹3 lakhs in plain areas and ₹4.50 lakhs in hilly areas, A&N Islands, and Lakshadweep. Completion of Entrepreneurship Development Programme (EDP) training is mandatory.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Mandatory Udyam Registration before physical verification and margin money adjustment; Aadhaar number authentication.

incentive_details.description: Financial assistance for expansion and technology modernization of well-performing existing units set up under PMEGP, REGP, or MUDRA.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: 15% to 20% subsidy on upgradation project costs up to ₹1.00 crore for manufacturing and up to ₹25 lakhs for service units.
incentive_details.application_process: Applications submitted online via PMEGP-e-Portal, preliminary scrutiny by district level agencies, and appraisal by financing banks.

quantified_benefits.source_text: The maximum cost of the project/unit admissible for Margin Money subsidy under Manufacturing sector for upgradation is Rs. 1.00 crore. Maximum subsidy would be Rs.15 lakh (Rs.20 lakh for NER and Hill States).

quantified_benefits.cap_raw: Rs. 3.75 lakh (Rs. 5 lakh for NER and Hill States)

policy_goals: Train 10.00 lakh persons (9.00 lakh in the organized sector and 1.00 lakh in traditional sectors) over a period of 3 years from 2017-18 to 2019-20 with a total financial outlay of Rs. 1300 crore

Provide demand-driven, placement-oriented National Skills Qualifications Framework (NSQF) compliant skilling programmes to incentivize and supplement industry efforts in creating jobs across the entire textile value chain (excluding Spinning and Weaving in the organized sector)
Promote skilling and skill upgradation in the traditional sectors of handlooms, handicrafts, sericulture, and jute
Enable sustainable livelihoods through wage employment or self-employment for all sections of society across India
policy_details.policy_summary: The Scheme for Capacity Building in Textile Sector (SCBTS), branded as Samarth under the Skill India Mission, is an employment-linked skilling initiative covering the textile value chain (excluding organized spinning and weaving). Implementing Agencies (IAs)—including textile industry units, government institutions, and reputed training organizations with industrial placement tie-ups—receive project funding aligned with MSDE Common Norms. Training comprises NSQF-aligned entry-level and advanced courses along with a minimum 30 hours of soft skills training. The scheme mandates Aadhaar-enabled biometric attendance, third-party assessment and certification, minimum 70% placement (100% wage employment for organized sector; at least 50% wage employment with balance in self-employment for traditional sectors), and 1-year post-placement tracking. Funding is disbursed in three outcome-linked tranches (30%, 50%, and 20%).
policy_details.benefit_headline: 100% grant funding for NSQF-compliant skill training in textiles up to Rs. 15,950 per trainee, released across 3 milestones against validated enrollment, certification, and 70% placement.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Ministry of Textiles, Government of India
special_focus_areas: Traditional textile crafts (Handlooms, Handicrafts, Sericulture, Jute)

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: 3.1 Implementing Agencies (IA): The skilling programmes will be implemented through the following Implementing Agencies: (i) Textile Industry. (ii) Institutions/ Organizations of the Ministry of Textiles/ State Governments having training infrastructure and placement tie-ups with the textile industry. (iii) Reputed training institutions/ NGOs/ Societies/ Trusts/ Organizations/ Companies /Start Ups / Entrepreneurs active in the textile sector having placement tie-ups with textile industry. 3.2 The empanelment of Implementing Agencies will be based on the following parameters: (i) Organization credentials. (ii) Past experience of skilling in the textile sector. (iii) Financial strength. (iv) Training Infrastructure, particularly in Aspirational Districts notified by the NITI Aayog. Trainee eligibility: 3.5.2 Selection of trainees: The trainee must be a citizen of India possessing an Aadhaar Card (unless exempted under Aadhaar Act, 2016) with age over 14 years. A minimum of 80% attendance is mandatory for a trainee to be eligible for assessment.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Spinning and Weaving in the organized sector are excluded from the scheme. Construction of new training center buildings is not permitted under the scheme.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Pan-India; preference is given to training infrastructure located in the 115 Aspirational Districts notified by NITI Aayog.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Valid registration/incorporation, PAN, GSTIN, and registration on the Samarth portal (samarth-textiles.gov.in) with submission of a non-refundable processing fee of Rs. 25,000 via Demand Draft.

incentive_details.description: Assessment and certification of trained candidates is funded by the scheme and paid separately through the Resource Support Agency (Textiles Committee) directly to empaneled third-party assessment agencies.

Undertake research and studies on MSME related issues

policy_details.policy_summary: The Scheme for Assistance to Training Institutions (ATI) is a Central Sector Scheme implemented by the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MoMSME). It provides financial assistance for the creation, strengthening, and expansion of training infrastructure, opening of new branches or centres of national-level training institutions under MoMSME, and meeting revenue deficits of NIMSME. It also supports eligible existing State Level Entrepreneurship Development Institutes (EDIs) and State Government-owned training institutes including District Industries Centres (DICs) in Eastern and North Eastern Regions (NER) with capital grants up to Rs. 3.00 Crore for physical infrastructure, equipment, and faculty training. Furthermore, the scheme provides financial assistance of a recurring and revenue nature to conduct NSQF-compliant skill development training programmes and Training of Trainers (ToTs) programmes through designated national training institutions and eligible State Government-owned training institutes/DICs.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Financial grant up to Rs. 3.00 Crore for infrastructure and capacity building of State Level EDIs/DICs, and hourly training assistance up to Rs. 38.50 per trainee plus Rs. 60 per trainee for Training of Trainers.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
special_focus_areas: Eastern Region and North Eastern Region (NER)

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: 3.1.1 Training Institutions of Ministry of MSME: Assistance may be provided for creation or strengthening/expansion of infrastructure, including opening of new branches/centers to training institutions of Ministry of MSME and for meeting revenue deficit, if any, of National Institute for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (ni-msme). 3.2.1 State Level EDIs: (i) Assistance may be provided to existing State Level EDIs owned or controlled or promoted by a State Government/UT for creation or strengthening/expansion of their infrastructure. (ii) Financial assistance may also be provided to State Government's owned training Institutes including Districts Industries Centers (DICs) located in Eastern Region and NER, for strengthening of its infrastructure for training related activities in the field of MSME. (iii) Costs of land, construction of staff quarters etc. would not qualify. (iv) Financial assistance will not be available for setting up of a new EDI. 3.3.1 Training Programmes: Assistance may be provided to conduct training programmes in the areas of Skill Development to: (a) ni-msme; (b) NSIC; (c) KVIC; (d) Coir Board; (e) Tool Rooms/Technology Centers; (f) MGIRI and (g) State Government owned training Institutes including Districts Industries Centers (DICs) located in Eastern Region and NER. Private training institutions/NGOs are not covered under the scheme for assistance for infrastructure support and training programmes.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Private training institutions/NGOs are not covered under the scheme for assistance for infrastructure support and training programmes. Costs of land and construction of staff quarters do not qualify for grant calculation. Financial assistance is not available for setting up a new EDI.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: All proposals of State Level EDIs/Institutions/DICs must be routed through and recommended by the respective State/UT Government. Proposals must be approved by the Screening Committee and Secretary (MSME). Assisted institutions must complete construction within the given timeframe, furnish utilization certificates, get accounts audited annually, submit annual reports for at least 5 years, and maintain a fixed assets register.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: State Government owned training institutes and DICs must be located in Eastern Region and North Eastern Region (NER) to be eligible under specific regional components.

incentive_details.description: Annual grant provided under the scheme to reputed academic and research institutions such as IITs and IIMs for establishing an MSME Chair to undertake dedicated studies and research on MSME sector challenges and opportunities.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: Annual grant for establishing MSME Chair at premier academic and research institutions like IITs and IIMs.
incentive_details.application_process: Proposals submitted to MoMSME are considered by a committee of Secretary (MSME), JS (SME), AS & FA, and AS & DC (MSME).

quantified_benefits.conditions: Considered by a dedicated committee comprising Secretary (MSME), Joint Secretary (SME), AS&FA, and AS&DC (MSME).
quantified_benefits.description: Annual grant for MSME Chair establishment
quantified_benefits.source_text: Annual grant may be provided under the scheme to academic and research institutions of repute like, IITs and IIMs for establishing MSME Chair for undertaking studies and research on MSME issues.
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: Academic and research institutions of repute like IITs and IIMs

parent_policy_name: Scheme for Promotion of Research and Innovation in Pharma MedTech Sector (PRIP)
policy_name: PRIP Component B: Early Stage Projects (Startups and MSMEs)
incentive_name: Incentives for Academic Collaboration and IP In-licensing

policy_goals: Transform India's Pharma MedTech sector from cost-based to innovation-based growth by strengthening research infrastructure in the country
Promote industry-academia linkage for R&D in priority areas and nurture a pool of scientists

Enable Indian pharmaceutical and MedTech industry and startups to leapfrog up the innovation value chain and capture higher global market share (envisioning 4% to 5% global market share reaching USD 130-160 billion by 2030)
Shift focus to high-value goods such as biopharmaceuticals, complex generics, patented drugs, cell and gene therapy, and novel medical devices

Accelerate investment in the R&D ecosystem through a total financial outlay of ₹5,000 crores across FY 2023-24 to FY 2029-30 (₹700 crore for Component A CoEs, ₹4,200 crore for Component B R&D assistance, and ₹100 crore administrative outlay)
policy_details.policy_summary: Component B of the PRIP Scheme provides financial assistance to DPIIT-recognized startups and Udyam-registered MSMEs to advance R&D products or technologies from Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 1, 2, or 3 up to TRL 5 across three priority areas: (i) New medicines (NCEs, NBEs, phytopharmaceuticals, AYUSH/homeopathic new medicines), (ii) Complex generics and biosimilars, and (iii) Novel medical devices. Projects receive 100% financial assistance for project costs up to ₹1 crore, and 50% financial assistance for costs above ₹1 crore up to ₹5 crore (with a maximum grant of ₹5 crore per project). Grants are disbursed in four milestone-linked instalments through a dedicated project bank account upon achieving sequential milestone descriptors and demonstrating financial closure.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to ₹5 crore in milestone-based financial assistance (100% funding up to ₹1 crore and 50% for costs up to ₹5 crore) for early-stage pharma and MedTech R&D.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Department of Pharmaceuticals, Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers, Government of India

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: Every entity registered in India that meets the following criteria is eligible for financial assistance under Component B of the Scheme: (a) It is a company registered under the Companies Act, 2013 or under any previous company law and is other than a company that has only one person as a member, or does not have any limit on liability, or is a section 8/section 25 non-profit; (b) It is a Limited Liability Partnership registered under the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008; (c) It is a partnership firm other than a sole proprietorship firm and is registered under the Indian Partnership Act, 1932. In case of an Early Stage Project, such company, partnership or firm is required to meet the following additional eligibility criterion: (a) It is a startup having a valid certificate granted by the Inter-Ministerial Board of Certification under DPIIT notification G.S.R. 127(E), dated 19.2.2019; or (b) It is a micro, small and medium enterprise (MSME) having a valid Udyam Registration Certificate under MSME notification S.O. 2119(E), dated 26.6.2020. TRL eligibility: Projects of startups and MSMEs to take products or technologies at TRL 1, 2 or 3 in any priority area to higher TRLs not beyond TRL 5 will be eligible. At least part of the project's commercialisation must target the Indian market.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Sole proprietorship firms, One Person Companies (OPC), companies registered under Section 8 of Companies Act 2013 / Section 25 of Companies Act 1956, trusts, societies, unregistered entities, entities whose key managerial personnel is convicted of an offence involving moral turpitude/corruption with imprisonment >= 6 months, entities undergoing insolvency/winding-up proceedings, and projects exclusively meant for export with no Indian market commercialisation.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Registration in India as a Private/Public Limited Company, LLP, or Registered Partnership Firm; Entity Locker registration; Valid DPIIT Certificate of Recognition for Startups OR Valid Udyam Registration Certificate for MSMEs.
special_category_benefits: Projects involving significant collaborative development with reputed Government academic and research institutions (up to 9 preference applications per category)
In-licensing costs of IP from eligible Government academic partners treated as eligible project cost at fair value
Capital assets transferred to Academia excluded from benefit-share calculation

incentive_details.description: Incentives for partnering with recognized Government academic/research institutions of national repute: (i) Preference given to up to nine applications per category with significant collaborative development; (ii) Costs of project-linked in-licensing of intellectual property from such institutes at fair value are funded as eligible project costs; (iii) Capital expenditure on project-linked assets/equipment transferred to Academia at fair value without consideration is deducted from the beneficiary's benefit-share repayment obligation.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: 100% funding for academic IP in-licensing at fair value and complete exemption of transferred academic capital assets from benefit-sharing obligations.
incentive_details.application_process: Include details of the academic partner from Appendix 1, provide MoU/LoI outlining collaborative scope, execute academic in-licensing agreement/intent letter, and furnish valuation report.

quantified_benefits.conditions: Requires valid contract or Academic Intent Letter and valuation report from an approved agency
quantified_benefits.description: In-licensing of intellectual property from eligible Government academic partners treated as eligible project cost at independent third-party assessed fair value.
quantified_benefits.source_text: Costs of project linked in-licensing of intellectual property from such institutes at fair value are considered as 'eligible costs' for funding
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: Startups and MSMEs collaborating with listed Government academic/research institutes

quantified_benefits.value_raw: 100% of fair value of transferred assets
quantified_benefits.conditions: Assets must be transferred without consideration and certified as public assets usable for R&D
quantified_benefits.description: Exemption of fair value of capital assets transferred to Academia from total benefit-share obligation.
quantified_benefits.source_text: In case capital assets are transferred by the beneficiary to the books of the Academia for their use without consideration and are certified by such Academia as constituting public assets usable for R&D, for purposes of computation of benefit-share, the independently assessed fair value of such assets will be netted out from the total financial assistance disbursed.
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: Collaborative projects where R&D equipment/assets are transferred to Academia

incentive_details.application_deadline: Concurrent with project application submission (10th November 2025)

policy_goals: Transform India's Pharma MedTech sector from cost-based to innovation-based growth by strengthening research infrastructure in the country
Promote industry-academia linkage for R&D in priority areas and nurture a pool of scientists

Enable Indian pharmaceutical and MedTech industry and startups to leapfrog up the innovation value chain and capture higher global market share (envisioning 4% to 5% global market share reaching USD 130-160 billion by 2030)

policy_details.policy_summary: Component B Later Stage Projects support industry, including large companies, MSMEs, and startups, to advance drug and MedTech products or technologies from TRL 4, 5, or 6 to higher TRLs (e.g. clinical trials Phase I/II/III, multi-site validation, and regulatory approval). policy_goals: Encourage and support more women enterprises in the Micro and Small Enterprise (MSE) sector
Economically empower women through entrepreneurship assistance, training, credit facilitation, cluster development, and market access in non-farm activities
Increase women participation and representation in domestic and international trade fairs and exhibitions

policy_details.policy_summary: Launched in August 2000, this scheme provides collateral-free credit facilities extended by Member Lending Institutions (MLIs) to new and existing Micro and Small Enterprises for loans up to Rs. 50 lakh. Standard guarantee cover is up to 75% of the loan amount, but is enhanced to 80% for: (i) micro enterprises for loans up to Rs. 5 lakh; (ii) MSEs operated and/or owned by women; and (iii) all loans in the North-East Region (NER). For loans up to Rs. 5 lakh, the one-time guarantee fee is reduced to 1% and annual service charge is 0.5%, compared to 1.5% and 0.75% respectively for other loans.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Enhanced 80% credit guarantee cover for collateral-free bank loans up to ₹50 lakh for women-owned/operated MSEs.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Office of the Development Commissioner (MSME), Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Government of India

eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Loan must be sanctioned without collateral security by Member Lending Institutions (MLIs).

policy_details.policy_summary: Formulated by the Office of the DC (MSME) to encourage Small and Micro manufacturing units owned by women and registered with DI/DIC to tap and develop overseas export markets. Under this marketing development assistance (MDA) scheme, women entrepreneurs participate in identified international trade fairs and exhibitions under the MSME stall. Beneficiaries receive rent-free stall space (6/9 sq. meters) and 100% reimbursement of economy-class return airfare for one representative, subject to an overall ceiling of Rs. 1.25 lakh per unit. policy_name: Micro & Small Enterprises Cluster Development Programme (MSE-CDP)
incentive_name: Assistance for Soft Interventions in Clusters

policy_goals: Encourage and support more women enterprises in the Micro and Small Enterprise (MSE) sector
Economically empower women through entrepreneurship assistance, training, credit facilitation, cluster development, and market access in non-farm activities
Increase women participation and representation in domestic and international trade fairs and exhibitions
Provide collateral-free credit flow and risk reduction to women-owned and women-managed enterprises
policy_details.policy_summary: The MSE-CDP scheme supports clusters of traditional and skill-based MSEs to enhance competitiveness, improve technology, adopt best manufacturing practices, and create common infrastructure. For existing clusters (ideally 100 members, reducible to 50 in difficult/backward regions), the programme provides support for soft interventions (capacity building, diagnostic studies, trust building, exposure visits) and hard interventions (CFCs, testing labs, design centres, tooling, mini tool rooms). While general contribution ranges from 30% to 80%, clusters owned and managed by women receive up to 90% project cost contribution from the Ministry of MSME. In physical infrastructure creation (developed industrial sites, power, water, roads, display centres), a central grant of 40% (up to Rs. 2 crore) is available exclusively for women enterprises.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to 90% project cost grant for hard interventions and 40% grant up to ₹2 crore for physical infrastructure exclusively for women clusters.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Office of the Development Commissioner (MSME), Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Government of India
special_focus_areas: Clusters owned and managed by women entrepreneurs

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: A cluster is defined as a group of enterprises, ideally having 100 members, producing same/similar products/services. While 100 members could be the minimum per cluster, depending on the density of population and other factors, even 200-300 could be a good target group. In difficult and backward regions the target numbers could come down to 50 or less. The hard interventions and creation of physical infrastructure require the setup of a users body/special purpose vehicle (SPV) which could be a society, trust, or company formed by cluster beneficiaries.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Must form a Special Purpose Vehicle (Society/Trust/Company) for hard interventions and physical infrastructure.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Difficult and backward regions have relaxed member size thresholds (down to 50 members).
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Registration of SPV/User Body as Society/Trust/Company
special_category_benefits: Clusters owned and managed by women entrepreneurs (eligible for up to 90% grant)
Infrastructure exclusively for women enterprises (40% central grant up to Rs. 2 crore)

incentive_details.benefit_headline: Financial assistance up to ₹10 lakh ceiling per cluster for soft interventions and capacity building.
incentive_details.application_process: Engaging a Cluster Development Executive (CDE) through DIC / MSME-DI to formulate and execute soft interventions.

quantified_benefits.conditions: Appointment of a Cluster Development Executive (CDE) for execution and monitoring.
