quantified_benefits.source_text: In the past depending upon the type of cluster, assistance available for soft interventions has varied in the range of Rs.25 – 35 lakh per cluster. Currently we have an internal ceiling of Rs.10 lakh for soft intervention under this Scheme.

incentive_name: Government of India Grant for Capacity Building and Project Assistance

policy_goals: Encourage and support more women enterprises in the Micro and Small Enterprise (MSE) sector
Economically empower women through entrepreneurship assistance, training, credit facilitation, cluster development, and market access in non-farm activities
Increase women participation and representation in domestic and international trade fairs and exhibitions
Provide collateral-free credit flow and risk reduction to women-owned and women-managed enterprises
policy_details.policy_summary: The TREAD scheme is formulated to economically empower women through the development of entrepreneurial skills in non-farm activities. Since poor and marginalized women face credit access barriers, financial loans are extended through NGOs along with GoI grant support. The scheme provides GoI grant up to 30% of the loan/credit amount (maximum up to Rs. 30 lakh) as appraised by lending banks/institutions, while the remaining 70% is financed as a bank loan. The grant is utilized for capacity building of the NGO and project support activities. Additionally, grants up to Rs. 1 lakh per programme are provided for training institutions/NGOs to train women entrepreneurs, and up to Rs. 5 lakh for institutions undertaking field surveys, research studies, and module design.
policy_details.benefit_headline: GoI grant up to 30% of project/loan cost (up to ₹30 lakh) for women micro-ventures through NGOs, plus training grant up to ₹1 lakh per programme.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Office of the Development Commissioner (MSME), Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Government of India

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: The applicant NGO must: a) Be a legal entity with a minimum registration of three years. b) Have experience in thrift and saving programmes with SHGs / individuals. c) Be engaged in entrepreneurship and income generation activities for women. d) Have basic infrastructure, qualified support staff and services to undertake micro-enterprise development for women. e) Shall be eligible for Government Assistance i.e. shall not be blacklisted by any Ministry or any State Government under any scheme. f) Shall not have any Government Assistance released earlier to the NGO pending i.e. Utilization Certificate overdue. Beneficiaries must be women taking up self-employment ventures in any kind of non-farm activity.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: NGOs blacklisted by any Ministry or State Government, or NGOs with pending/overdue Utilization Certificates from earlier Government Assistance. Selected NGOs cannot receive GoI grant again in the subsequent two years from the release date.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: NGOs must submit composite bankable proposals for a group of women entrepreneurs. Training batches must have at least 20 participants.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Minimum legal registration of 3 years as an NGO/Society/Trust
special_category_benefits: North Eastern Region (NER) institutions (promoters contribution reduced to 10% instead of 25%)

incentive_details.description: GoI grant up to 30% of the loan/credit amount (maximum Rs. 30.00 lakh) as appraised by lending institutions/banks. The grant is disbursed through the lending bank to the NGO for capacity building components, including ESDP training (30-40%), project coordinator honorarium (5-8%), marketing manager honorarium (4-6%), office assistant honorarium (3-5%), staff training (2-3%), documentation (3-5%), IT/MIS hardware/software/furniture (8-10%), SHG formation (2-3%), travel (2-3%), auditor fee (2-3%), insurance (5-8%), exhibition/exposure visits (3-5%), evaluation study (2-3%), and last installments for repayment of loan (20%).
incentive_details.benefit_headline: Grant up to 30% of loan amount, capped at ₹30 lakh, for women micro-enterprise projects and NGO capacity building.
incentive_details.application_process: Proposals submitted online or in prescribed format to concerned Director, MSME-DI. MSME-DI scrutinizes and forwards to designated lending bank (MoU banks like SBI, Canara Bank, BoB, etc.) for appraisal. Bank issues in-principle sanction and forwards to State Level Screening Committee (SLSC). Recommended proposals go to the National Steering Committee chaired by AS&DC (MSME) for final grant approval and RTGS release via bank.

quantified_benefits.conditions: Remaining 70% financed by lending bank as loan; 20% of GoI grant component can be used for last installments of loan repayment.
quantified_benefits.description: GoI grant towards project cost/loan amount for capacity building and project activities
quantified_benefits.source_text: There is a provision for Government of India Grant up to 30% of the loan/ credit maximum up to Rs. 30.00 lakh as appraised by lending institution/ banks.
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: Eligible NGOs handling bank loans for women beneficiaries

incentive_details.application_authority: Director, MSME-Development Institute (MSME-DI) of the respective State and Office of DC (MSME)
incentive_details.incentive_specific_eligibility: NGO must have minimum 3 years registration, experience in SHG thrift/savings, and be engaged in entrepreneurship for women.

policy_name: Special Incentives Scheme for ESDM Sector 2020 - 2025
incentive_name: Capital Investment Subsidy - Land Subsidy

policy_goals: Promote and accelerate the growth of the Electronics System Design and Manufacturing (ESDM) sector in Karnataka
Offer comprehensive fiscal incentives and concessions to attract domestic and international ESDM manufacturing investments
Support new enterprise creation as well as expansion, modernization, and diversification of existing electronics units across Karnataka
Drive large-scale employment generation in the electronics manufacturing ecosystem
policy_details.policy_summary: The Special Incentives Scheme for ESDM Sector 2020–2025 provides a targeted package of financial and operational incentives to promote Electronics System Design and Manufacturing in Karnataka. Administered by the Karnataka Innovation and Technology Society (KITS), the scheme supports both new manufacturing enterprises and the expansion, modernization, or diversification of existing units. Key benefits include a 20% capital investment subsidy on plant and machinery, a 25% subsidy on land value (outside Bengaluru Urban and Rural districts, capped at INR 12.5 crore), 100% reimbursement of stamp duty, registration charges, and land conversion fees, 100% exemption from electricity duty for 5 years, power tariff reimbursement of INR 1.00 per unit for 5 years, and a production-linked incentive (PLI) of 1.00% of net sales turnover for 5 years. Total incentives are generally capped at 100% of the Value of Fixed Assets (50% for solar cell manufacturing with VFA of INR 500 Cr or more).
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to 20% subsidy on plant & machinery, 25% land subsidy up to ₹12.5 Cr, 100% stamp duty and land conversion refund, 5-year power concessions, and 1% PLI for ESDM units in Karnataka.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Department of Electronics, Information Technology, Biotechnology, and Science & Technology, Government of Karnataka
special_focus_areas: Investments outside Bengaluru Urban and Rural

eligibility_criteria.raw_text:
2. Eligibility Criteria
2.1. Target Segments
The company applying for Special Incentive Scheme for ESDM Sector ('Scheme') should be involved in manufacturing of one or more of the following Target Segments or related activities ('Eligible Products/Activities'):
a) Manufacturing and / or design of electronics products such as Telecom Systems / Mobiles / IT Systems and Hardware / Consumer Electronics / Medical Electronics / Avionics / Industrial Electronics / Defense & Strategic Electronics / Automotive Electronics / Information & Broadcasting Equipment etc., covered by Karnataka ESDM Policy 2017-22
b) Semiconductor manufacturing & design including manufacturing of Semiconductors, ICs, PCBs, bare boards, chip components, chemicals for board manufacture, covered by Karnataka ESDM Policy 2017-22
c) Electronic Manufacturing Services including design / IP / software services for electronics products, covered by Karnataka ESDM Policy 2017-22
d) The products / activities covered by National Policy of Electronics 2019 of Government of India and Schemes of Government of India such as Scheme for Promotion of Manufacturing of Electronic Components and Semiconductors (SPECS) and Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) for Large Scale Electronics Manufacturing.
e) Solar Cells Manufacturing - Standalone and with Modules
f) LED - Fab, Intermediaries and manufacturing & assembly of LED products
g) Other ESDM and its related Target Segments that may get approved by Executive Committee on case to case basis on receipt of Applications under this category during active policy duration.

2.2. Location: The company or entity should be registered in Karnataka under the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishment Act, 1961.

2.3. Employment: Employment Criteria (as per Karnataka Industrial Policy 2020-25) for enterprises availing incentives and concessions under this Scheme are as follows:
- > INR 15 Crore: 15 jobs per INR 15 Crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery and then 7 additional jobs for every additional INR 10 Crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery
- INR 50 to INR 250 Crore: 50 jobs per INR 50 Crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery and then 35 additional jobs for every additional INR 50 Crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery
- INR 250 to INR 500 Crore: 200 jobs per INR 250 Crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery and then 35 additional jobs for every additional INR 50 Crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery
- Above INR 500 Crore: 400 jobs per INR 500 Crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery and then 35 additional jobs for every additional INR 50 Crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery.

2.4. Minimum Investment: Eligible Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery: New Project/Unit: INR 15 Crore; Existing Project/Unit (Expansion/Modernization/Diversification): INR 50 Crore.

Mandatory single-window approval: It is mandatory to have obtained SLSWCC / SHLCC approval for New and Diversification / Expansion / Modernization Units to apply for incentives under the Scheme.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Companies availing incentives under this Scheme cannot avail incentives under any of the other policies of Government of Karnataka for the same Project. Any irregularity / misrepresentation in this regard may disqualify the company from availing any incentives under this Scheme.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: The company or entity should be registered in Karnataka under the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishment Act, 1961. Land subsidy is available only in areas other than Bengaluru Urban and Bengaluru Rural districts.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Registration under Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishment Act, 1961; approval from SLSWCC (for investments > INR 15 Cr up to INR 500 Cr) or SHLCC (for investments > INR 500 Cr).

incentive_details.description: Government of Karnataka provides up to 25% subsidy on land value up to an extent of 50 acres for setting up ESDM units. Land Subsidy is applicable for land located only in areas other than Bengaluru Urban and Bengaluru Rural districts. The expenditure on land considered for subsidy is capped at 25% of the Value of Fixed Assets (VFA) and subject to a monetary ceiling of INR 12.5 Crore.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: 25% subsidy on land value up to 50 acres, capped at ₹12.5 crore, for units outside Bengaluru Urban and Rural districts.
incentive_details.application_process: Apply online via itbtst.karnataka.gov.in using the Common Application Form (Annexure 3) along with Annexures 4 & 4A and requisite property title and CA certificates.

quantified_benefits.conditions: Expenditure on Land for subsidy shall be capped at 25% of Value of Fixed Assets; maximum land extent up to 50 acres.
quantified_benefits.description: Subsidy on eligible land value capped at 25% of Value of Fixed Assets, up to 50 acres, outside Bengaluru Urban and Rural districts.
quantified_benefits.source_text: Government of Karnataka shall provide up to 25% subsidy on land value up to an extent of 50 acres. The Land Subsidy shall be applicable for land only in areas other than Bengaluru Urban and Bengaluru Rural districts.
quantified_benefits.applicable_to: ESDM units located outside Bengaluru Urban and Bengaluru Rural districts

incentive_details.application_deadline: Within 12 months from the Date of Commencement of Commercial Production
incentive_details.incentive_specific_eligibility: Only applicable to land in districts other than Bengaluru Urban and Bengaluru Rural. Maximum land considered is 50 acres.

2. Eligibility Criteria
2.1. Target Segments
The company applying for Special Incentive Scheme for ESDM Sector ('Scheme') should be involved in manufacturing of one or more of the following Target Segments or related activities ('Eligible Products/Activities'):
a) Manufacturing and / or design of electronics products such as Telecom Systems / Mobiles / IT Systems and Hardware / Consumer Electronics / Medical Electronics / Avionics / Industrial Electronics / Defense & Strategic Electronics / Automotive Electronics / Information & Broadcasting Equipment etc., covered by Karnataka ESDM Policy 2017-22
b) Semiconductor manufacturing & design including manufacturing of Semiconductors, ICs, PCBs, bare boards, chip components, chemicals for board manufacture, covered by Karnataka ESDM Policy 2017-22
c) Electronic Manufacturing Services including design / IP / software services for electronics products, covered by Karnataka ESDM Policy 2017-22
d) The products / activities covered by National Policy of Electronics 2019 of Government of India and Schemes of Government of India such as Scheme for Promotion of Manufacturing of Electronic Components and Semiconductors (SPECS) and Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) for Large Scale Electronics Manufacturing.
e) Solar Cells Manufacturing - Standalone and with Modules
f) LED - Fab, Intermediaries and manufacturing & assembly of LED products
g) Other ESDM and its related Target Segments that may get approved by Executive Committee on case to case basis on receipt of Applications under this category during active policy duration.

2.2. Location: The company or entity should be registered in Karnataka under the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishment Act, 1961.

2.3. Employment: Employment Criteria (as per Karnataka Industrial Policy 2020-25) for enterprises availing incentives and concessions under this Scheme are as follows:
- > INR 15 Crore: 15 jobs per INR 15 Crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery and then 7 additional jobs for every additional INR 10 Crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery
- INR 50 to INR 250 Crore: 50 jobs per INR 50 Crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery and then 35 additional jobs for every additional INR 50 Crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery
- INR 250 to INR 500 Crore: 200 jobs per INR 250 Crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery and then 35 additional jobs for every additional INR 50 Crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery
- Above INR 500 Crore: 400 jobs per INR 500 Crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery and then 35 additional jobs for every additional INR 50 Crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery.

2.4. Minimum Investment: Eligible Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery: New Project/Unit: INR 15 Crore; Existing Project/Unit (Expansion/Modernization/Diversification): INR 50 Crore.

Mandatory single-window approval: It is mandatory to have obtained SLSWCC / SHLCC approval for New and Diversification / Expansion / Modernization Units to apply for incentives under the Scheme.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Companies availing incentives under this Scheme cannot avail incentives under any of the other policies of Government of Karnataka for the same Project. Any irregularity / misrepresentation in this regard may disqualify the company from availing any incentives under this Scheme.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: The company or entity should be registered in Karnataka under the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishment Act, 1961. Land subsidy is available only in areas other than Bengaluru Urban and Bengaluru Rural districts.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Registration under Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishment Act, 1961; approval from SLSWCC (for investments > INR 15 Cr up to INR 500 Cr) or SHLCC (for investments > INR 500 Cr).

incentive_details.description: Reimbursement of power tariff at INR 1.00 per unit of power consumed for a period of 5 years from the month of commencement of commercial production. For existing companies undertaking expansion, modernization, or diversification, subsidy is granted on incremental power consumed over the base year (highest consumption of the previous 2 financial years), measured via an exclusive meter.
incentive_details.benefit_headline: Power tariff reimbursement of ₹1.00 per unit for 5 years from commercial production.
incentive_details.application_process: Apply every 6 months using Annexures 3, 7, and 7A along with ESCOM sanction letters, electricity bills, and receipts.

quantified_benefits.conditions: Claims filed every 6 months. For existing units, calculated on incremental consumption over the higher consumption year of the preceding two financial years.
quantified_benefits.description: Reimbursement of electricity tariff per unit consumed (or incremental units consumed for existing expanding units).

quantified_benefits.applicable_to: All eligible ESDM units in Karnataka

incentive_details.application_deadline: Filing once every 6 months (October to March for April–September consumption and vice versa)

2. Eligibility Criteria
2.1. Target Segments
The company applying for Special Incentive Scheme for ESDM Sector ('Scheme') should be involved in manufacturing of one or more of the following Target Segments or related activities ('Eligible Products/Activities'):
a) Manufacturing and / or design of electronics products such as Telecom Systems / Mobiles / IT Systems and Hardware / Consumer Electronics / Medical Electronics / Avionics / Industrial Electronics / Defense & Strategic Electronics / Automotive Electronics / Information & Broadcasting Equipment etc., covered by Karnataka ESDM Policy 2017-22
b) Semiconductor manufacturing & design including manufacturing of Semiconductors, ICs, PCBs, bare boards, chip components, chemicals for board manufacture, covered by Karnataka ESDM Policy 2017-22
c) Electronic Manufacturing Services including design / IP / software services for electronics products, covered by Karnataka ESDM Policy 2017-22
d) The products / activities covered by National Policy of Electronics 2019 of Government of India and Schemes of Government of India such as Scheme for Promotion of Manufacturing of Electronic Components and Semiconductors (SPECS) and Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) for Large Scale Electronics Manufacturing.
e) Solar Cells Manufacturing - Standalone and with Modules
f) LED - Fab, Intermediaries and manufacturing & assembly of LED products
g) Other ESDM and its related Target Segments that may get approved by Executive Committee on case to case basis on receipt of Applications under this category during active policy duration.

2.2. Location: The company or entity should be registered in Karnataka under the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishment Act, 1961.

2.3. Employment: Employment Criteria (as per Karnataka Industrial Policy 2020-25) for enterprises availing incentives and concessions under this Scheme are as follows:
- > INR 15 Crore: 15 jobs per INR 15 Crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery and then 7 additional jobs for every additional INR 10 Crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery
- INR 50 to INR 250 Crore: 50 jobs per INR 50 Crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery and then 35 additional jobs for every additional INR 50 Crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery
- INR 250 to INR 500 Crore: 200 jobs per INR 250 Crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery and then 35 additional jobs for every additional INR 50 Crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery
- Above INR 500 Crore: 400 jobs per INR 500 Crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery and then 35 additional jobs for every additional INR 50 Crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery.

2.4. Minimum Investment: Eligible Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery: New Project/Unit: INR 15 Crore; Existing Project/Unit (Expansion/Modernization/Diversification): INR 50 Crore.

Mandatory single-window approval: It is mandatory to have obtained SLSWCC / SHLCC approval for New and Diversification / Expansion / Modernization Units to apply for incentives under the Scheme.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Companies availing incentives under this Scheme cannot avail incentives under any of the other policies of Government of Karnataka for the same Project. - INR 50 to INR 250 Crore: 50 jobs per INR 50 Crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery and then 35 additional jobs for every additional INR 50 Crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery
- INR 250 to INR 500 Crore: 200 jobs per INR 250 Crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery and then 35 additional jobs for every additional INR 50 Crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery
- Above INR 500 Crore: 400 jobs per INR 500 Crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery and then 35 additional jobs for every additional INR 50 Crore worth Capital Expenditure on Plant & Machinery.

incentive_name: Credit Guarantee Scheme for Stand Up India (CGSSI)

policy_goals: Facilitate bank loans between ₹10 lakh and ₹1 Crore to at least one Scheduled Caste (SC) or Scheduled Tribe (ST) borrower and at least one woman borrower per bank branch for setting up greenfield enterprises
Support greenfield enterprises in manufacturing, services, or trading sectors across India
Promote entrepreneurship among underserved segments (SC, ST, and women) to transform job seekers into job creators
Establish an integrated ecosystem providing credit access, collateral-free credit guarantee, and comprehensive handholding support through the Standupmitra portal
policy_details.policy_summary: The Stand Up India Scheme was launched on April 5, 2016, under the Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance, Government of India, and managed through SIDBI's www.standupmitra.in portal. The scheme facilitates composite bank loans ranging between ₹10 lakh and ₹1 Crore to at least one SC or ST borrower and at least one woman borrower per bank branch across all Scheduled Commercial Banks for establishing greenfield enterprises in manufacturing, services, or trading. Non-individual enterprises must have at least 51% shareholding and controlling stake held by SC/ST or woman entrepreneurs. The composite loan covers up to 75% of the project cost (comprising term loan for plant and machinery and working capital) with repayable tenure up to 7 years including up to 18 months moratorium. It incorporates collateral-free funding through the Credit Guarantee Scheme for Stand Up India (CGSSI) operated by NCGTC, margin money requirements capped at 25% (with borrower minimum contribution of 10% in convergence with eligible central/state subsidies), and an extensive handholding support structure linking LDMs, SIDBI, NABARD, DICs, and dedicated handholding agencies.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Composite bank loans from ₹10 lakh up to ₹1 Crore with collateral-free credit guarantee and up to 7-year repayment tenure for SC, ST, and Women entrepreneurs.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance, Government of India
special_focus_areas: Greenfield enterprises in manufacturing, services, or trading

This enterprise may be in manufacturing, services or the trading sector. In case of non-individual enterprises at least 51% of the shareholding and controlling stake should be held by either an SC/ST or Woman entrepreneur. Applicant should not be defaulter in any Bank/F.I.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Applicant should not be a defaulter in any Bank or Financial Institution.

policy_goals: Provide financial assistance to startups for proof of concept, prototype development, product trials, market entry, and commercialization
Enable startups to graduate to a level where they can raise investments from angel investors, venture capitalists, or seek loans from commercial banks
Resolve capital inadequacy in the seed and Proof of Concept development stage

Encourage entrepreneurship, foster innovation in critical sectors, and generate employment across India
policy_details.policy_summary: The Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SISFS) provides financial assistance to early-stage startups for proof of concept, prototype development, product trials, market entry, and commercialization. Financial support is disbursed through eligible incubators across India. Startups can receive up to ₹20 lakhs in milestone-based grant funding for validation and prototyping, or up to ₹50 lakhs in investment through convertible debentures or debt-linked instruments (with an interest rate capped at prevailing repo rate, tenure up to 5 years, and up to 12 months moratorium) for scaling and market entry.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to ₹20 lakhs in grants for prototype development and up to ₹50 lakhs in low-interest debt or convertible debentures for commercialization and scaling.

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: 3.1 Eligibility Criteria for Startups: 1. A startup, recognized by DPIIT, incorporated not more than 2 years ago at the time of application. 2. Startup must have a business idea to develop a product or a service with market fit, viable commercialization, and scope of scaling. 3. Startup should be using technology in its core product or service, or business model, or distribution model, or methodology to solve the problem being targeted. 4. policy_details.policy_summary: The Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SISFS) is formulated by DPIIT to address early-stage capital inadequacy for Indian startups. Under the scheme, funding is routed through eligible incubators across India. Eligible startups recognized by DPIIT and incorporated not more than 2 years prior can receive up to ₹20 Lakhs as grant assistance for proof of concept, prototype development, and product trials, and up to ₹50 Lakhs via convertible debentures, debt, or debt-linked instruments for market entry, commercialization, or scaling. Selected incubators are eligible for milestone-based grant assistance of up to ₹5 Crore along with a 5% management fee component.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Up to ₹20 Lakhs grant for proof of concept and up to ₹50 Lakhs debt/convertible debenture investment for early-stage startups via partner incubators.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade, Ministry of Commerce and Industry

eligibility_criteria.raw_text:
The eligibility criteria for a startup to apply under the Startup India Seed Fund Scheme shall be as follows:
1. A startup, recognized by DPIIT, incorporated not more than 2 years ago at the time of application
2. Startup must have a business idea to develop a product or a service with market fit, viable commercialization, and scope of scaling
3. Startup should be using technology in its core product or service, or business model, or distribution model, or methodology to solve the problem being targeted
4. Preference would be given to startups creating innovative solutions in sectors such as social impact, waste management, water management, financial inclusion, education, agriculture, food processing, biotechnology, healthcare, energy, mobility, defence, space, railways, oil and gas, textiles, etc.
5. Startup should not have received more than Rs 10 lakh of monetary support under any other Central or State Government scheme. This does not include prize money from competitions and grand challenges, subsidized working space, founder monthly allowance, access to labs, or access to prototyping facility
6. Shareholding by Indian promoters in the startup should be at least 51% at the time of application to incubator for the scheme, as per Companies Act, 2013 and SEBI (ICDR) Regulations, 2018
7. Any startup will not receive seed support more than once each as per provisions of para 8.1 (i) and 8.1 (ii) respectively
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Startups that have received more than ₹10 lakh of monetary support under any other Central or State Government scheme (excluding prize money, subsidized working space, founder monthly allowance, lab access, or prototyping facility access). Seed fund strictly cannot be used for the creation of any facilities. Startups cannot receive seed support more than once under each funding component.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Must have an innovative business idea with market fit, viable commercialization, and scope of scaling. Must incorporate technology in its core product/service, business model, distribution model, or methodology. Indian promoter shareholding must be at least 51% at the time of application as per Companies Act 2013 and SEBI (ICDR) Regulations 2018.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: DPIIT-recognized startup incorporated not more than 2 years ago at the time of application.
special_category_benefits: Preference given to startups creating innovative solutions in social impact, waste management, water management, financial inclusion, education, agriculture, food processing, biotechnology, healthcare, energy, mobility, defence, space, railways, oil and gas, textiles, etc.

incentive_details.application_process: Apply via Startup India portal choosing up to three incubators in order of preference. Evaluated by ISMC on parameters including need, feasibility, impact, novelty, team, and fund utilization plan.

quantified_benefits.description: Investment through convertible debentures, debt, or debt-linked instruments for commercialization and scaling
quantified_benefits.source_text: Up to Rs. 50 Lakhs of investment for market entry, commercialization, or scaling up through convertible debentures or debt or debt-linked instruments

policy_name: Technology Development Fund (TDF) Scheme
incentive_name: Grant-in-Aid for Defence Technology and Prototype Development

policy_goals: Promote self-reliance in Defence Technology as a part of the 'Make in India' initiative
Stimulate development of defence technologies that will form kernel of components and assemblies for defence equipment, systems, sub-systems, and platforms
Meet the requirements of Tri-Services (Army, Air Force and Navy), Defence Production and DRDO
Foster and encourage participation of public and private industries, especially MSMEs, for defence manufacturing supported through TDF funding up to 90% with a development period of two years
Increase collaborative approaches and establish linkages between industry and academia
policy_details.policy_summary: The Technology Development Fund (TDF) Scheme is an initiative under the Ministry of Defence executed by the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) to promote self-reliance in defence technology under the 'Make in India' initiative. The scheme supports public and private industries, especially MSMEs, providing grant-in-aid of up to 90% of total project costs for developing defence and dual-use technologies and prototypes over a two-year development period. Eligible costs cover manpower, equipment, consumables, subcontracting, travel, contingency, and academia participation (capped at 40%). Funding is provided either as an advance against a matching bank guarantee or as reimbursement linked to milestone completion.
policy_details.benefit_headline: Grant-in-aid funding up to 90% of project cost for defence technology and prototype development over a two-year period.
policy_details.issuing_authority: Defence Research and Development Organisation, Ministry of Defence

eligibility_criteria.raw_text: The Development Agency is an Indian company/ Partnership firm/ Limited Liability partnership/ Sole proprietorship, registered as per applicable Indian laws with a minimum of 51 percent Indian ownership and shall continue to be owned as such over the total duration of the project. The Development Agency having foreign investment, if any, is 'owned' and 'controlled' by resident Indian citizens and/or Indian companies which are ultimately owned and controlled by resident Indian citizens as per the FDI policy of the GoI. MOA / Applicable regulatory compliances DA should allow them to accept Grants, and Research and Development (Related to this project) should form part of its main or ancillary business in MOA/ Applicable regulatory compliances. The scheme encourages participation of public/private industries, especially MSMEs.
eligibility_criteria.exclusions: Any entity blacklisted by any Indian Government Agency/Organization, involved in unlawful acts, facing statutory winding up/insolvency orders, or where dues/penal orders have been passed by tax authorities/courts leading to legal action. Non-allowable costs include bad debts, interest on loans, land, permanent buildings, contributions/donations, fines/penalties, advocacy/business development, losses on other contracts, entertainment, alcoholic beverages, business reorganization/merger costs, and workshops/seminars.
eligibility_criteria.other_requirements: Development Agency must maintain a separate dedicated bank account in a nationalized scheduled bank. In case of academic or research institution collaboration, the work involvement of academia/research institutions cannot exceed 40% of the total efforts/project cost. All plant, machinery, fixtures, and equipment acquired under the grant must be insured for a minimum period of 2 years with insurance monies payable to the Government of India.
eligibility_criteria.location_requirements: Registered and operating in India under applicable Indian laws.
eligibility_criteria.registration_requirements: Registered as an Indian company, Partnership firm, Limited Liability Partnership (LLP), or Sole Proprietorship under applicable Indian laws.

incentive_details.description: Financial support covering up to 90% of the total project cost for the development of defence and dual-use technologies, components, and prototypes. Disbursed as milestone-linked reimbursement or as milestone advances against a 100% collateral Bank Guarantee. Eligible costs include manpower, equipment, consumables, sub-contracts, domestic travel, overhead (capped at 10%), contingency, and academia costs (capped at 40%).
incentive_details.benefit_headline: Up to 90% grant funding for R&D and prototype development in defence technologies.
incentive_details.application_process: Expressions of Interest (EoI) must be submitted online through the TDF Scheme web-portal against projected requirements. Selection follows a three-level evaluation comprising Project Monitoring and Mentoring Group (PMMG), Technical Committee, and Empowered Committee.

quantified_benefits.conditions: Development period of two years; remaining share to be borne by the Development Agency.
quantified_benefits.description: Funding support by DRDO covering up to 90% of the project development cost
quantified_benefits.source_text: Foster and encourage participation of public/private industries, especially MSMEs, for defence manufacturing, supported through TDF funding upto 90% with development period of two years.
